meta.name: Machine learning
meta.note: LLM-decomposed concepts; metrics computed on the graph before transitive reduction.

nodes.label: element
nodes.definition: An element of a set $A$ is an object $x$ satisfying $x \in A$. Membership is the primitive relation of set theory, and in combinatorics it identifies the atomic objects from which finite sets, sequences, and discrete structures are formed.

nodes.label: logical conjunction
nodes.definition: Logical conjunction is the binary connective $p \wedge q$ that is true exactly when both propositions $p$ and $q$ are true. In Boolean algebra it corresponds to the meet operation and, under the identification $\{0,1\}$, to multiplication.

nodes.label: set
nodes.definition: A set is an unordered collection of distinct objects, called its elements. Two sets are equal exactly when they contain the same elements, regardless of order or repetition.

nodes.label: 3d reconstruction
nodes.definition: Recovering the 3D geometry of a scene or object from 2D images. Methods: Structure from Motion (sparse), Multi-View Stereo (dense), NeRF (neural implicit), 3D Gaussian Splatting (neural explicit).

nodes.label: absolute value
nodes.definition: The absolute value of a real number $x$ is $|x| = \begin{cases} x & \text{if } x \geq 0 \\ -x & \text{if } x < 0 \end{cases}$, representing the distance of $x$ from zero on the real number line.

nodes.label: acceptance probability
nodes.definition: In Metropolis-Hastings MCMC, the probability of accepting a proposed move from state $\boldsymbol{\theta}$ to $\boldsymbol{\theta}'$: $\alpha(\boldsymbol{\theta}, \boldsymbol{\theta}') = \min\left(1, \frac{\pi(\boldsymbol{\theta}') q(\boldsymbol{\theta} | \boldsymbol{\theta}')}{\pi(\boldsymbol{\theta}) q(\boldsymbol{\theta}' | \boldsymbol{\theta})}\right)$, ensuring detailed balance and convergence to the target dist…

nodes.label: action
nodes.definition: In reinforcement learning, a decision made by the agent at each time step, selected from the action space $\mathcal{A}$. Can be discrete (finite set of choices) or continuous ($\mathcal{A} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$). The policy maps states to actions.

nodes.label: activation function
nodes.definition: A nonlinear function applied element-wise to the output of a linear transformation in a neural network layer: $h = \sigma(\mathbf{W}\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{b})$, introducing nonlinearity that enables the network to learn complex functions. Common choices: ReLU, sigmoid, tanh, GELU, Swish.

nodes.label: adafactor
nodes.definition: A memory-efficient adaptive optimizer for large models that replaces Adam's second-moment matrix with a low-rank factorization: for weight matrix $\mathbf{W} \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$, maintain row and column factors $\mathbf{r}_t \in \mathbb{R}^m$ and $\mathbf{c}_t \in \mathbb{R}^n$ such that $\hat{v}_{ij} = r_i c_j / \bar{r}$, reducing memory from $O(mn)$ to $O(m+n)$.

nodes.label: advantage function
nodes.definition: The difference between the action-value and state-value functions: $A^\pi(s, a) = Q^\pi(s, a) - V^\pi(s)$, measuring how much better action $a$ is compared to the average action under policy $\pi$ in state $s$. Used in policy gradient methods to reduce variance.

nodes.label: aggregation function
nodes.definition: A function that combines multiple values into a single summary value. In GNNs: sum, mean, max, or attention-weighted aggregation of neighbor messages. In ensembles: voting, averaging.

nodes.label: aic
nodes.definition: Akaike Information Criterion: a model selection criterion balancing fit and complexity: $\text{AIC} = 2k - 2\ln(\hat{L})$ where $k$ is the number of parameters and $\hat{L}$ is the maximum likelihood. Lower AIC indicates a better model.

nodes.label: algebra
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: The branch of mathematics studying structures defined by operations on sets: groups, rings, fields, vector spaces, modules. In computation: symbolic manipulation of expressions.

nodes.label: alignment
nodes.definition: In sequence models: the correspondence between input and output positions (hard: each output aligns to one input, soft: weighted combination via attention). In LLMs: the process of making model behavior match human values and preferences (RLHF, DPO).

nodes.label: anti-monotone property
nodes.definition: A property of a measure (like support in itemset mining) where if a set does not satisfy a condition, then no superset can satisfy it: if $\text{support}(X) < \text{min\_sup}$, then $\text{support}(X \cup Y) < \text{min\_sup}$ for all $Y$. Enables efficient pruning in Apriori.

nodes.label: approximation
nodes.definition: A value or function that is close to but not exactly equal to a target quantity, with error bounds characterizing the closeness. Approximation theory studies how well functions can be approximated by simpler classes (polynomials, neural networks).

nodes.label: archive
nodes.definition: In quality-diversity optimization, a structured collection of elite solutions indexed by behavior descriptors, storing the highest-fitness solution for each behavioral niche.

nodes.label: array
nodes.definition: An ordered collection of elements arranged in a regular structure (1D: vector, 2D: matrix, higher: tensor). In programming, a contiguous block of memory storing elements of the same type, accessed by indices.

nodes.label: asymmetric loss
nodes.definition: A loss function that penalizes overestimates and underestimates differently. Quantile loss: $\rho_\tau(u) = u(\tau - \mathbf{1}(u<0))$. Expectile loss: $L_\tau(u) = |\tau - \mathbf{1}(u<0)| u^2$.

nodes.label: asynchronous computing
nodes.definition: A parallel computing model where multiple workers operate independently without synchronization barriers, each computing and communicating updates at its own pace.

nodes.label: attention mask
nodes.definition: A binary or float matrix applied to attention scores before softmax to prevent attending to certain positions: causal mask ($M_{ij} = -\infty$ for $j > i$), padding mask ($M_{ij} = -\infty$ for pad tokens), or custom patterns.

nodes.label: attribute dependence
nodes.definition: Statistical dependency between features/attributes in a dataset, violating the conditional independence assumption of Naive Bayes.

nodes.label: audio waveform
nodes.definition: The time-domain representation of sound as a sequence of amplitude values sampled at a fixed rate (e.g., 16kHz, 24kHz, 44.1kHz). Each sample is typically a 16-bit integer or 32-bit float. WaveNet, WaveRNN, and neural vocoders generate raw waveforms.

nodes.label: backpropagation through time
nodes.definition: The application of backpropagation to recurrent neural networks by unrolling the network across time steps and computing gradients through the entire unrolled graph, accumulating gradients from each time step. Truncated BPTT limits the number of unrolled steps for computational efficiency.

nodes.label: backshift operator
nodes.definition: An operator $B$ defined on time series as $B X_t = X_{t-1}$ (shifts the series back by one period). Used to express ARIMA models compactly: $(1 - \phi_1 B)(1 - B)^d X_t = (1 + \theta_1 B)\epsilon_t$.

nodes.label: basis
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: A set of vectors $\{\mathbf{v}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{v}_n\}$ in a vector space $V$ that is linearly independent and spans $V$: every vector in $V$ can be uniquely written as $\mathbf{v} = \sum c_i \mathbf{v}_i$. The number of basis vectors is the dimension of $V$.

nodes.label: basis function
nodes.definition: A member of a set of functions $\{\phi_k\}$ used to represent other functions as linear combinations: $f(x) = \sum_k w_k \phi_k(x)$. Examples: polynomials, B-splines, Fourier basis, wavelets, radial basis functions.

nodes.label: bayes theorem
nodes.definition: A fundamental theorem relating conditional probabilities: $P(A \mid B) = \frac{P(B \mid A) P(A)}{P(B)}$, enabling the inversion of conditional probabilities. The foundation of Bayesian statistics and inference.

nodes.label: bayesian information criterion
nodes.definition: The Bayesian information criterion is the model-selection score $\mathrm{BIC}=k\log n-2\log \hat L$, where $k$ is the number of free parameters, $n$ is sample size, and $\hat L$ is the maximized likelihood. It is an asymptotic approximation to a log marginal-likelihood comparison under regularity assumptions.

nodes.label: behavior descriptor
nodes.definition: In quality-diversity optimization, a function $\mathbf{b}: \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}^d$ that maps solutions to a low-dimensional behavior space characterizing how a solution behaves (not how well), defining the niches that QD algorithms fill.

nodes.label: behavior policy
nodes.definition: In off-policy RL, the policy $\mu(a \mid s)$ that was used to collect the data (behavior), as opposed to the target policy $\pi(a \mid s)$ being evaluated or improved. The importance ratio $\pi(a|s)/\mu(a|s)$ corrects for the mismatch.

nodes.label: bellman equation
nodes.definition: The Bellman equation is the recursive relation satisfied by value functions in a Markov decision process. For a policy $\pi$, it states $V^\pi(s)=\sum_a \pi(a\mid s)\left[r(s,a)+\gamma \sum_{s'} P(s'\mid s,a)V^\pi(s')\right]$, with analogous optimality equations for $V^*$ and $Q^*$.

nodes.label: bernoulli distribution
nodes.definition: A discrete distribution for a single binary trial with probability of success $p$: $P(X = 1) = p$, $P(X = 0) = 1 - p$, with mean $p$ and variance $p(1-p)$.

nodes.label: beta distribution
nodes.definition: A continuous distribution on $[0, 1]$ with PDF $f(x; \alpha, \beta) = \frac{x^{\alpha-1}(1-x)^{\beta-1}}{B(\alpha, \beta)}$ where $B$ is the beta function. Conjugate prior for Bernoulli/binomial likelihoods. Mean: $\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)$.

nodes.label: beta-vae
nodes.definition: A VAE variant that uses a hyperparameter $\beta > 1$ to upweight the KL divergence term in the ELBO: $\mathcal{L} = E_q[\log p(\mathbf{x} \mid \mathbf{z})] - \beta \cdot \text{KL}(q(\mathbf{z} \mid \mathbf{x}) \| p(\mathbf{z}))$, encouraging the model to learn a more disentangled latent representation where individual latent dimensions correspond to independent generative factors.

nodes.label: bidirectional context
nodes.definition: The ability of a model to access both preceding and following tokens when producing a representation for a given position, achieved by bidirectional attention (BERT) as opposed to causal (left-to-right) attention (GPT).

nodes.label: bijection
nodes.definition: A function $f: X \to Y$ that is both injective (one-to-one: $f(a) = f(b) \Rightarrow a = b$) and surjective (onto: $\forall y \in Y, \exists x: f(x) = y$). Bijections have inverses. The cardinality of a set is defined via bijections.

nodes.label: bilinear form
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: A function $B: V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$ that is linear in each argument separately: $B(\alpha x_1 + x_2, y) = \alpha B(x_1, y) + B(x_2, y)$ and similarly for the second argument. Represented by a matrix: $B(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) = \mathbf{x}^\top \mathbf{A} \mathbf{y}$.

nodes.label: bilinear interpolation
nodes.definition: A 2D interpolation method that linearly interpolates first along one axis and then along the other: $f(x,y) = (1-t)(1-s)f_{00} + t(1-s)f_{10} + (1-t)sf_{01} + tsf_{11}$ for unit square with corners $f_{ij}$.

nodes.label: binary operation
nodes.definition: A function $\star: S \times S \to S$ that takes two elements from a set $S$ and produces a third element of $S$. Examples: addition, multiplication, matrix multiplication, composition of functions. Properties: associativity, commutativity, identity, inverse.

nodes.label: binary partition
nodes.definition: A partition of a set into exactly two disjoint subsets. Used in: binary decision trees (split at each node), bisecting k-means, recursive partitioning.

nodes.label: binary variable
nodes.definition: A variable taking exactly two values, typically 0 and 1 (or $-1$ and $+1$). In statistics: Bernoulli random variable. In ML: binary features, binary labels, binary masks.

nodes.label: blank token
nodes.definition: A special token in CTC and RNN-T that represents 'no output at this time step', enabling alignment-free sequence-to-sequence mapping by absorbing timing variations.

nodes.label: bootstrap sampling
nodes.definition: Drawing $n$ samples with replacement from a dataset of size $n$, creating a new dataset of the same size where some points appear multiple times and ~36.8% are missing. Foundation for bagging and bootstrap confidence intervals.

nodes.label: bootstrapping
nodes.definition: In RL: using an estimated value to update the current value estimate, rather than waiting for the actual return: $V(s) \leftarrow V(s) + \alpha[r + \gamma V(s') - V(s)]$ uses $V(s')$ as an estimate. In statistics: resampling with replacement to estimate sampling distributions.

nodes.label: boundary condition
nodes.definition: Constraints specifying the value of a PDE solution on the boundary of the domain: Dirichlet ($u = g$ on boundary), Neumann ($\partial u/\partial n = g$), or Robin (mixed). Required for a well-posed PDE problem.

nodes.label: breakdown point
nodes.definition: The smallest fraction of outliers in a dataset that can cause an estimator to give arbitrarily bad results. OLS has breakdown 0 (one outlier can destroy it). Median has breakdown 0.5 (maximum possible). Theil-Sen has ~29.3%.

nodes.label: camera model
nodes.definition: A mathematical model relating 3D world coordinates to 2D image coordinates. Pinhole model: $\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{K}[\mathbf{R}|\mathbf{t}]\mathbf{X}$ where $\mathbf{K}$ is the intrinsic matrix (focal length, principal point) and $[\mathbf{R}|\mathbf{t}]$ is the extrinsic (rotation, translation).

nodes.label: capsule network
nodes.definition: A neural network that replaces scalar-output neurons with vector-output capsules representing entity properties, using dynamic routing by agreement between layers: lower-level capsules send predictions to higher-level capsules, and the routing algorithm iteratively determines which predictions are consistent, enabling the network to model part-whole hierarchical relationships.

nodes.label: cascade r-cnn
nodes.definition: A multi-stage object detection framework that chains multiple detection heads with progressively increasing IoU thresholds ($u_1 < u_2 < u_3$, e.g., 0.5, 0.6, 0.7), where each stage refines the proposals from the previous stage, addressing the mismatch between training and inference IoU thresholds in standard detectors.

nodes.label: categorical variable
nodes.definition: A variable taking values from a finite, unordered set of categories (e.g., color: {red, blue, green}). Encoded for ML as: one-hot vectors, embeddings, label encoding, target encoding.

nodes.label: causal convolution
nodes.definition: A 1D convolution where the output at time $t$ depends only on inputs at times $\leq t$ (no future information), implemented by left-padding the input. Used in: WaveNet, TCN for autoregressive modeling.

nodes.label: censoring
nodes.definition: Censoring occurs when the quantity of interest is only partially observed rather than measured exactly. In survival analysis, one often knows only that an event time $T$ lies beyond, before, or between observation bounds.

nodes.label: channel
nodes.definition: In convolutional neural networks, a feature map dimension representing different learned features at each spatial location. An RGB image has 3 input channels; convolutional layers produce multiple output channels, each detecting a different pattern. Also called feature maps or filters.

nodes.label: channel independence
nodes.definition: A design choice in time series models (PatchTST) where each variable (channel) is processed independently by the same model, acting as a form of regularization and enabling the model to handle varying numbers of variables.

nodes.label: character n-gram
nodes.definition: A contiguous subsequence of $n$ characters from a word, used as subword features. For 'hello' with $n=3$: '<he', 'hel', 'ell', 'llo', 'lo>'. Used in FastText for composing word embeddings from subword parts.

nodes.label: chordal graph
nodes.definition: A graph where every cycle of length 4 or more has a chord (an edge connecting two non-adjacent vertices in the cycle). Required for the junction tree algorithm: any graph can be made chordal by triangulation (adding edges).

nodes.label: class
nodes.definition: In classification, one of the discrete categories that a data point can belong to. In object-oriented programming, a template for creating objects. In ML: $y \in \{1, \ldots, K\}$ for $K$-class classification.

nodes.label: closed-form solution
nodes.definition: An explicit mathematical expression for the solution of a problem that can be computed directly from the inputs using a finite number of standard operations (arithmetic, roots, logarithms), without iteration or approximation. OLS has a closed-form; Lasso does not.

nodes.label: cluster ordering
nodes.definition: In OPTICS, the sequence of data points produced by the algorithm, where each point is annotated with its reachability distance. Valleys in the reachability plot correspond to clusters.

nodes.label: co-occurrence matrix
nodes.definition: A matrix $\mathbf{C}$ where $C_{ij}$ counts the number of times items $i$ and $j$ appear together within a context window. In NLP: word co-occurrence matrix used for GloVe. In recommendation: item co-occurrence for item-based CF.

nodes.label: codebook
nodes.definition: A finite dictionary of prototype vectors $\mathcal{C} = \{\mathbf{e}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{e}_K\}$ used in vector quantization: each input is mapped to the nearest codebook entry. Learnable in VQ-VAE and neural codecs.

nodes.label: codomain
nodes.definition: The set $Y$ in a function $f: X \to Y$ specifying the type of possible outputs. Distinguished from the range (image), which is the set of actual outputs $\{f(x) : x \in X\} \subseteq Y$.

nodes.label: collaborative filtering
nodes.definition: Collaborative filtering predicts user preferences from patterns of user-item interactions, exploiting the idea that similar users prefer similar items and similar items attract similar users. It is a core approach to recommendation from implicit or explicit feedback alone.

nodes.label: collocation method
nodes.definition: A method for solving ODEs/PDEs by requiring the solution to satisfy the equation at a discrete set of collocation points. In PINN: the PDE residual is evaluated at random collocation points.

nodes.label: comparison
nodes.definition: The act of evaluating the relative magnitude of two values, determining whether one is less than, equal to, or greater than another using the ordering relation on $\mathbb{R}$.

nodes.label: completeness
nodes.definition: A property of a metric space where every Cauchy sequence converges to a limit within the space. The real numbers $\mathbb{R}$ are complete (this distinguishes them from $\mathbb{Q}$). Completeness ensures that limits of convergent sequences remain in the space.

nodes.label: composition
nodes.definition: The operation of applying one function after another: $(f \circ g)(x) = f(g(x))$. In neural networks, deep networks are compositions of many layers. The chain rule computes derivatives of compositions.

nodes.label: compositional data
nodes.definition: Data where components represent proportions of a whole, summing to a constant (usually 1): $\mathbf{x} \in \Delta^{K-1}$. Requires special treatment (log-ratio transformations) because standard statistics on the simplex can be misleading.

nodes.label: computation
nodes.definition: The process of performing mathematical operations or executing algorithms to transform inputs into outputs. In ML: forward pass (compute predictions), backward pass (compute gradients).

nodes.label: computational complexity
nodes.definition: The study of the resources (time, space) required to solve computational problems as a function of input size. Common complexity classes: P (polynomial time), NP (non-deterministic polynomial), NP-hard, NP-complete. Big-O notation: $O(f(n))$ bounds growth rate.

nodes.label: concatenation
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: The operation of joining vectors, sequences, or tensors along a dimension: $[\mathbf{a}; \mathbf{b}] = (a_1, \ldots, a_m, b_1, \ldots, b_n) \in \mathbb{R}^{m+n}$. In neural networks: combining features from different sources.

nodes.label: concentration inequality
nodes.definition: A probabilistic bound on how much a random variable deviates from some value (typically its mean). Key inequalities: Hoeffding, Bernstein, Chernoff, sub-Gaussian. Used for: bandit bounds (UCB), PAC learning, generalization bounds.

nodes.label: concentration parameter
nodes.definition: In the Dirichlet process, $\alpha > 0$ controls the expected number of clusters ($\sim \alpha \log n$) and the discreteness of the random measure: small $\alpha$ = few clusters, large $\alpha$ = many clusters.

nodes.label: conditional computation
nodes.definition: A neural network design principle where only a subset of the network's parameters are activated for each input, enabling larger models with constant per-input computation. Examples: MoE (route to top-$k$ experts), Mixture of Depths, early exit.

nodes.label: confidence bound
nodes.definition: An upper or lower bound on an unknown quantity with high probability, used for exploration in bandits/BO: UCB selects $a = \arg\max [\hat{\mu}_a + c\sqrt{\log t / N_a}]$, where the second term is the confidence bound.

nodes.label: confidence interval
nodes.definition: An interval $[\hat{\theta}_L, \hat{\theta}_U]$ constructed from data that contains the true parameter $\theta$ with a specified probability (confidence level, e.g., 95%): $P(\hat{\theta}_L \leq \theta \leq \hat{\theta}_U) = 1 - \alpha$.

nodes.label: confounding
nodes.definition: A confounding variable $Z$ is associated with both the treatment $X$ and the outcome $Y$, creating a spurious association between $X$ and $Y$. Controlling for confounders is essential for unbiased causal effect estimation.

nodes.label: conjugate prior
nodes.definition: A prior distribution that, when combined with a specific likelihood via Bayes' theorem, produces a posterior of the same distributional family: the prior is conjugate to the likelihood. Examples: Beta-Bernoulli, Normal-Normal, Dirichlet-Multinomial, Gamma-Poisson.

nodes.label: conjunction
nodes.definition: The logical AND operation: $A \wedge B$ is true if and only if both $A$ and $B$ are true. In Tsetlin Machine: clauses are conjunctions of Boolean literals.

nodes.label: consistency
nodes.definition: In statistics: an estimator is consistent if it converges in probability to the true parameter as $n \to \infty$: $\hat{\theta}_n \xrightarrow{P} \theta$. MLE is consistent under regularity conditions. GEE: $\hat{\beta}$ is consistent even with misspecified working correlation.

nodes.label: constrained optimization
nodes.definition: An optimization problem where the feasible set is restricted by constraints: $\min f(\mathbf{x})$ subject to $g_i(\mathbf{x}) \leq 0$ (inequality) and $h_j(\mathbf{x}) = 0$ (equality). Solved via Lagrangian methods, penalty methods, or barrier methods.

nodes.label: context
nodes.definition: Information surrounding or relevant to a particular element. In NLP: surrounding words that inform meaning. In contextual bandits: feature vector observed before action selection. In Transformers: all tokens attended to.

nodes.label: continuity
nodes.definition: A function $f$ is continuous at $a$ if $\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = f(a)$. Intuitively: small changes in input produce small changes in output. A continuous function on a closed interval attains its maximum and minimum (extreme value theorem).

nodes.label: continuous action space
nodes.definition: An action space $\mathcal{A} \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ where actions are continuous-valued vectors (e.g., joint torques, steering angles). Requires policy gradient methods (DDPG, TD3, SAC) rather than discrete Q-learning.

nodes.label: continuous variable
nodes.definition: A variable that can take any real value within an interval (or all of $\mathbb{R}$), as opposed to a discrete/categorical variable. Continuous features in ML are processed differently from categorical ones.

nodes.label: controller
nodes.definition: In Neural Turing Machine/DNC: a neural network (LSTM or feedforward) that interfaces with external memory, producing read/write commands and processing retrieved information to generate outputs.

nodes.label: convergence rate
nodes.definition: The speed at which an iterative algorithm approaches its solution. Sublinear: $O(1/T)$ (GD for convex). Linear: $\|x_t - x^*\| \leq \rho^t$ with $\rho < 1$ (GD for strongly convex). Quadratic: $\|x_t - x^*\| \leq c \|x_{t-1} - x^*\|^2$ (Newton's method).

nodes.label: convex function
nodes.definition: A function $f: \mathbb{R}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying $f(\lambda \mathbf{x} + (1-\lambda) \mathbf{y}) \leq \lambda f(\mathbf{x}) + (1-\lambda) f(\mathbf{y})$ for all $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}$ and $\lambda \in [0,1]$, meaning the function lies below any chord. Every local minimum is a global minimum.

nodes.label: convex set
nodes.definition: A set $C \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ such that the line segment between any two points in $C$ lies entirely in $C$: $\forall \mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y} \in C, \forall \lambda \in [0,1]: \lambda \mathbf{x} + (1-\lambda) \mathbf{y} \in C$.

nodes.label: coordinate system
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: A system for specifying the position of points in a space using ordered tuples of numbers (coordinates). Cartesian coordinates $(x, y, z)$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$, polar $(r, \theta)$ in $\mathbb{R}^2$, spherical $(r, \theta, \phi)$ in $\mathbb{R}^3$.

nodes.label: coreset selection
nodes.definition: Selecting a small, representative subset of a dataset that approximates the full dataset for a given task. In PatchCore: greedy coreset of patch features maximizes coverage. In dataset pruning: select most informative examples.

nodes.label: cosine
nodes.definition: The cosine function $\cos(\theta)$ gives the $x$-coordinate of the point on the unit circle at angle $\theta$. Key identity: $\cos\theta = \frac{\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b}}{\|\mathbf{a}\| \|\mathbf{b}\|}$. Cosine similarity measures alignment between vectors.

nodes.label: counting
nodes.definition: The process of determining the number of elements in a finite set, producing a natural number. Foundation for combinatorics, frequency analysis, and discrete probability.

nodes.label: covariance
nodes.definition: A measure of the joint variability of two random variables: $\text{Cov}(X, Y) = E[(X - E[X])(Y - E[Y])] = E[XY] - E[X]E[Y]$. Positive covariance: variables tend to move together. Zero: uncorrelated. The covariance matrix $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}$ generalizes to multiple variables.

nodes.label: covariate
nodes.definition: A variable that is observed alongside the response variable and may affect it, but is not the primary variable of interest. In regression: predictor/feature. In causal inference: potential confounder to control for.

nodes.label: credit assignment
nodes.definition: In multi-agent RL: the problem of determining each agent's contribution to the team reward. In RL generally: determining which actions in a long trajectory were responsible for the eventual outcome (temporal credit assignment).

nodes.label: cross-attention
nodes.definition: Cross-attention is an attention mechanism in which queries come from one sequence or modality while keys and values come from another. It allows one representation to selectively retrieve information from a different source representation.

nodes.label: cross-validation
nodes.definition: Cross-validation is a resampling procedure for estimating out-of-sample performance by repeatedly fitting a model on part of the data and evaluating it on held-out subsets. The most common version is $k$-fold cross-validation.

nodes.label: crowding distance
nodes.definition: In NSGA-II: a measure of how isolated a solution is in the objective space, computed as the sum of distances to the nearest neighbors along each objective. Higher crowding distance → more diverse → preferred.

nodes.label: cumulative distribution function
nodes.definition: The function $F(x) = P(X \leq x)$ giving the probability that a random variable $X$ takes a value less than or equal to $x$. Non-decreasing, right-continuous, with $F(-\infty) = 0$ and $F(\infty) = 1$.

nodes.label: curse of dimensionality
nodes.definition: The phenomenon where the difficulty of many computational and statistical problems grows exponentially with the number of dimensions: in high dimensions, data becomes sparse, distances become nearly uniform, and the volume of the space grows so fast that the available data becomes insufficient for reliable estimation.

nodes.label: data
nodes.definition: Collections of observations, measurements, or facts used for analysis and model training. Types: structured (tabular), unstructured (text, images, audio), semi-structured (JSON, graphs). Data is the foundation of machine learning.

nodes.label: data filtering
nodes.definition: The process of removing low-quality, noisy, or irrelevant data points from a dataset before training. In LLM training: perplexity filtering, deduplication, toxicity filtering. In BLIP: CapFilt bootstrapping.

nodes.label: data structure
nodes.definition: An organized way of storing and accessing data for efficient operations. Examples: arrays, hash tables, trees (binary, B-tree, KD-tree), graphs, heaps, stacks, queues, tries.

nodes.label: decision stump
nodes.definition: A decision tree with only one internal node (the root) and two leaf nodes, making a single binary split on one feature, used as a weak learner in boosting algorithms like AdaBoost.

nodes.label: deconvolution
nodes.definition: Loosely: the inverse of convolution. In CNNs: transposed convolution (upsampling, not true deconvolution). In ZFNet: deconvolutional network for feature visualization (mapping activations back to pixel space). Mathematically: recovering $f$ from $f * g$ given $g$.

nodes.label: deep belief network
nodes.definition: A generative model consisting of a stack of Restricted Boltzmann Machines, trained greedily layer by layer (each RBM's hidden layer becomes the visible layer of the next), with the top two layers forming an RBM and all lower layers forming a directed sigmoid belief network, optionally fine-tuned with backpropagation for discriminative tasks.

nodes.label: dendrogram
nodes.definition: A tree diagram showing the hierarchical clustering structure: each leaf is a data point, and each internal node represents a merge event with height proportional to the merge distance/dissimilarity.

nodes.label: denoising
nodes.definition: The process of removing noise from a signal or image. In diffusion models: the reverse process of iteratively removing Gaussian noise. In denoising autoencoders: reconstructing clean input from corrupted input.

nodes.label: depth
nodes.definition: In neural networks: the number of layers (transformations) from input to output. Deeper networks can represent more complex functions but are harder to train (vanishing gradients). In trees: the number of edges from root to leaf.

nodes.label: depthwise separable convolution
nodes.definition: A factored convolution consisting of two steps: (1) depthwise convolution (one filter per input channel, no cross-channel mixing) and (2) pointwise convolution (1x1 convolution for cross-channel mixing). Reduces computation from $O(C_{\text{in}} C_{\text{out}} K^2)$ to $O(C_{\text{in}} K^2 + C_{\text{in}} C_{\text{out}})$.

nodes.label: derivative
nodes.definition: The instantaneous rate of change of a function $f$ at a point $x$: $f'(x) = \lim_{h \to 0} \frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}$, representing the slope of the tangent line. Extends to partial derivatives ($\partial f/\partial x_i$) for multivariate functions.

nodes.label: design space
nodes.definition: In NAS/RegNet: the set of all possible architectures (parameterized by depth, width, resolution, kernel sizes, etc.). RegNet simplified the design space to a few parameters defining a family of architectures.

nodes.label: deterministic mapping
nodes.definition: A function $f: X \to Y$ that maps each input to exactly one output (no randomness). DDIM with $\sigma = 0$ defines a deterministic mapping between noise and data. Contrast with stochastic mappings (sampling from distributions).

nodes.label: dimension
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: The number of independent coordinates needed to specify a point in a space. For $\mathbb{R}^n$, the dimension is $n$. For a vector space, the dimension is the cardinality of any basis. For data, the number of features.

nodes.label: discretization
nodes.definition: Converting continuous quantities to discrete values. In RL: discretize continuous action space into bins. In Trajectory Transformer: discretize states/actions/rewards into tokens. In SSMs: convert continuous-time to discrete-time (zero-order hold).

nodes.label: distance matrix
nodes.definition: A symmetric matrix $\mathbf{D}$ where $D_{ij} = d(\mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j)$ stores all pairwise distances between $n$ data points. Used in: MDS, DBSCAN, hierarchical clustering, spectral clustering.

nodes.label: distance metric
nodes.definition: A function $d: X \times X \to \mathbb{R}_{\geq 0}$ satisfying: (1) non-negativity, (2) identity of indiscernibles ($d(x,y)=0 \iff x=y$), (3) symmetry ($d(x,y)=d(y,x)$), (4) triangle inequality. Also called a metric. Makes $(X, d)$ a metric space.

nodes.label: distance threshold
nodes.definition: A boundary value $\epsilon$ used in density-based clustering: points within $\epsilon$ of a core point are in its neighborhood. In DBSCAN: the radius parameter. In DP-Means: new cluster created if distance $> \lambda$.

nodes.label: distributed computing
nodes.definition: Computing that distributes work across multiple networked machines. In ML: distributed training across GPUs/TPUs. Communication patterns: all-reduce (data parallel), all-to-all (MoE), pipeline (model parallel).

nodes.label: distributional dqn
nodes.definition: A class of deep reinforcement learning algorithms that learn the full distribution of returns $Z(s, a)$ (rather than just the expected value $Q(s, a) = E[Z(s, a)]$) and apply the distributional Bellman operator $T^\pi Z(s,a) \overset{D}{=} R(s,a) + \gamma Z(S', A')$ to update the return distribution, providing richer learning signals.

nodes.label: distributional shift
nodes.definition: Same as distribution shift: mismatch between training and deployment data distributions, causing model performance degradation.

nodes.label: diversity
nodes.definition: In evolutionary algorithms: maintaining variety in the population to prevent premature convergence. In ensembles: diversity among base learners improves ensemble performance. In QD: behavioral diversity is the explicit goal.

nodes.label: doc2vec
nodes.definition: An extension of Word2Vec that learns fixed-length vector representations for variable-length documents by adding a document vector that is shared across all contexts within a document, using either Distributed Memory (PV-DM: predict word from document vector + context) or Distributed Bag of Words (PV-DBOW: predict random words from document vector).

nodes.label: document representation
nodes.definition: A vector encoding of a text document for downstream tasks. Methods: bag-of-words, TF-IDF, Doc2Vec, mean of word embeddings, [CLS] token from BERT, sentence embeddings (Sentence-BERT).

nodes.label: domain
nodes.definition: The set of all valid inputs to a function $f: X \to Y$; the set $X$. For example, the domain of $\sqrt{x}$ is $[0, \infty)$, and the domain of $\log x$ is $(0, \infty)$.

nodes.label: edge features
nodes.definition: Attributes associated with edges in a graph: bond type (molecular graphs), relation type (knowledge graphs), distance (geometric graphs), timestamps (temporal graphs). Incorporated in message passing via edge-conditioned messages: $m_{ij} = \phi(\mathbf{h}_i, \mathbf{h}_j, \mathbf{e}_{ij})$.

nodes.label: elman network
nodes.definition: A simple recurrent neural network where the hidden layer's previous output is fed back as an additional input to the hidden layer at the next time step: $\mathbf{h}_t = \sigma(\mathbf{W}_{xh}\mathbf{x}_t + \mathbf{W}_{hh}\mathbf{h}_{t-1} + \mathbf{b}_h)$, representing the basic form of an RNN with context units.

nodes.label: encoding
nodes.definition: The process of converting data from one representation to another, typically from raw or complex format to a more structured or compact format. Examples: one-hot encoding (categories → binary vectors), positional encoding (positions → sinusoidal vectors), text encoding (text → token IDs).

nodes.label: energy conservation
nodes.category: Calculus of variations and optimal control
nodes.definition: The principle that the total energy of an isolated system remains constant over time. In Hamiltonian systems: $dH/dt = 0$. HNNs and LNNs enforce this by construction, ensuring physically consistent dynamics.

nodes.label: energy function
nodes.definition: A function $E: \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}$ assigning a scalar energy to each configuration, with lower energy corresponding to more probable or more stable states. Used in: Hopfield networks ($E = -\frac{1}{2}\sum w_{ij}s_is_j$), Boltzmann machines, EBMs.

nodes.label: equality constraint
nodes.definition: A constraint of the form $h(\mathbf{x}) = 0$ in an optimization problem, requiring the solution to lie on the surface defined by $h$. Handled via Lagrange multipliers: $\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{x}, \lambda) = f(\mathbf{x}) + \lambda h(\mathbf{x})$.

nodes.label: equivalence
nodes.definition: A relation that is reflexive, symmetric, and transitive, partitioning a set into equivalence classes. In graph theory: graph isomorphism is an equivalence relation.

nodes.label: estimator
nodes.definition: A function of the data used to estimate a population parameter: $\hat{\theta} = T(X_1, \ldots, X_n)$. Properties: bias ($E[\hat{\theta}] - \theta$), variance ($\text{Var}(\hat{\theta})$), consistency ($\hat{\theta} \to \theta$ as $n \to \infty$), efficiency (minimum variance among unbiased estimators).

nodes.label: evolutionary algorithm
nodes.definition: A class of population-based metaheuristic optimization algorithms inspired by biological evolution: maintain a population of candidate solutions, iteratively apply selection, variation (crossover, mutation), and replacement to evolve better solutions.

nodes.label: exemplar
nodes.definition: In clustering/classification: a representative data point that serves as the prototype for a cluster or class. In Affinity Propagation: each cluster is represented by an exemplar (actual data point). In prototype methods: representative examples per class.

nodes.label: expectation
nodes.definition: Synonym for expected value: $E[X] = \sum x P(x)$ (discrete) or $\int x f(x)dx$ (continuous). Also refers to the E-step in EM: computing expected sufficient statistics.

nodes.label: expected improvement
nodes.definition: An acquisition function for Bayesian optimization: $\text{EI}(\mathbf{x}) = E[\max(f(\mathbf{x}) - f^+, 0)]$ where $f^+$ is the best observed value. For a GP: $\text{EI} = (\mu - f^+ - \xi)\Phi(z) + \sigma\phi(z)$ where $z = (\mu - f^+ - \xi)/\sigma$.

nodes.label: expected sarsa
nodes.definition: A TD control algorithm that replaces the next-state Q-value with its expectation under the current policy: $Q(s_t, a_t) \leftarrow Q(s_t, a_t) + \alpha [r_t + \gamma \sum_a \pi(a \mid s_{t+1}) Q(s_{t+1}, a) - Q(s_t, a_t)]$, reducing variance compared to SARSA while maintaining the on-policy character.

nodes.label: exponential function
nodes.definition: The function $\exp(x) = e^x = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{x^n}{n!}$, the unique function satisfying $f'(x) = f(x)$ with $f(0) = 1$. Fundamental in probability (exponential family), optimization (softmax), and analysis.

nodes.label: external memory
nodes.definition: An explicit, addressable memory module outside the neural network's parameters, accessed via read/write operations: NTM's memory matrix $\mathbf{M} \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times W}$, DNC's dynamic memory, Memorizing Transformer's kNN memory.

nodes.label: factorial
nodes.definition: The product of all positive integers up to $n$: $n! = \prod_{k=1}^n k = 1 \times 2 \times \cdots \times n$, with $0! = 1$. Used in: combinatorics ($\binom{n}{k} = n!/(k!(n-k)!)$), multinomial coefficient, Stirling's approximation ($n! \approx \sqrt{2\pi n}(n/e)^n$).

nodes.label: factorized convolution
nodes.definition: Decomposing a standard convolution into simpler operations for efficiency. Already referenced in inception. Types: spatial factorization ($n \times n$ → $1 \times n$ + $n \times 1$), depthwise separable (depthwise + pointwise), group convolution.

nodes.label: feature engineering
nodes.definition: The process of creating, selecting, and transforming features to improve model performance. Manual: domain knowledge-based features. Automated: deep learning learns features, genetic feature synthesis. Feature crosses: $x_i \times x_j$ for interactions.

nodes.label: feature extraction
nodes.definition: Feature extraction is the construction of informative variables or representations from raw data for use in downstream modeling. Formally, it applies a map $\phi:x \mapsto \phi(x)$ that emphasizes task-relevant structure while reducing nuisance variation.

nodes.label: feature function
nodes.definition: In CRFs and structured prediction: a function $f_k(y_t, y_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}, t)$ extracting relevant features from the input and output at each position. The model: $P(\mathbf{y}|\mathbf{x}) \propto \exp(\sum_t \sum_k \lambda_k f_k)$.

nodes.label: feature rotation
nodes.definition: In Rotation Forest: applying PCA to random subsets of features per tree, creating diverse rotated feature spaces for ensemble diversity.

nodes.label: feature selection
nodes.definition: The process of selecting a subset of relevant features for model training, removing irrelevant or redundant features. Methods: filter (correlation, mutual information), wrapper (recursive feature elimination), embedded (Lasso, tree importance).

nodes.label: feature space
nodes.definition: The space in which feature vectors reside. For raw features: $\mathbb{R}^d$. For kernel methods: the implicit (possibly infinite-dimensional) feature space $\mathcal{H}$ induced by $\phi: \mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{H}$ with $K(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) = \langle \phi(\mathbf{x}), \phi(\mathbf{y}) \rangle_\mathcal{H}$.

nodes.label: feature visualization
nodes.definition: Techniques for understanding what features a neural network has learned: activation maximization (optimize input to maximize a neuron), saliency maps (gradient w.r.t. input), CAM/Grad-CAM (class activation maps), deconvolution (ZFNet).

nodes.label: feed-forward network
nodes.definition: A feed-forward network is a neural architecture in which information flows through layers without recurrent cycles, typically as a composition of affine maps and nonlinearities. In transformers, the term often refers to the positionwise multilayer perceptron sublayer.

nodes.label: financial time series
nodes.definition: Time series of financial data: stock prices, returns, volatility, exchange rates. Characterized by: heavy tails, volatility clustering (GARCH), non-stationarity. Models: ARIMA, GARCH, regime-switching.

nodes.label: fine-tuning
nodes.definition: Fine-tuning is the continued training of a pretrained model on a narrower dataset, task, or domain in order to adapt its parameters to a specific use case. It transfers previously learned representations instead of training from scratch.

nodes.label: finite state machine
nodes.definition: A computational model with a finite number of states, transitions between states triggered by inputs, and outputs determined by the current state. Tsetlin automaton: a finite-state automaton for learning.

nodes.label: fitness function
nodes.definition: A fitness function assigns a scalar score to each candidate solution in an evolutionary algorithm, measuring how well that candidate satisfies the search objective. It defines the selective pressure that guides population evolution.

nodes.label: fixed point
nodes.definition: A value $x^*$ such that $f(x^*) = x^*$. Fixed-point iteration: $x_{t+1} = f(x_t)$ converges if $|f'(x^*)| < 1$ (contraction). Deep Equilibrium Models compute fixed points of network layers. Belief propagation converges to a fixed point.

nodes.label: forward-backward algorithm
nodes.definition: A dynamic programming algorithm for computing marginal posterior probabilities $P(z_t \mid \mathbf{x}_{1:T})$ in an HMM. The forward pass computes $\alpha_t(j) = P(\mathbf{x}_{1:t}, z_t = j)$ and the backward pass computes $\beta_t(j) = P(\mathbf{x}_{t+1:T} \mid z_t = j)$.

nodes.label: foundation model
nodes.definition: A large-scale model pre-trained on broad data that can be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks: BERT, GPT, CLIP, SAM, LLaMA. Characterized by: scale, self-supervised pre-training, task generality, emergent abilities.

nodes.label: frozen model
nodes.definition: Already defined.

nodes.label: function space
nodes.definition: An infinite-dimensional vector space whose elements are functions. Examples: $L^2$ (square-integrable functions), $C[a,b]$ (continuous functions), RKHS (reproducing kernel Hilbert space). Neural operators (FNO, DeepONet) learn mappings between function spaces.

nodes.label: fuzzy set
nodes.definition: A set where membership is a degree $\mu_A(x) \in [0, 1]$ rather than binary: $\mu_A(x) = 0$ (non-member), $\mu_A(x) = 1$ (full member), $\mu_A(x) \in (0,1)$ (partial member). Operations: union ($\max$), intersection ($\min$), complement ($1-\mu$).

nodes.label: gaussian noise
nodes.definition: Random noise drawn from a Gaussian distribution: $\epsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$. Added in: diffusion models (forward process), DAE (corrupted input), DP-SGD (privacy noise), exploration (DDPG), weight noise (Bayesian NN).

nodes.label: geodesic distance
nodes.definition: The shortest-path distance along a surface or manifold, as opposed to straight-line (Euclidean) distance. In Isomap: approximated by shortest graph path on the k-NN graph. Preserves the intrinsic geometry of the manifold.

nodes.label: gibbs distribution
nodes.definition: A probability distribution proportional to the exponential of a negative energy function: $P(\mathbf{x}) \propto \exp(-E(\mathbf{x})/T)$. Equivalent to the Boltzmann distribution. Foundation for: energy-based models, Markov random fields, softmax.

nodes.label: gibbs sampling
nodes.definition: An MCMC algorithm that generates samples from a multivariate distribution by iteratively sampling each variable from its full conditional: $x_i^{(t+1)} \sim P(x_i \mid x_1^{(t+1)}, \ldots, x_{i-1}^{(t+1)}, x_{i+1}^{(t)}, \ldots)$, cycling through all variables.

nodes.label: global optimization
nodes.definition: Finding the global minimum of a (possibly non-convex) function: $\mathbf{x}^* = \arg\min_{\mathbf{x} \in \mathcal{X}} f(\mathbf{x})$. Methods: Bayesian optimization, simulated annealing, evolutionary algorithms, basin hopping, multi-start local search.

nodes.label: goal-conditioned reinforcement learning
nodes.definition: RL where the agent pursues different goals specified at each episode: the policy is conditioned on the goal $\pi(a \mid s, g)$ and the reward depends on goal achievement $r(s, a, g)$. HER: relabel failed trajectories with achieved goals.

nodes.label: graph
nodes.definition: A mathematical structure $G = (V, E)$ consisting of a set of vertices (nodes) $V$ and a set of edges $E \subseteq V \times V$ connecting pairs of vertices. Directed graphs have ordered edge pairs; undirected graphs have unordered pairs. Weighted graphs assign values to edges.

nodes.label: graphgps
nodes.definition: General, Powerful, Scalable Graph Transformer: a modular framework that combines local message-passing (MPNN) with global Transformer attention in each layer, using structural and positional encodings (random walk, Laplacian eigenvectors) to inject graph structure into the Transformer, achieving state-of-the-art on diverse graph benchmarks.

nodes.label: grid discretization
nodes.definition: Partitioning a continuous space into a regular grid of cells. In MAP-Elites: behavior space is discretized into grid cells, each storing one elite. In voxelization: 3D space into voxels. In reinforcement learning: state/action space discretization.

nodes.label: group convolution
nodes.definition: A convolution where the input channels are divided into $G$ groups, each with its own set of filters, and the outputs are concatenated. Reduces parameters and computation by a factor of $G$. ResNeXt uses group conv; depthwise separable conv is $G = C_{\text{in}}$.

nodes.label: group theory
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: The mathematical study of symmetry via algebraic structures called groups: a set $G$ with an operation $\cdot$ satisfying closure, associativity, identity, and inverse. In ML: SO(3) (rotations), SE(3) (rigid motions), permutation groups. Equivariant networks respect group symmetries.

nodes.label: grouped-query attention
nodes.definition: An attention mechanism that groups query heads into $G$ groups, with each group sharing one set of key-value heads: an interpolation between multi-head attention ($G = H$) and multi-query attention ($G = 1$), providing a tunable trade-off between quality and inference speed.

nodes.label: gru
nodes.definition: Gated Recurrent Unit: a simplified RNN gating mechanism with two gates (reset $\mathbf{r}_t$ and update $\mathbf{z}_t$) and no separate cell state: $\mathbf{h}_t = (1-\mathbf{z}_t) \odot \mathbf{h}_{t-1} + \mathbf{z}_t \odot \tilde{\mathbf{h}}_t$, where $\tilde{\mathbf{h}}_t = \tanh(\mathbf{W}[\mathbf{r}_t \odot \mathbf{h}_{t-1}, \mathbf{x}_t])$, providing comparable performance to LSTM with fewer parameters.

nodes.label: hamiltonian mechanics
nodes.category: Calculus of variations and optimal control
nodes.definition: A reformulation of classical mechanics using position $\mathbf{q}$ and momentum $\mathbf{p}$ coordinates, with dynamics governed by Hamilton's equations: $\dot{\mathbf{q}} = \partial H/\partial \mathbf{p}$, $\dot{\mathbf{p}} = -\partial H/\partial \mathbf{q}$, where $H(\mathbf{q}, \mathbf{p})$ is the Hamiltonian (total energy).

nodes.label: hazard function
nodes.definition: The hazard function of a nonnegative event time $T$ is $h(t)=f(t)/S(t)$ whenever the density $f$ and survival function $S(t)=P(T>t)$ exist. It represents the instantaneous event rate at time $t$ conditional on survival up to time $t$.

nodes.label: hidden variable
nodes.definition: A variable in a probabilistic model that is not directly observed but influences the observed data. Same as latent variable. In Boltzmann machines: hidden units. In HMMs: hidden states. In PGMs: hidden/unobserved nodes.

nodes.label: hierarchical reinforcement learning
nodes.definition: A framework that decomposes complex tasks into hierarchies of subtasks with temporal abstraction, enabling efficient exploration and transfer in long-horizon tasks.

nodes.label: hierarchical representation
nodes.definition: A multi-scale representation where features at different levels capture different abstractions: low-level (edges, textures), mid-level (parts, shapes), high-level (objects, scenes). CNN layers naturally create hierarchical features. Swin Transformer produces hierarchical feature maps.

nodes.label: hinge function
nodes.definition: A piecewise linear function: $h(x) = \max(0, x - t)$ (positive hinge) or $h(x) = \max(0, t - x)$ (negative hinge), creating a bend (hinge) at the knot $t$. MARS uses products of hinge functions as basis functions.

nodes.label: hoeffding bound
nodes.definition: A concentration inequality: for $n$ i.i.d. bounded random variables $X_i \in [a, b]$: $P(|\bar{X} - \mu| \geq t) \leq 2\exp\left(-\frac{2nt^2}{(b-a)^2}\right)$. Used in: UCB (exploration bonus), PAC learning bounds, Hoeffding tree splitting.

nodes.label: human preference
nodes.definition: A judgment by a human evaluator comparing two (or more) model outputs for quality, helpfulness, safety, or other criteria, expressed as a preference ordering. Used in RLHF to train reward models.

nodes.label: hybrid system
nodes.definition: A system combining different approaches: neuro-fuzzy (neural + fuzzy logic), neuro-symbolic (neural + symbolic reasoning), hybrid models (statistical + deep learning, e.g., ES-RNN), hybrid architectures (attention + convolution, e.g., CoAtNet).

nodes.label: hyperband
nodes.definition: A hyperparameter optimization algorithm that addresses the exploration-exploitation trade-off in Successive Halving by running it multiple times with different numbers of initial configurations $n$ and per-configuration budgets $r$, exploring the full range from many cheap evaluations to few expensive ones, and selecting the best overall configuration.

nodes.label: hypernetwork
nodes.definition: A neural network that generates the weights of another neural network: $\mathbf{W} = h_\phi(\mathbf{c})$ where $h_\phi$ is the hypernetwork and $\mathbf{c}$ is a conditioning signal. In QMIX: hypernetwork generates mixing network weights conditioned on global state.

nodes.label: hyperparameter
nodes.definition: Already defined.

nodes.label: hyperparameter optimization
nodes.definition: The process of selecting the best hyperparameters (learning rate, regularization, architecture choices) for a model. Methods: grid search, random search, Bayesian optimization (TPE, GP-BO), Hyperband, BOHB, PBT.

nodes.label: hyperplane
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: An $(n-1)$-dimensional affine subspace of $\mathbb{R}^n$ defined by $\{\mathbf{x} : \mathbf{w}^\top \mathbf{x} = b\}$, dividing the space into two half-spaces. Used as the decision boundary in linear classifiers (SVM, perceptron, logistic regression).

nodes.label: hypersphere
nodes.definition: The set of points at a fixed distance $r$ from a center point in $n$-dimensional space: $S^{n-1} = \{\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n : \|\mathbf{x}\| = r\}$. Deep SVDD fits a minimum-volume hypersphere around normal data. SVDD: support vector data description.

nodes.label: idempotent matrix
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: A matrix satisfying $\mathbf{A}^2 = \mathbf{A}$. Projection matrices are idempotent: $\mathbf{P} = \mathbf{X}(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^\top$ satisfies $\mathbf{P}^2 = \mathbf{P}$. MCL converges to an idempotent matrix (revealing clusters).

nodes.label: identity mapping
nodes.definition: The function $f(\mathbf{x}) = \mathbf{x}$ that maps every input to itself. In ResNet: the skip connection provides an identity mapping, making it easy for the network to learn $F(\mathbf{x}) = 0$ (do nothing) at any layer.

nodes.label: image
nodes.definition: A 2D array of pixel values representing a visual scene: $\mathbf{I} \in \mathbb{R}^{H \times W \times C}$ where $H$ is height, $W$ is width, and $C$ is channels (3 for RGB, 1 for grayscale). The primary input modality for computer vision.

nodes.label: image generation
nodes.definition: Creating new images from noise, text, or other conditioning signals. Methods: GANs (StyleGAN), diffusion models (Stable Diffusion, DALL-E), autoregressive (PixelCNN, Parti), flow-based (Glow), VAE-based.

nodes.label: image understanding
nodes.definition: The ability to perceive, interpret, and reason about visual content: recognizing objects, understanding spatial relationships, reading text, answering questions about images. Foundation for: VQA, captioning, visual reasoning.

nodes.label: indicator function
nodes.definition: A function that equals 1 if a condition is satisfied and 0 otherwise: $\mathbf{1}_A(x) = \begin{cases} 1 & x \in A \\ 0 & x \notin A \end{cases}$. Used in: quantile loss ($\mathbf{1}(u < 0)$), conditional distributions, Kronecker delta ($\delta_{ij}$).

nodes.label: inductive learning
nodes.definition: Learning that generalizes from training examples to unseen data (standard supervised ML). In graph learning: inductive GNNs (GraphSAGE) can generalize to new nodes/graphs, unlike transductive methods (spectral GCN) that require retraining.

nodes.label: inequality
nodes.definition: A mathematical statement comparing two expressions using $<, >, \leq, \geq, \neq$. Key inequalities in ML: Cauchy-Schwarz, Jensen's, triangle inequality, AM-GM, Hoeffding, Markov, Chebyshev.

nodes.label: inference efficiency
nodes.definition: The speed and resource usage of model inference (prediction). Key metrics: latency (ms per sample), throughput (samples/second), memory footprint. Techniques: quantization, pruning, distillation, speculative decoding, KV cache optimization.

nodes.label: inference optimization
nodes.definition: Techniques for speeding up neural network inference: quantization (INT8/INT4), operator fusion, KV cache management, speculative decoding, dynamic batching, TensorRT/ONNX Runtime compilation, flash attention.

nodes.label: inference rule
nodes.definition: In fuzzy logic: a rule of the form 'IF $x$ is $A$ THEN $y$ is $B$' that maps fuzzy input sets to fuzzy output sets. Mamdani: fuzzy consequent. Takagi-Sugeno: linear consequent.

nodes.label: infinite-dimensional space
nodes.definition: A vector space with infinite dimension: it has no finite basis. Examples: function spaces ($L^2$, $C[0,1]$), RKHS (feature space of RBF kernel), sequence spaces ($\ell^2$). GPs define distributions over functions in infinite-dimensional spaces.

nodes.label: information set
nodes.definition: In extensive-form games: a set of decision nodes that are indistinguishable to the acting player (same available actions, same information). In poker: cards dealt to opponents are hidden → multiple game states are in the same information set.

nodes.label: initial condition
nodes.definition: The value(s) of the state variable(s) at the starting time $t_0$ in a differential equation or dynamical system: $\mathbf{x}(t_0) = \mathbf{x}_0$. Together with the differential equation, specifies an initial value problem (IVP) with a unique solution under standard conditions.

nodes.label: inner product
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: A function $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle: V \times V \to \mathbb{R}$ on a vector space satisfying: (1) linearity in first argument, (2) symmetry $\langle x, y \rangle = \langle y, x \rangle$, (3) positive definiteness $\langle x, x \rangle > 0$ for $x \neq 0$. The dot product is the standard inner product on $\mathbb{R}^n$.

nodes.label: interaction term
nodes.definition: In regression: a product of two features $x_i x_j$ capturing their combined effect on the response, beyond their individual effects. Including $x_1 x_2$ allows the effect of $x_1$ on $y$ to depend on $x_2$. MARS, FM, DCN capture interactions automatically.

nodes.label: interatomic distance
nodes.definition: The distance between two atoms in a molecule or crystal: $d_{ij} = \|\mathbf{r}_i - \mathbf{r}_j\|$. Used as input features in molecular GNNs (SchNet, DimeNet). Rotationally invariant quantity.

nodes.label: intermittent demand
nodes.definition: A demand pattern with many zero periods interspersed with occasional non-zero demand. Common in: spare parts, slow-moving inventory. Forecasting: Croston's method (separate size and interval), TSB method.

nodes.label: interpolation
nodes.definition: Estimating values between known data points. Linear: $f(x) = f(a) + (f(b)-f(a))(x-a)/(b-a)$. Bilinear (2D), trilinear (3D). Spline: smooth piecewise polynomial. In N-HiTS: upsampling forecasts from low to full resolution.

nodes.label: invariant point attention
nodes.definition: In AlphaFold's Structure Module: an attention mechanism that operates on 3D point clouds of residue frames, ensuring the output is invariant to global rotations and translations of the input structure while using local geometric features.

nodes.label: inverse function
nodes.definition: A function $f^{-1}: Y \to X$ such that $f^{-1}(f(x)) = x$ for all $x \in X$ and $f(f^{-1}(y)) = y$ for all $y \in Y$. Exists only for bijective functions. Example: $\exp^{-1} = \ln$, $\sigma^{-1} = \text{logit}$.

nodes.label: item
nodes.definition: In recommendation systems: a product, article, video, or any object that can be recommended to a user. Each item has features (title, category, price) and an embedding learned from interactions.

nodes.label: itemset
nodes.definition: A set of items (products, features) occurring together. In association rule mining: an itemset $X = \{a, b, c\}$ has support $= P(X \subseteq \text{transaction})$. Frequent itemset: support $\geq$ threshold.

nodes.label: iteration
nodes.definition: A single execution of the body of a loop or recursive process. In optimization: one gradient update step. In EM: one E-step + M-step cycle. In MCTS: one selection-expansion-simulation-backpropagation cycle.

nodes.label: iterative algorithm
nodes.definition: An algorithm that repeatedly applies an update rule to produce a sequence of approximations converging to a solution: $\mathbf{x}_{t+1} = T(\mathbf{x}_t)$, where $T$ is a mapping. Examples: gradient descent, EM, power iteration, fixed-point iteration.

nodes.label: johnson-lindenstrauss lemma
nodes.definition: For any $\epsilon > 0$ and $n$ points, there exists a linear projection to $k = O(\epsilon^{-2} \log n)$ dimensions that preserves all pairwise distances within $(1 \pm \epsilon)$. Random Gaussian projections achieve this with high probability.

nodes.label: joint feature map
nodes.definition: In structured SVM: a function $\Phi(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y})$ mapping input-output pairs to a feature space: $\hat{\mathbf{y}} = \arg\max_\mathbf{y} \mathbf{w}^\top \Phi(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y})$.

nodes.label: joint probability distribution
nodes.definition: The probability distribution over all possible combinations of values of two or more random variables: $P(X = x, Y = y)$ (discrete) or $f_{X,Y}(x,y)$ (continuous), from which marginal and conditional distributions can be derived.

nodes.label: kernel matrix
nodes.definition: A matrix $\mathbf{K} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ where $K_{ij} = K(\mathbf{x}_i, \mathbf{x}_j)$ evaluates a kernel function on all pairs of data points. Always positive semidefinite (Mercer). Also called the Gram matrix in the kernel context.

nodes.label: kernel trick
nodes.definition: Computing inner products in a high-dimensional feature space $\langle \phi(\mathbf{x}), \phi(\mathbf{y}) \rangle = K(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y})$ without explicitly computing $\phi$. Enables nonlinear algorithms (SVM, PCA, regression) by replacing dot products with kernel evaluations. Mercer's theorem guarantees validity.

nodes.label: key-value pair
nodes.definition: A fundamental data structure element pairing a key (for lookup) with a value (the stored data). In Transformers: key-value pairs $(\mathbf{k}_i, \mathbf{v}_i)$ are attended to by queries. In key-value memory networks: external knowledge storage.

nodes.label: key-value store
nodes.definition: A data structure mapping keys to values, supporting efficient lookup. In attention: keys $\mathbf{K}$ and values $\mathbf{V}$ form a key-value store queried by queries $\mathbf{Q}$. KV cache: stores computed K,V for autoregressive generation.

nodes.label: lagrangian mechanics
nodes.category: Calculus of variations and optimal control
nodes.definition: A reformulation of classical mechanics using generalized coordinates $\mathbf{q}$ and the Lagrangian $L = T - V$ (kinetic minus potential energy), with equations of motion given by the Euler-Lagrange equations. LNNs learn $L_\theta(\mathbf{q}, \dot{\mathbf{q}})$ from data.

nodes.label: lambda return
nodes.definition: The $\lambda$-weighted average of all $n$-step returns: $G_t^\lambda = (1-\lambda) \sum_{n=1}^\infty \lambda^{n-1} G_t^{(n)}$, interpolating between TD(0) ($\lambda=0$) and MC ($\lambda=1$). Equivalent to the GAE advantage + value.

nodes.label: latent space
nodes.definition: The learned representation space in which encoders (autoencoders, VAEs) map input data. In latent diffusion: the compressed space where diffusion operates. In StyleGAN: the $\mathcal{W}$ space for disentangled control. Properties: smoothness, disentanglement, interpolation.

nodes.label: lateral connection
nodes.definition: In FPN: a connection between the bottom-up (encoder) and top-down (decoder) pathways at matching resolution levels, typically via a 1x1 convolution + element-wise addition, enriching upsampled features with high-resolution spatial details.

nodes.label: leaky relu
nodes.definition: A variant of ReLU that allows a small gradient for negative inputs: $\text{LeakyReLU}(x) = \max(\alpha x, x)$ with $\alpha \sim 0.01$, preventing dead neurons that can occur with standard ReLU.

nodes.label: learning rate warmup
nodes.definition: Gradually increasing the learning rate from 0 (or a small value) to the target value during the initial training steps, preventing large, destabilizing updates when the model is far from any reasonable solution. Critical for Transformer training.

nodes.label: limit
nodes.definition: The value that a function or sequence approaches as the input approaches some value: $\lim_{x \to a} f(x) = L$ means for every $\epsilon > 0$, there exists $\delta > 0$ such that $|f(x) - L| < \epsilon$ whenever $0 < |x - a| < \delta$ ($\epsilon$-$\delta$ definition).

nodes.label: linear algebra
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: The branch of mathematics studying vector spaces, linear transformations, matrices, and systems of linear equations. Foundation for: neural networks (matrix multiplication), PCA (eigendecomposition), SVD, optimization, and virtually all of machine learning.

nodes.label: linear constraint
nodes.definition: A constraint of the form $\mathbf{a}^\top \mathbf{x} \leq b$ (inequality) or $\mathbf{a}^\top \mathbf{x} = b$ (equality), defining a half-space or hyperplane in the feasible region. A set of linear constraints defines a polyhedron.

nodes.label: linear interpolation
nodes.definition: A method for estimating values between two known data points by connecting them with a straight line: $y = y_0 + (y_1 - y_0) \frac{x - x_0}{x_1 - x_0} = (1-t) y_0 + t y_1$ where $t = (x - x_0)/(x_1 - x_0) \in [0, 1]$.

nodes.label: linear scoring function
nodes.definition: A scoring function $s(d) = \mathbf{w}^\top \mathbf{f}(d)$ that is linear in the weights: the score is a weighted sum of features. Used in: linear learning to rank (coordinate ascent), logistic regression, linear SVM.

nodes.label: linkage criterion
nodes.definition: In agglomerative clustering: the rule for measuring distance between clusters. Single (min distance), complete (max), average (mean pairwise), Ward (min variance increase). Choice strongly affects cluster shapes.

nodes.label: lipschitz continuity
nodes.definition: A function $f$ is $L$-Lipschitz if $\|f(\mathbf{x}) - f(\mathbf{y})\| \leq L \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{y}\|$ for all $\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}$. WGAN requires the discriminator to be 1-Lipschitz (enforced by weight clipping or gradient penalty). Lipschitz bounds → generalization bounds.

nodes.label: llm alignment
nodes.definition: The process of making LLM outputs helpful, harmless, and honest, aligning behavior with human values and preferences. Methods: RLHF, DPO, Constitutional AI, RLAIF.

nodes.label: load balancing
nodes.definition: In MoE: ensuring all experts receive roughly equal numbers of tokens, preventing expert collapse (some experts unused). Achieved via auxiliary loss: $\mathcal{L}_{\text{aux}} = \alpha N \sum_i f_i P_i$ where $f_i$ is fraction routed to expert $i$ and $P_i$ is average routing probability.

nodes.label: log-likelihood
nodes.definition: The logarithm of the likelihood: $\ell(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \log L(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \sum_{i=1}^n \log P(x_i \mid \boldsymbol{\theta})$. Maximized in MLE. Converted products to sums for numerical stability. Negative log-likelihood = cross-entropy loss.

nodes.label: log-sum-exp
nodes.definition: The function $\text{lse}(\mathbf{z}) = \log \sum_i \exp(z_i)$, a smooth approximation to the maximum function. Used in: softmax (numerically stable implementation), free energy computation, modern Hopfield networks. Property: $\max(\mathbf{z}) \leq \text{lse}(\mathbf{z}) \leq \max(\mathbf{z}) + \log n$.

nodes.label: loopy belief propagation
nodes.definition: An approximate inference algorithm that applies the belief propagation (sum-product) message-passing equations on graphical models with cycles (loops), iterating until convergence despite the lack of convergence guarantees, to approximate marginal distributions at each node.

nodes.label: low-rank approximation
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: Approximating a matrix $\mathbf{A}$ by a matrix of lower rank $k$: $\mathbf{A} \approx \mathbf{A}_k = \mathbf{U}_k \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_k \mathbf{V}_k^\top$ (truncated SVD). Optimal in Frobenius/spectral norm (Eckart-Young theorem). Used in: PCA, matrix completion, LoRA, Linformer.

nodes.label: luong attention
nodes.definition: A simplified attention mechanism where the alignment score is computed as a dot product (or general bilinear form) between the decoder state and encoder states: $e_{tj} = \mathbf{s}_t^\top \mathbf{h}_j$ (dot) or $e_{tj} = \mathbf{s}_t^\top \mathbf{W} \mathbf{h}_j$ (general), applied after the decoder RNN step.

nodes.label: lyapunov function
nodes.definition: A function $V(\mathbf{x})$ used to prove stability of a dynamical system: if $V > 0$ and $\dot{V} \leq 0$ (non-increasing along trajectories), the system is stable. In Hopfield networks: the energy function is a Lyapunov function (decreases with updates), proving convergence.

nodes.label: magnitude
nodes.definition: The absolute value (scalars) or norm (vectors) of a quantity: $|x|$ or $\|\mathbf{x}\|$. In pruning: remove weights with smallest magnitude. In gradient clipping: bound gradient magnitude.

nodes.label: magnitude pruning
nodes.definition: Removing neural network weights with the smallest absolute value: set $w_i = 0$ if $|w_i| < \tau$ (threshold). The simplest and most common pruning method. Iterative magnitude pruning (IMP): train → prune → retrain. Foundation for Lottery Ticket Hypothesis.

nodes.label: margin
nodes.definition: In classification: the distance between the decision boundary and the nearest data points (support vectors). SVM maximizes the margin $2/\|\mathbf{w}\|$. In metric learning: a minimum distance between positive and negative pairs in the loss.

nodes.label: masking
nodes.definition: Setting certain elements to a special value (zero, $-\infty$, or [MASK] token) to hide information: attention masking (causal, padding), input masking (BERT MLM, MAE), dropout masking (random zeros).

nodes.label: matching
nodes.definition: In causal inference: pairing treated and control units with similar covariates (or propensity scores) to estimate treatment effects. In feature matching: finding correspondences between keypoints. In DETR: Hungarian matching of predictions to ground truth.

nodes.label: matrix function
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: A function applied to a matrix via its eigendecomposition: $f(\mathbf{A}) = \mathbf{U} f(\boldsymbol{\Lambda}) \mathbf{U}^\top$. Examples: matrix exponential, matrix square root, matrix logarithm. Muon optimizer uses the matrix sign function.

nodes.label: matrix update
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: An incremental modification to a matrix without full recomputation. Sherman-Morrison: rank-1 update to inverse. BLS: pseudoinverse update for new nodes. Woodbury: general rank-$k$ update. K-FAC: EMA update of Kronecker factors.

nodes.label: maximum
nodes.definition: The largest element of a set or the largest value of a function: $\max S = \sup S$ when the supremum is attained. The argmax is the element achieving the maximum: $\arg\max_x f(x) = \{x : f(x) = \max f\}$.

nodes.label: mean pooling
nodes.definition: Computing the mean over a set of values for aggregation: average over spatial dimensions (global average pooling), over sequence positions (Sentence-BERT mean pooling), or over graph neighbors (GCN aggregation).

nodes.label: measurement
nodes.definition: The process of quantifying an attribute of an object or phenomenon, producing a numerical value. Measurements form the raw data for statistical analysis and ML. Subject to noise, bias, and precision limitations.

nodes.label: median
nodes.definition: The middle value when data is sorted: for $n$ values, the median is the $(n+1)/2$-th value (odd $n$) or the average of the $n/2$-th and $(n/2+1)$-th values (even $n$). Robust to outliers (breakdown point 50%). Used in: Theil-Sen slope, MAD, median regression.

nodes.label: medoid
nodes.definition: The data point within a cluster that minimizes the total distance to all other points in the cluster: $\mathbf{m} = \arg\min_{\mathbf{x} \in C} \sum_{\mathbf{y} \in C} d(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y})$. Unlike centroids (which may not be data points), medoids are actual observations.

nodes.label: membership function
nodes.definition: In fuzzy sets: a function $\mu_A: X \to [0, 1]$ assigning each element $x$ a degree of membership in the fuzzy set $A$. Common shapes: triangular, trapezoidal, Gaussian, sigmoid. In fuzzy c-means: $u_{ik}$ is the membership of point $i$ in cluster $k$.

nodes.label: membrane potential
nodes.definition: In biological and spiking neural network models: the voltage across a neuron's membrane: $V(t)$. Accumulates input currents, decays toward resting potential, and fires a spike when exceeding the threshold. LIF: $\tau dV/dt = -(V - V_{\text{rest}}) + RI$.

nodes.label: memoization
nodes.definition: Caching the results of expensive function calls and returning the cached result when the same inputs occur again. Top-down dynamic programming uses memoization to avoid recomputing overlapping subproblems.

nodes.label: mercer theorem
nodes.definition: A continuous, symmetric, positive semi-definite kernel function $K(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y})$ can be represented as $K(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) = \sum_{i=1}^\infty \lambda_i \phi_i(\mathbf{x}) \phi_i(\mathbf{y})$ (eigenfunction expansion), ensuring it defines a valid inner product in some feature space.

nodes.label: meta-learner
nodes.definition: A model or algorithm that learns across tasks to improve learning efficiency on new tasks. In stacking: a meta-learner combines base model predictions. In MAML: the meta-learner is the initialization. In uplift modeling: T/S/X-learners are meta-learners for CATE estimation.

nodes.label: meta-learning
nodes.definition: Learning to learn: training a model on a distribution of tasks so it can quickly adapt to new tasks with few examples. Approaches: optimization-based (MAML), metric-based (Prototypical Networks), memory-based (Neural Statistician), in-context learning (GPT).

nodes.label: metis algorithm
nodes.definition: A multilevel graph partitioning algorithm: (1) coarsen the graph by matching and collapsing vertices, (2) partition the coarsened graph, (3) uncoarsen while refining the partition. Fast and produces high-quality partitions. Used in Chameleon clustering and ClusterGCN.

nodes.label: metropolis-hastings
nodes.definition: A Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that generates samples from a target distribution $\pi(\boldsymbol{\theta})$ by proposing moves from a proposal distribution $q(\boldsymbol{\theta}' \mid \boldsymbol{\theta})$ and accepting them with probability $\alpha = \min\left(1, \frac{\pi(\boldsymbol{\theta}') q(\boldsymbol{\theta} \mid \boldsymbol{\theta}')}{\pi(\boldsymbol{\theta}) q(\boldsymbol{\theta}' \mid \boldsymbol{\…

nodes.label: min-max optimization
nodes.definition: An optimization problem $\min_\mathbf{x} \max_\mathbf{y} f(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y})$ where one player minimizes and the other maximizes. Used in GANs (generator vs. discriminator), adversarial training, game theory (minimax theorem), and SAM.

nodes.label: minimax game
nodes.definition: A two-player zero-sum game where one player minimizes and the other maximizes the same objective: $\min_G \max_D f(G, D)$. GANs: generator minimizes, discriminator maximizes. Von Neumann: equilibrium exists for convex-concave games.

nodes.label: minimum
nodes.definition: The smallest element of a set or the smallest value of a function: $\min S$ or $\min_x f(x)$. Argmin: the point achieving the minimum. Used in: optimization ($\min_\theta \mathcal{L}$), min pooling, min in clipping.

nodes.label: missing data
nodes.definition: Data points with unobserved values. Types: MCAR (completely random), MAR (depends on observed), MNAR (depends on unobserved). Methods: deletion (listwise, pairwise), imputation (mean, regression, MICE, EM), probabilistic models that handle missing values (GPs, factor analysis).

nodes.label: mixture model
nodes.definition: A probabilistic model representing the data as a mixture of simpler distributions: $p(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_{k=1}^K \pi_k p_k(\mathbf{x})$ where $\pi_k$ are mixing weights. GMM: Gaussian components. LDA: multinomial components. DPMM: infinite components.

nodes.label: model
nodes.definition: A mathematical representation of a system or process, parameterized by $\boldsymbol{\theta}$: $f_\theta: X \to Y$. In ML, a model maps inputs to predictions. In statistics, a probabilistic model specifies $P(\text{data} \mid \theta)$.

nodes.label: model efficiency
nodes.definition: The ratio of model performance to computational cost (FLOPs, parameters, latency, memory). Efficient architectures: MobileNet, EfficientNet, SqueezeNet. Efficient inference: quantization, pruning, distillation. Efficient training: mixed precision, DeepSpeed ZeRO.

nodes.label: model fitting
nodes.definition: The process of estimating model parameters from data: OLS for linear regression, MLE for parametric models, EM for latent variable models, backpropagation for neural networks, IRLS for GLMs. The estimated parameters minimize a loss or maximize a likelihood.

nodes.label: model predictive control
nodes.definition: Model predictive control is a control method that repeatedly solves a finite-horizon optimization problem using a model of system dynamics, applies only the first action, and then replans at the next step. It is a receding-horizon strategy for constrained sequential decision making.

nodes.label: molecular graph
nodes.definition: A graph representation of a molecule where nodes are atoms (with features: atomic number, charge, hybridization) and edges are chemical bonds (with features: bond type, aromaticity, conjugation). Input to molecular GNNs.

nodes.label: monotone alignment
