nodes.definition: A simulation-free training framework for continuous normalizing flows that regresses a neural network velocity field $v_\theta(\mathbf{x}, t)$ against a target conditional vector field $u_t(\mathbf{x} \mid \mathbf{x}_1)$ defined by simple conditional probability paths (e.g., Gaussian), without requiring ODE simulation during training.

nodes.label: fnet
nodes.definition: A Transformer variant that replaces the self-attention sublayer with a parameter-free 2D discrete Fourier transform applied along the sequence and hidden dimensions: $\mathbf{Y} = \operatorname{Re}(\operatorname{FFT}_{\text{seq}}(\operatorname{FFT}_{\text{hidden}}(\mathbf{X})))$, achieving $O(n \log n)$ complexity with no learnable attention parameters.

nodes.label: forecasting
nodes.definition: Predicting future values of a time series based on historical observations. Methods: statistical (ARIMA, ETS, Prophet), ML (gradient boosting on features), deep learning (DeepAR, TFT, PatchTST, N-BEATS). Evaluation: MAE, MAPE, SMAPE, MASE.

nodes.label: fourier features
nodes.definition: Random or deterministic features $\phi(\mathbf{x}) = [\cos(\mathbf{w}_1^\top \mathbf{x}), \sin(\mathbf{w}_1^\top \mathbf{x}), \ldots]$ that approximate kernel evaluations: $K(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) \approx \phi(\mathbf{x})^\top \phi(\mathbf{y})$ (Random Fourier Features, Rahimi & Recht, 2007). Used in: Performer, NeRF positional encoding, IQN.

nodes.label: free energy
nodes.definition: In statistical mechanics: $F = U - TS$ (Helmholtz) or $F = -T \log Z$ (connects partition function to free energy). In variational inference: the negative ELBO $-\mathcal{L}(q) = \text{KL}(q \| p) + \text{const}$ is the variational free energy.

nodes.label: frobenius norm
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: The $L_2$ norm of a matrix treated as a vector: $\|\mathbf{A}\|_F = \sqrt{\sum_{i,j} |a_{ij}|^2} = \sqrt{\text{tr}(\mathbf{A}^\top \mathbf{A})} = \sqrt{\sum_i \sigma_i^2}$ (square root of sum of squared singular values).

nodes.label: fully connected layer
nodes.definition: A neural network layer where every input neuron is connected to every output neuron: $\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{W}\mathbf{x} + \mathbf{b}$ with $\mathbf{W} \in \mathbb{R}^{m \times n}$. Also called a dense layer or linear layer (without activation).

nodes.label: function
nodes.definition: A function $f:A \to B$ assigns to each input $a \in A$ exactly one output $f(a) \in B$. The sets $A$ and $B$ are called the domain and codomain, and functions are the formal language of dependence and transformation in mathematics.

nodes.label: fused lasso
nodes.definition: A regularized regression method that penalizes both the $\ell_1$ norm of coefficients and the $\ell_1$ norm of consecutive differences: $\min_{\boldsymbol{\beta}} \frac{1}{2}\|\mathbf{y} - \mathbf{X}\boldsymbol{\beta}\|_2^2 + \lambda_1 \|\boldsymbol{\beta}\|_1 + \lambda_2 \sum_{j=2}^{p} |\beta_j - \beta_{j-1}|$, encouraging both sparsity and piecewise constancy in the coefficient profile.

nodes.label: fusion-in-decoder
nodes.definition: A retrieval-augmented generation method where multiple retrieved passages are independently encoded by the encoder (each passage concatenated with the query), and the decoder attends to all encoded passages jointly via cross-attention, enabling efficient fusion of evidence from multiple sources.

nodes.label: fuzzy c-means
nodes.definition: A soft clustering algorithm that assigns each point a membership degree $u_{ik} \in [0,1]$ to each cluster (with $\sum_k u_{ik} = 1$), minimizing $J = \sum_{i=1}^{n} \sum_{k=1}^{c} u_{ik}^m \|\mathbf{x}_i - \mathbf{v}_k\|^2$ where $m > 1$ is the fuzziness parameter, iterating between updating memberships and centroids.

nodes.label: gamma function
nodes.definition: The gamma function is the analytic continuation of the factorial to noninteger arguments, defined for $\Re(z)>0$ by $\Gamma(z)=\int_0^{\infty} t^{z-1}e^{-t} \; dt$. It satisfies $\Gamma(n+1)=n!$ for every natural number $n$.

nodes.label: gated linear unit
nodes.definition: An activation function that uses a gating mechanism: $\text{GLU}(\mathbf{x}) = (\mathbf{x} \mathbf{W}_1 + \mathbf{b}_1) \otimes \sigma(\mathbf{x} \mathbf{W}_2 + \mathbf{b}_2)$, where $\otimes$ is element-wise multiplication and $\sigma$ is sigmoid. Variants: SwiGLU (Swish gate), GeGLU (GELU gate).

nodes.label: gated residual network
nodes.definition: A building block in Temporal Fusion Transformer consisting of: (1) skip connection, (2) nonlinear processing (dense + ELU + dense), (3) gating layer (GLU), and (4) layer normalization. Provides flexible nonlinear processing with skip connection for gradient flow.

nodes.label: gating mechanism
nodes.definition: A neural network component that controls information flow using learned gates (typically sigmoid-activated vectors) that element-wise multiply another signal: $\mathbf{g} = \sigma(\mathbf{W}_g \mathbf{x} + \mathbf{b}_g)$, $\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{g} \odot \mathbf{h}$. Used in LSTM, GRU, GLU, highway networks.

nodes.label: gaussian distribution
nodes.definition: A Gaussian distribution is a probability distribution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ with density $p(x)=(2\pi)^{-d/2}\det(\Sigma)^{-1/2}\exp\!\bigl(-\tfrac12(x-\mu)^\top \Sigma^{-1}(x-\mu)\bigr)$ for mean vector $\mu$ and positive-definite covariance matrix $\Sigma$. It is the multivariate family determined entirely by first and second moments.

nodes.label: gaussian process
nodes.definition: A Gaussian process is a stochastic process indexed by inputs such that every finite collection of function values is jointly Gaussian. It is completely specified by a mean function $m(x)$ and covariance kernel $k(x,x')$.

nodes.label: gaussian process bandit
nodes.definition: A Bayesian optimization framework where a Gaussian process models the unknown reward function, and an acquisition function (GP-UCB: $\mu_t(\mathbf{x}) + \beta_t \sigma_t(\mathbf{x})$, or Thompson sampling from the GP posterior) guides exploration-exploitation, achieving sublinear regret bounds that depend on the kernel's maximum information gain.

nodes.label: generalized estimating equations
nodes.definition: A semi-parametric method for estimating regression parameters in models for correlated data by solving $\sum_{i=1}^{n} \mathbf{D}_i^\top \mathbf{V}_i^{-1} (\mathbf{y}_i - \boldsymbol{\mu}_i) = \mathbf{0}$, where $\mathbf{V}_i = \mathbf{A}_i^{1/2} \mathbf{R}(\boldsymbol{\alpha}) \mathbf{A}_i^{1/2}$ uses a working correlation matrix $\mathbf{R}(\boldsymbol{\alpha})$ that need not be correctly specified for consistent e…

nodes.label: genetic algorithm
nodes.definition: A genetic algorithm is a population-based optimization method that iteratively applies selection, crossover, and mutation to candidate solutions encoded as genomes. It searches for high-fitness individuals without requiring gradient information.

nodes.label: geometric series
nodes.definition: A series where each term is a constant multiple $r$ (ratio) of the previous: $\sum_{k=0}^{n} r^k = \frac{1-r^{n+1}}{1-r}$ (finite) and $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} r^k = \frac{1}{1-r}$ for $|r| < 1$ (infinite). Foundation for discounted returns in RL ($\gamma < 1$) and exponential decay.

nodes.label: ghostnet
nodes.definition: An efficient CNN architecture that generates redundant feature maps (ghost features) through cheap linear operations (depthwise convolutions) applied to a subset of intrinsic features, rather than computing all feature maps with standard convolutions, reducing computational cost while maintaining accuracy.

nodes.label: gini impurity
nodes.definition: A measure of impurity for classification: $G = 1 - \sum_{k=1}^{K} p_k^2$ where $p_k$ is the fraction of class $k$. Ranges from 0 (pure) to $1 - 1/K$ (maximally mixed). Used as the default splitting criterion in CART.

nodes.label: glow
nodes.definition: A normalizing flow model that extends RealNVP with invertible $1 \times 1$ convolutions (learned permutations of channels, parameterized via LU decomposition) between coupling layers, and uses the actnorm layer (data-dependent normalization) instead of batch normalization, enabling high-quality image generation.

nodes.label: gradient aggregation
nodes.definition: In distributed training: combining gradients from multiple workers before applying the parameter update. All-reduce: average gradients across all workers. Async: workers apply gradients independently.

nodes.label: gradient boosting
nodes.definition: Gradient boosting is an additive ensemble method that builds a predictor as a sum of weak learners fit sequentially to reduce the current loss, often by approximating negative gradients or residuals. It is one of the most powerful generic methods for tabular prediction.

nodes.label: gradient clipping
nodes.definition: Preventing exploding gradients by scaling the gradient when its norm exceeds a threshold. Already defined.

nodes.label: gradient penalty
nodes.definition: A regularization term penalizing the gradient norm of the discriminator in Wasserstein GAN (WGAN-GP): $\mathcal{L}_{\text{GP}} = \lambda E_{\hat{\mathbf{x}}}[(\|\nabla_{\hat{\mathbf{x}}} D(\hat{\mathbf{x}})\| - 1)^2]$ where $\hat{\mathbf{x}}$ is interpolated between real and fake samples, enforcing the 1-Lipschitz constraint.

nodes.label: graph attention network
nodes.definition: A GNN that uses attention mechanisms to compute different weights for different neighbors when aggregating features: $\alpha_{ij} = \text{softmax}_j(\text{LeakyReLU}(\mathbf{a}^\top [\mathbf{W}\mathbf{h}_i \| \mathbf{W}\mathbf{h}_j]))$, enabling the model to learn which neighbors are most important for each node.

nodes.label: graph classification
nodes.definition: The task of predicting a label for an entire graph (not individual nodes). Methods: GNN + readout (sum/mean/attention pooling of node features), DiffPool (hierarchical pooling), WL kernel + SVM.

nodes.label: graph coarsening
nodes.definition: Reducing the number of nodes in a graph while preserving its structure: group nodes into super-nodes and merge edges. DiffPool learns a soft assignment for coarsening. Used in: hierarchical GNN, graph pooling, multi-resolution processing.

nodes.label: graph cut
nodes.definition: A partition of a graph's vertices into two or more disjoint sets, with the cost being the total weight of edges crossing the partition. Minimum cut: partition minimizing edge weight. Normalized cut: balances partition sizes. Used in spectral clustering.

nodes.label: graph isomorphism
nodes.definition: Two graphs are isomorphic if there exists a bijection between their vertex sets that preserves adjacency. Testing graph isomorphism is not known to be in P or NP-complete. The WL test is a practical heuristic; GIN matches its discriminative power.

nodes.label: graph partitioning
nodes.definition: Dividing a graph's vertices into $k$ roughly equal-sized groups while minimizing the number of edges between groups. NP-hard; solved approximately by: METIS (multilevel), spectral methods, streaming algorithms.

nodes.label: graph transformer
nodes.definition: A Transformer architecture adapted for graphs that computes self-attention between all node pairs (or a selected subset) with positional/structural encodings (e.g., Laplacian eigenvectors, random walk statistics) to inject graph topology information, overcoming the locality limitation of message-passing GNNs.

nodes.label: graphical lasso
nodes.definition: A method for estimating a sparse inverse covariance (precision) matrix $\boldsymbol{\Theta} = \boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1}$ of a multivariate Gaussian distribution by maximizing the $\ell_1$-penalized log-likelihood: $\max_{\boldsymbol{\Theta} \succ 0} \log \det \boldsymbol{\Theta} - \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{S}\boldsymbol{\Theta}) - \lambda \|\boldsymbol{\Theta}\|_{1,\text{off}}$.

nodes.label: greedy layer-wise training
nodes.definition: Training a deep network one layer at a time (bottom-up): train layer 1 as an RBM/autoencoder, freeze it, train layer 2 on layer 1's output, etc. Used to initialize deep belief networks before fine-tuning. Largely superseded by modern initialization and normalization.

nodes.label: grounded sam
nodes.definition: A pipeline combining Grounding DINO (for text-prompted open-set object detection) with the Segment Anything Model (for prompt-based segmentation): Grounding DINO detects bounding boxes for text-described objects, which are then used as box prompts for SAM to generate precise segmentation masks.

nodes.label: gru4rec
nodes.definition: The first RNN-based session-based recommendation model that processes a session's click sequence through a GRU network and predicts the next clicked item, using a ranking-based loss (BPR or TOP1) and mini-batch parallel processing of sessions.

nodes.label: h3
nodes.definition: Hungry Hungry Hippos: a state space model layer that combines two SSM layers with multiplicative gating: $y = (\text{SSM}_1(\mathbf{x}) \odot \mathbf{x}) \cdot \text{SSM}_2(\text{shift}(\mathbf{x}))$, designed to close the gap with Transformers on language modeling by improving the model's ability to perform recall (associative memory) tasks.

nodes.label: handwritten digit recognition
nodes.definition: The classic pattern recognition task of classifying images of handwritten digits (0-9). MNIST dataset: 28×28 grayscale images. First CNN application (LeNet-5). Benchmark for: autoencoders, GANs, few-shot learning.

nodes.label: hdbscan
nodes.definition: Hierarchical DBSCAN: an extension of DBSCAN that builds a hierarchy of clusterings across all possible $\epsilon$ values, extracts a condensed cluster tree, and selects the most stable clusters (those persisting over the widest range of density thresholds), handling clusters of varying density without requiring a fixed $\epsilon$.

nodes.label: hessian lle
nodes.definition: A variant of LLE that uses the Hessian matrix of the local tangent space at each point to construct the weight matrix, providing a theoretically grounded method that correctly recovers the global coordinates of data lying on a manifold when the manifold is locally isometric to Euclidean space.

nodes.label: hessian matrix
nodes.definition: The matrix of second-order partial derivatives of a scalar function: $H_{ij} = \frac{\partial^2 f}{\partial x_i \partial x_j}$. For smooth functions, $\mathbf{H}$ is symmetric. $\mathbf{H} \succ 0$ at a critical point indicates a local minimum.

nodes.label: hidden naive bayes
nodes.definition: An extension of Naive Bayes that introduces a hidden parent for each attribute to model attribute dependencies, where the hidden parent combines information from all other attributes, relaxing the conditional independence assumption while maintaining computational efficiency.

nodes.label: hierarchical clustering
nodes.definition: Clustering methods that create a hierarchy of clusters (dendrogram). Agglomerative (bottom-up): start with singletons, merge closest. Divisive (top-down): start with one cluster, split.

nodes.label: hierarchical mixture of experts
nodes.definition: A tree-structured mixture of experts where a hierarchy of gating networks recursively partitions the input space: the top-level gate selects a branch, each branch contains sub-gates that further specialize, with expert networks at the leaves, enabling a soft decision tree-like decomposition of the input space.

nodes.label: hifi-gan
nodes.definition: A neural vocoder that converts mel spectrograms to audio waveforms using a GAN with: (1) a generator with multi-scale transposed convolutions and multi-receptive field fusion, (2) multi-scale and multi-period discriminators. Extremely fast and high-quality synthesis.

nodes.label: hindsight experience replay
nodes.definition: A technique for goal-conditioned RL that replays failed trajectories by substituting the achieved goal as the desired goal in hindsight, generating successful training experiences from failures.

nodes.label: hippo matrix
nodes.definition: History through Projected Polynomials: a specific initialization for the state matrix $\mathbf{A}$ in SSMs (S4) that optimally compresses the input history into a polynomial basis, providing a theoretically grounded way to capture long-range dependencies.

nodes.label: holt-winters
nodes.definition: An exponential smoothing method for time series with trend and seasonality, using three smoothing equations for level ($\ell_t = \alpha(y_t - s_{t-m}) + (1-\alpha)(\ell_{t-1}+b_{t-1})$), trend ($b_t = \beta(\ell_t - \ell_{t-1}) + (1-\beta)b_{t-1}$), and seasonality ($s_t = \gamma(y_t - \ell_t) + (1-\gamma)s_{t-m}$), supporting both additive and multiplicative seasonal patterns.

nodes.label: i-jepa
nodes.definition: Image-based Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture: a self-supervised method that predicts the representation of a target image block from the representation of a context block (with a large portion masked), using an asymmetric architecture where the predictor operates in representation space rather than pixel space, avoiding the need for handcrafted augmentations.

nodes.label: id3
nodes.definition: Iterative Dichotomiser 3: a decision tree algorithm that selects the attribute with the highest information gain (reduction in entropy) at each node, creates one branch per attribute value (multi-way splits), and does not perform pruning.

nodes.label: image captioning
nodes.definition: The task of generating a natural language description of an image. Encoder-decoder: CNN/ViT encodes image → RNN/Transformer decodes caption. Modern: VLMs generate captions via prompting.

nodes.label: image-to-image translation
nodes.definition: Converting an image from one domain to another: input→output paired (Pix2Pix) or unpaired (CycleGAN). Examples: sketch→photo, day→night, semantic map→photo.

nodes.label: imitation learning
nodes.definition: Learning from expert demonstrations. Already defined.

nodes.label: impala
nodes.definition: Importance Weighted Actor-Learner Architecture: a distributed RL framework that decouples acting (many actors collecting experience in parallel) from learning (a centralized learner), using V-trace off-policy corrections $v_s = V(x_s) + \sum_{t=s}^{s+n-1} \gamma^{t-s} (\prod_{i=s}^{t-1} c_i) \delta_t V$ to correct for the policy lag between actors and learner.

nodes.label: implicit differentiation
nodes.definition: Computing derivatives of implicitly defined functions: if $F(x, y) = 0$ defines $y$ as a function of $x$, then $dy/dx = -F_x/F_y$. In DEQ: differentiate through fixed-point equations $z^* = f(z^*, x)$ without unrolling. In bilevel optimization: differentiate through the inner optimum.

nodes.label: incremental pca
nodes.definition: An online algorithm for PCA that processes data in mini-batches, updating the principal components incrementally without storing or revisiting the entire dataset, using techniques like the incremental SVD update or the Candid Covariance-Free approach.

nodes.label: influence function
nodes.definition: In robust statistics: the effect of infinitesimally contaminating the data distribution on an estimator: $\text{IF}(x; T, F) = \lim_{\epsilon \to 0} \frac{T((1-\epsilon)F + \epsilon \delta_x) - T(F)}{\epsilon}$. Bounded IF → robust estimator. In ML: measures the effect of removing a training point on model predictions.

nodes.label: infonce loss
nodes.definition: The InfoNCE (Information Noise-Contrastive Estimation) loss: $\mathcal{L} = -\log \frac{\exp(\text{sim}(z_i, z_j^+)/\tau)}{\sum_{k=1}^{K} \exp(\text{sim}(z_i, z_k)/\tau)}$, a contrastive loss that maximizes a lower bound on mutual information $I(X; Y)$. Foundation for: SimCLR, MoCo, CLIP, CPC.

nodes.label: initialization
nodes.definition: Setting the initial values of neural network weights before training. Methods: Xavier/Glorot ($\text{Var} = 2/(n_{\text{in}} + n_{\text{out}})$), He/Kaiming ($\text{Var} = 2/n_{\text{in}}$ for ReLU), orthogonal, zero-init for residual branches (GPT, ControlNet).

nodes.label: instant-ngp
nodes.definition: A method for training neural radiance fields in seconds by replacing the MLP-based positional encoding with a multi-resolution hash table of learnable feature vectors, where 3D positions are mapped to table indices via spatial hashing, and features are trilinearly interpolated and concatenated across resolution levels before passing through a small MLP.

nodes.label: instructpix2pix
nodes.definition: A conditional diffusion model for instruction-based image editing that learns to follow natural language editing instructions (e.g., 'make it sunset') by training on a synthetic dataset of (input image, edit instruction, output image) triples generated using GPT-3 for instruction generation and Stable Diffusion for image pair creation.

nodes.label: internvl
nodes.definition: A family of vision-language foundation models that align a large-scale vision encoder (InternViT, up to 6B parameters) with a large language model through a dynamic high-resolution image processing strategy and progressive training, achieving strong performance on multimodal understanding and generation tasks.

nodes.label: intersection
nodes.definition: The intersection of sets $A$ and $B$ is $A \cap B = \{x : x \in A \text{ and } x \in B\}$, containing elements in both sets. Intersection of convex sets is convex. Foundation for logical AND, common neighbors in graphs, and set operations.

nodes.label: intersection over union
nodes.definition: A measure of overlap between two bounding boxes: $\text{IoU} = \frac{|A \cap B|}{|A \cup B|} = \frac{\text{area of intersection}}{\text{area of union}}$, ranging from 0 (no overlap) to 1 (perfect overlap). Used for matching predictions to ground truth in object detection evaluation.

nodes.label: inverse autoregressive flow
nodes.definition: A normalizing flow where the transformation is $x_i = z_i \cdot \sigma_i(\mathbf{x}_{<i}) + \mu_i(\mathbf{x}_{<i})$, with each output depending on the previously computed outputs (not inputs), making sampling (forward pass) parallelizable in one MADE pass but density evaluation sequential — the reverse speed tradeoff of MAF.

nodes.label: inverse reinforcement learning
nodes.definition: The problem of recovering a reward function from observed expert behavior, under the assumption that the expert is optimizing this reward.

nodes.label: iql
nodes.definition: Implicit Q-Learning: an offline RL algorithm that avoids querying out-of-distribution actions by learning the value function $V(s)$ via expectile regression on $Q(s,a)$: $\mathcal{L}_V = E_{(s,a) \sim D}[L_2^\tau(Q(s,a) - V(s))]$ where $L_2^\tau$ is the asymmetric squared loss, then extracting the policy via advantage-weighted regression.

nodes.label: iqn
nodes.definition: Implicit Quantile Networks: a distributional RL algorithm that learns a continuous quantile function $Z_\tau(s,a) = f_\theta(s, a, \tau)$ for any quantile fraction $\tau \in [0,1]$, using a neural network that takes $\tau$ as an additional input (embedded via random Fourier features), enabling sampling any number of quantiles at runtime.

nodes.label: isomap
nodes.definition: A nonlinear dimensionality reduction method that preserves geodesic (shortest-path) distances on the data manifold: constructs a $k$-NN graph, computes shortest-path distances between all pairs using Dijkstra's algorithm, then applies classical MDS to the geodesic distance matrix.

nodes.label: iteratively reweighted least squares
nodes.definition: An algorithm for fitting GLMs that iteratively solves weighted least squares problems: at each iteration, compute weights $w_i = 1/(V(\mu_i)(g'(\mu_i))^2)$ and working responses $z_i = \eta_i + (y_i - \mu_i)g'(\mu_i)$, then solve the WLS problem. Equivalent to Fisher scoring/Newton-Raphson for GLMs.

nodes.label: jamba
nodes.definition: A hybrid SSM-Transformer architecture from AI21 that interleaves Mamba layers (for efficient long-context processing) with Transformer attention layers (for precise retrieval) and MoE layers (for capacity), achieving strong quality with efficient inference: 256K context with only 12B active parameters out of 52B total.

nodes.label: jepa
nodes.definition: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture: a general self-supervised learning framework where a predictor network predicts the representation of a target view from the representation of a context view in an abstract representation space (not pixel space), avoiding collapse through asymmetric architectures (EMA target encoder, stop-gradient) rather than contrastive objectives.

nodes.label: junction tree algorithm
nodes.definition: An exact inference algorithm for probabilistic graphical models that converts the graph into a junction tree (clique tree) — a tree of maximal cliques satisfying the running intersection property — and performs belief propagation on this tree to compute exact marginal probabilities and the partition function.

nodes.label: k-medoids
nodes.definition: A clustering algorithm similar to $k$-means but uses actual data points (medoids) as cluster centers instead of means, minimizing $\sum_{k=1}^{K} \sum_{\mathbf{x} \in C_k} d(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{m}_k)$ where $\mathbf{m}_k \in C_k$ is the medoid, making it more robust to outliers and applicable with any distance metric.

nodes.label: kernel density estimation
nodes.definition: A non-parametric method for estimating the probability density function of a random variable by placing a kernel function $K$ (e.g., Gaussian) at each data point and averaging: $\hat{f}(x) = \frac{1}{nh} \sum_{i=1}^{n} K\left(\frac{x - x_i}{h}\right)$, where $h$ is the bandwidth controlling smoothness.

nodes.label: kernel logistic regression
nodes.definition: An extension of logistic regression to nonlinear classification via the kernel trick, where the linear predictor is replaced by a kernel expansion: $P(y=1 \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sigma(\sum_i \alpha_i K(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{x}_i) + b)$, trained by maximizing the penalized log-likelihood with a kernel-based regularizer $\boldsymbol{\alpha}^\top \mathbf{K} \boldsymbol{\alpha}$.

nodes.label: keypoint detection
nodes.definition: The task of detecting salient points (corners, junctions, blobs) in images that are repeatable under viewpoint and illumination changes. Methods: Harris, SIFT, SuperPoint, ALIKE.

nodes.label: kl divergence
nodes.definition: The Kullback-Leibler divergence from a distribution $P$ to a distribution $Q$ is $D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\|Q)=\int p(x) \log \frac{p(x)}{q(x)} \, dx$ in the continuous case, with the corresponding sum in the discrete case. It measures information loss when $Q$ is used to approximate $P$, but it is not a metric because it is generally asymmetric and does not satisfy the triangle inequality.

nodes.label: l-bfgs
nodes.definition: Limited-memory Broyden-Fletcher-Goldfarb-Shanno: a quasi-Newton optimization method that approximates the inverse Hessian using the $m$ most recent gradient differences, requiring only $O(md)$ storage (vs. $O(d^2)$ for full BFGS), enabling second-order-like convergence for smooth optimization problems without storing the full Hessian.

nodes.label: label propagation
nodes.definition: Label propagation is a graph-based semi-supervised learning method that spreads labels from labeled nodes to unlabeled nodes according to graph connectivity and similarity weights. It assumes labels vary smoothly over the similarity graph.

nodes.label: lamb
nodes.definition: Layer-wise Adaptive Moments optimizer for Batch training: extends LARS to the Adam optimizer by applying layer-wise trust ratio scaling $\phi(\|\mathbf{w}_l\|) / \|\mathbf{r}_l\|$ to Adam's update $\mathbf{r}_l = m_l / (\sqrt{v_l} + \epsilon) + \lambda \mathbf{w}_l$, enabling large-batch training (up to 64K) for Transformer models like BERT.

nodes.label: lanenet
nodes.definition: A lane detection network that uses a dual-branch architecture: a semantic segmentation branch to classify pixels as lane/non-lane, and an instance embedding branch that maps lane pixels to an embedding space where pixels of the same lane instance cluster together, followed by a clustering step (mean shift) and curve fitting.

nodes.label: language model
nodes.definition: A probabilistic model that assigns probabilities to sequences of tokens: $P(w_1, w_2, \ldots, w_n)$, typically factored autoregressively as $P(w_1, \ldots, w_n) = \prod_{i=1}^{n} P(w_i \mid w_1, \ldots, w_{i-1})$, used for text generation, scoring fluency, and as the foundation for modern LLMs.

nodes.label: laplace smoothing
nodes.definition: A technique for handling zero probabilities in Naive Bayes by adding a small count $\alpha$ to each class-feature combination: $\hat{P}(x_j \mid y) = \frac{n_{jy} + \alpha}{n_y + \alpha |V|}$ where $|V|$ is the vocabulary size. Also called additive smoothing.

nodes.label: latent diffusion model
nodes.definition: A diffusion model that operates in the latent space of a pre-trained autoencoder (VQ-GAN or similar): the encoder compresses images to a lower-dimensional latent representation where the diffusion process is applied, and the decoder maps the denoised latent back to pixel space, dramatically reducing computational cost.

nodes.label: leapfrog integrator
nodes.definition: A symplectic numerical integrator for Hamiltonian dynamics: $\mathbf{p}_{t+\epsilon/2} = \mathbf{p}_t - (\epsilon/2)\nabla U(\mathbf{q}_t)$, $\mathbf{q}_{t+\epsilon} = \mathbf{q}_t + \epsilon \mathbf{M}^{-1}\mathbf{p}_{t+\epsilon/2}$, $\mathbf{p}_{t+\epsilon} = \mathbf{p}_{t+\epsilon/2} - (\epsilon/2)\nabla U(\mathbf{q}_{t+\epsilon})$. Preserves volume and time-reversibility.

nodes.label: learning vector quantization
nodes.definition: A supervised prototype-based classification method that maintains a set of prototype vectors $\{\mathbf{w}_k\}$ with class labels, and updates them by moving correctly classified prototypes toward the input ($\mathbf{w}_k \leftarrow \mathbf{w}_k + \alpha(\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{w}_k)$) and incorrectly classified prototypes away ($\mathbf{w}_k \leftarrow \mathbf{w}_k - \alpha(\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{w}_k)$).

nodes.label: least angle regression
nodes.definition: An iterative regression algorithm that starts with all coefficients at zero and incrementally moves coefficients in the direction equiangular to the most correlated predictors, providing the full regularization path of the Lasso efficiently.

nodes.label: least squares
nodes.definition: An optimization criterion that minimizes the sum of squared residuals: $\min_{\boldsymbol{\beta}} \sum_i (y_i - f(\mathbf{x}_i; \boldsymbol{\beta}))^2$. Linear: closed-form $(\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}^\top\mathbf{y}$. Nonlinear: Gauss-Newton, Levenberg-Marquardt.

nodes.label: least squares svm
nodes.definition: A variant of the standard SVM that replaces the hinge loss with a squared loss and the inequality constraints with equality constraints, leading to a solution via a system of linear equations (rather than a quadratic program): minimize $\frac{1}{2}\|\mathbf{w}\|^2 + \frac{C}{2}\sum_{i=1}^{n} e_i^2$ subject to $y_i(\mathbf{w}^\top \phi(\mathbf{x}_i) + b) = 1 - e_i$.

nodes.label: leveraging bagging
nodes.definition: An enhanced online bagging method that increases ensemble diversity by using higher Poisson weights ($\operatorname{Poisson}(\lambda)$ with $\lambda > 1$, typically $\lambda = 6$) for resampling and adding output detection codes or random output perturbation, combined with ADWIN-based drift detection for individual base learners.

nodes.label: lightgbm
nodes.definition: A gradient boosting framework that uses Gradient-based One-Side Sampling (GOSS: keeping instances with large gradients and randomly sampling those with small gradients) and Exclusive Feature Bundling (EFB: bundling mutually exclusive sparse features) to achieve faster training on large datasets while maintaining accuracy.

nodes.label: likelihood function
nodes.definition: The probability of the observed data viewed as a function of the parameters: $L(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = P(\text{data} \mid \boldsymbol{\theta}) = \prod_i P(x_i \mid \boldsymbol{\theta})$ (for i.i.d. data). Maximized in MLE. The log-likelihood $\ell = \log L$ is more convenient.

nodes.label: linear programming
nodes.definition: Optimization with a linear objective and linear constraints: $\min \mathbf{c}^\top \mathbf{x}$ s.t. $\mathbf{Ax} \leq \mathbf{b}$, $\mathbf{x} \geq 0$. Solved in polynomial time by interior-point methods. Simplex: practical, usually fast. Quantile regression is an LP.

nodes.label: linear regression
nodes.definition: Linear regression models a real-valued response as $y=X\beta+\varepsilon$, where $X$ is a design matrix, $\beta$ is a coefficient vector, and $\varepsilon$ is an error term. Estimation is typically performed by ordinary least squares, which minimizes the residual sum of squares.

nodes.label: linformer
nodes.definition: An efficient Transformer that projects the key and value matrices from $n \times d$ to $k \times d$ using learned projection matrices $\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{F} \in \mathbb{R}^{k \times n}$, computing attention as $\operatorname{softmax}(\mathbf{Q}(\mathbf{E}\mathbf{K})^\top / \sqrt{d}) \mathbf{F}\mathbf{V}$, reducing complexity from $O(n^2)$ to $O(nk)$.

nodes.label: linucb
nodes.definition: A contextual bandit algorithm that assumes linear reward: $E[r \mid \mathbf{x}, a] = \boldsymbol{\theta}_a^\top \mathbf{x}$, maintains a ridge regression estimate $\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_a$ per arm with uncertainty $\mathbf{A}_a^{-1}$, and selects arms by UCB: $a^* = \arg\max_a [\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_a^\top \mathbf{x}_t + \alpha \sqrt{\mathbf{x}_t^\top \mathbf{A}_a^{-1} \mathbf{x}_t}]$.

nodes.label: listnet
nodes.definition: A listwise learning-to-rank method that defines a probability distribution over permutations using the Plackett-Luce model: $P(\pi \mid \mathbf{s}) = \prod_{j=1}^{n} \frac{\exp(s_{\pi(j)})}{\sum_{k=j}^{n} \exp(s_{\pi(k)})}$, and minimizes the cross-entropy between the ground-truth and predicted permutation distributions.

nodes.label: local outlier factor
nodes.definition: A density-based anomaly detection method that computes the Local Outlier Factor as the ratio of a point's local density to its neighbors' local densities: $\text{LOF}_k(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{|N_k(\mathbf{x})|} \sum_{\mathbf{y} \in N_k(\mathbf{x})} \frac{\text{lrd}_k(\mathbf{y})}{\text{lrd}_k(\mathbf{x})}$, where $\text{lrd}$ is the local reachability density.

nodes.label: local regression
nodes.definition: Fitting a regression model within a local neighborhood of each query point. LOESS: weighted polynomial regression with kernel weights. Nadaraya-Watson: weighted average with kernel weights. Local linear: corrects LOESS boundary bias.

nodes.label: log-linear model
nodes.definition: A probabilistic model where the log-probability is a linear function of features: $\log P(\mathbf{y} \mid \mathbf{x}) \propto \boldsymbol{\theta}^\top \boldsymbol{\phi}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y})$. CRFs, MaxEnt models, and exponential family models are log-linear.

nodes.label: logistic-normal distribution
nodes.definition: A distribution on the simplex obtained by applying softmax to a multivariate normal: $\boldsymbol{\eta} \sim N(\boldsymbol{\mu}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma})$, $\theta_k = \exp(\eta_k)/\sum_j \exp(\eta_j)$. Used in the Correlated Topic Model as the prior for topic proportions (instead of Dirichlet), enabling correlated topics.

nodes.label: lora
nodes.definition: Low-Rank Adaptation: a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that adds trainable low-rank decomposition matrices to frozen pre-trained weight matrices: $\mathbf{W}' = \mathbf{W}_0 + \Delta\mathbf{W} = \mathbf{W}_0 + \mathbf{B}\mathbf{A}$ where $\mathbf{B} \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times r}$, $\mathbf{A} \in \mathbb{R}^{r \times k}$ with $r \ll \min(d, k)$, enabling fine-tuning with very few trainable parameters.

nodes.label: lstm
nodes.definition: Long Short-Term Memory: an RNN architecture with a memory cell $\mathbf{c}_t$ and three gates (input $\mathbf{i}_t$, forget $\mathbf{f}_t$, output $\mathbf{o}_t$) that control information flow, enabling learning of long-range dependencies by providing a path for gradients to flow through the cell state with minimal transformation.

nodes.label: mae
nodes.definition: Masked Autoencoder: a self-supervised pre-training method for Vision Transformers that masks 75% of image patches, encodes only visible patches, and reconstructs masked patches in pixel space, achieving strong representations through high-ratio masking.

nodes.label: mahalanobis distance
nodes.definition: A distance measure accounting for correlations between variables: $d_M(\mathbf{x}, \boldsymbol{\mu}) = \sqrt{(\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol{\mu})^\top \boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1} (\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol{\mu})}$, reducing to Euclidean distance when $\boldsymbol{\Sigma} = \mathbf{I}$. Used in: outlier detection (elliptic envelope), Gustafson-Kessel, PaDiM.

nodes.label: majority voting
nodes.definition: An ensemble combination method where the final prediction is the class receiving the most votes from the base classifiers: $\hat{y} = \arg\max_c \sum_t \mathbf{1}[h_t(\mathbf{x}) = c]$. Used in: bagging, random forest, tri-training. Weighted voting: weight by classifier accuracy.

nodes.label: maml
nodes.definition: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning: a meta-learning algorithm that learns an initialization $\boldsymbol{\theta}^*$ of model parameters such that a few gradient steps on a new task's data yield good performance: $\boldsymbol{\theta}^* = \arg\min_\theta \sum_{\mathcal{T}_i} \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{T}_i}(\theta - \alpha \nabla_\theta \mathcal{L}_{\mathcal{T}_i}(\theta))$, requiring second-order gradients (gradients through the…

nodes.label: manifold learning
nodes.definition: Methods that discover low-dimensional structure (manifold) underlying high-dimensional data: Isomap (geodesic distances), LLE (local linear), Laplacian Eigenmaps (graph Laplacian), t-SNE, UMAP, diffusion maps.

nodes.label: mappo
nodes.definition: Multi-Agent PPO: applies PPO to multi-agent settings with parameter sharing and centralized value function, demonstrating that well-tuned vanilla PPO is competitive with specialized multi-agent methods.

nodes.label: margin loss
nodes.definition: A loss function that enforces a margin between classes or between positive/negative pairs: hinge loss ($\max(0, 1-y\hat{y})$), triplet loss ($\max(0, d_+ - d_- + \alpha)$), contrastive loss with margin $m$.

nodes.label: markov chain
nodes.definition: A stochastic process $\{X_t\}$ satisfying the Markov property: the conditional distribution of the future state depends only on the present state, not the past: $P(X_{t+1} \mid X_t, X_{t-1}, \ldots) = P(X_{t+1} \mid X_t)$, characterized by a transition matrix $\mathbf{P}$ where $P_{ij} = P(X_{t+1} = j \mid X_t = i)$.

nodes.label: markov random field
nodes.definition: An undirected graphical model where the joint distribution factorizes as a product of potential functions over cliques: $P(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{Z} \prod_c \psi_c(\mathbf{x}_c)$. Encodes conditional independence via graph separation (global, local, pairwise Markov properties).

nodes.label: masked autoencoder vit
nodes.definition: A self-supervised pre-training method for Vision Transformers that masks a large fraction (75%) of random image patches, encodes only the visible patches with a ViT encoder, and reconstructs the masked patches in pixel space using a lightweight decoder, achieving strong representations through the reconstruction pretext task.

nodes.label: masked image modeling
nodes.definition: A self-supervised pre-training approach for vision models that masks portions of the input image and trains the model to predict the masked content: pixel reconstruction (MAE), token prediction (BEiT), or representation prediction (I-JEPA).

nodes.label: maskgit
nodes.definition: A masked image modeling approach for image generation that represents images as discrete tokens (via VQ-GAN) and generates them by iteratively predicting masked tokens in parallel, starting from a fully masked sequence and progressively unmasking tokens based on prediction confidence across multiple decoding iterations.

nodes.label: matrix multiplication
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: Matrix multiplication is the bilinear operation defined by $(AB)_{ij}=\sum_k A_{ik}B_{kj}$ whenever the inner dimensions match. It represents composition of linear maps and is one of the fundamental operations in linear algebra and machine learning.

nodes.label: maximum entropy irl
nodes.definition: An IRL method that models the expert's stochastic policy as a Boltzmann distribution over trajectories: $P(\tau) \propto \exp(R(\tau))$, resolving IRL ambiguity by choosing the maximum entropy distribution matching observed feature statistics.

nodes.label: maximum entropy principle
nodes.definition: Choose the probability distribution that maximizes entropy subject to known constraints (expected values of certain quantities): $\max_p H(p)$ s.t. $E_p[f_k(x)] = F_k$. The result is an exponential family distribution. Used in: MaxEnt IRL, SAC, information theory.

nodes.label: maximum likelihood estimation
nodes.definition: Maximum likelihood estimation chooses parameter values $\hat	heta$ that maximize the likelihood $L(	heta;x)=p(x \mid 	heta)$ of the observed data under a model. Equivalently, it minimizes the negative log-likelihood.

nodes.label: mc dropout
nodes.definition: A simple approximate Bayesian inference method that uses dropout at test time (not just training) as a form of variational inference: multiple forward passes with different dropout masks produce a distribution of predictions, with the mean as the prediction and variance as the uncertainty estimate.

nodes.label: mean
nodes.definition: The arithmetic mean (average) of a set of values: $\bar{x} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i$. For a random variable, the expected value $E[X] = \int x \, dP(x)$. The most common measure of central tendency.

nodes.label: mean shift
nodes.definition: Mean shift is a nonparametric mode-seeking algorithm that iteratively moves points toward local maxima of a kernel density estimate. It can be used both for clustering and for locating density modes.

nodes.label: mean squared error
nodes.definition: A loss function measuring the average squared difference between predictions and targets: $\text{MSE} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^{n}(y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2$, the most common regression loss. Minimizing MSE is equivalent to maximum likelihood under Gaussian noise.

nodes.label: mean teacher
nodes.definition: A semi-supervised learning method that maintains a student model and a teacher model (an exponential moving average of student weights: $\theta_t' = \alpha \theta_{t-1}' + (1-\alpha) \theta_t$), enforcing consistency between their predictions on unlabeled data under different augmentations.

nodes.label: mean-field variational inference
nodes.definition: An approximate Bayesian inference method that approximates the posterior $p(\boldsymbol{\theta} \mid \mathbf{y})$ with a factored distribution $q(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = \prod_{i} q_i(\theta_i)$ by minimizing $\operatorname{KL}(q \| p)$, yielding the coordinate ascent updates $q_j^*(\theta_j) \propto \exp(E_{q_{-j}}[\log p(\boldsymbol{\theta}, \mathbf{y})])$.

nodes.label: mel spectrogram
nodes.definition: A time-frequency representation of audio obtained by applying the Short-Time Fourier Transform (STFT) and mapping frequencies to the mel scale (perceptually uniform): $m = 2595 \log_{10}(1 + f/700)$. Log-mel spectrograms are standard input for speech/audio models.

nodes.label: memory network
nodes.definition: A neural architecture consisting of a memory array $\mathbf{M}$ of stored vectors, an input encoder, and attention-based read operations that query the memory with the input to retrieve relevant information for reasoning and prediction, enabling the network to access a large external knowledge store beyond its parameters.

nodes.label: message passing neural network
nodes.definition: A general framework for graph neural networks where each layer updates node representations by: (1) computing messages from neighbors $\mathbf{m}_{v \to u} = M_t(\mathbf{h}_v, \mathbf{h}_u, \mathbf{e}_{vu})$, (2) aggregating messages $\mathbf{m}_u = \bigoplus_{v \in \mathcal{N}(u)} \mathbf{m}_{v \to u}$, and (3) updating node state $\mathbf{h}_u' = U_t(\mathbf{h}_u, \mathbf{m}_u)$.

nodes.label: mind
nodes.definition: Multi-Interest Network with Dynamic Routing: a recommendation model that uses dynamic routing (inspired by capsule networks) to extract multiple interest vectors from a user's behavior sequence, where each interest vector captures a distinct aspect of user preferences, rather than compressing all interests into a single vector.

nodes.label: mini-batch
nodes.definition: A random subset of the training data used to compute an approximate gradient in stochastic gradient descent. The mini-batch size $B$ trades off between gradient accuracy ($B$ large → more accurate, slower) and stochastic noise ($B$ small → noisier, faster, better generalization).

nodes.label: minimum cut
nodes.definition: The minimum total weight of edges whose removal disconnects the graph into two components. Related to maximum flow (max-flow min-cut theorem). Normalized cut: balances partition sizes. Used in: graph partitioning, spectral clustering, image segmentation.

nodes.label: minimum spanning tree
nodes.definition: A spanning tree of a weighted graph with the minimum total edge weight: connects all vertices with minimum cost without cycles. Algorithms: Kruskal ($O(E \log E)$), Prim ($O(E + V \log V)$). Used in HDBSCAN, graph-based clustering.

nodes.label: mixtral
nodes.definition: A Mixture-of-Experts LLM based on Mistral that replaces each Transformer's FFN with a sparse MoE layer containing 8 expert FFNs, routing each token to the top-2 experts via a learned gate, achieving much higher capacity (46.7B total, 12.9B active) while maintaining fast inference.

nodes.label: mixture of depths
nodes.definition: A Transformer architecture that dynamically allocates computation by routing each token to either pass through a full Transformer block or skip it via a residual connection, using a learned router to select the top-$k$ tokens per layer that receive full computation, reducing FLOPs while maintaining quality.

nodes.label: mixture of factor analyzers
nodes.definition: A probabilistic generative model that combines mixture models with factor analysis, where each mixture component $k$ models the data as $\mathbf{x} = \boldsymbol{\mu}_k + \mathbf{\Lambda}_k \mathbf{z} + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_k$ with latent factors $\mathbf{z} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I})$ and $\boldsymbol{\epsilon}_k \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{\Psi}_k)$, yielding a cluster-specific low-rank-plus-diagonal covariance…

nodes.label: mobile architecture
nodes.definition: Neural network architectures designed for efficient inference on mobile/edge devices with limited compute, memory, and power. Key designs: depthwise separable conv (MobileNet), channel shuffle (ShuffleNet), squeeze-excitation, inverted bottleneck.

nodes.label: mode
nodes.definition: The most frequently occurring value (discrete) or the peak of a density function (continuous). In KDE/mean shift: modes are local maxima of the density. In GMM: each component has a mode at $\mu_k$. Mode-seeking: minimizing $\text{KL}(q\|p)$ concentrates $q$ on modes of $p$.

nodes.label: model selection
nodes.definition: Choosing among candidate models (or hyperparameter settings) based on estimated generalization performance. Criteria: cross-validation, AIC, BIC, validation loss, marginal likelihood (Bayesian). Automated: NAS, AutoML.

nodes.label: modern hopfield network
nodes.definition: An extension of classical Hopfield networks that uses an energy function with exponential (or polynomial) interaction terms $E = -\log \sum_{\mu=1}^{P} \exp(\boldsymbol{\xi}^\mu \cdot \mathbf{s})$, dramatically increasing storage capacity to exponential $P \sim \exp(d)$ in pattern dimension $d$ and yielding an update rule equivalent to the attention mechanism in Transformers.

nodes.label: monte carlo method
nodes.definition: A class of computational algorithms that use random sampling to estimate quantities that are difficult to compute deterministically. Examples: MC integration ($\hat{I} = \frac{1}{N}\sum f(x_i)$), MCMC (sample from distributions), MC tree search.

nodes.label: moving average model
nodes.definition: A time series model where the value at time $t$ is a linear combination of current and past white noise terms: $X_t = \mu + \epsilon_t + \sum_{i=1}^{q} \theta_i \epsilon_{t-i}$, denoted MA($q$).

nodes.label: mt5
nodes.definition: Multilingual T5: an extension of T5 pre-trained on the mC4 corpus covering 101 languages, using the same text-to-text framework and span corruption objective but with a multilingual vocabulary (SentencePiece with 250K tokens) and no language identification, enabling zero-shot cross-lingual transfer.

nodes.label: multi-query attention
nodes.definition: An efficient attention variant where all query heads share a single set of keys and values: instead of separate $\mathbf{K}_h, \mathbf{V}_h$ per head, use one $\mathbf{K}, \mathbf{V}$ across all $H$ heads, reducing the KV cache size by a factor of $H$ and significantly speeding up autoregressive inference.

nodes.label: multilingual model
nodes.definition: A single model trained on data from multiple languages, learning shared representations that enable cross-lingual transfer. Examples: mBERT, XLM-R, mT5, Qwen (Chinese+English).

nodes.label: multinomial naive bayes
nodes.definition: A Naive Bayes classifier for count/frequency data (e.g., word counts in text) that models features as multinomial distributed: $P(\mathbf{x} \mid y=c) \propto \prod_j \theta_{jc}^{x_j}$, with parameters $\theta_{jc}$ estimated by $\hat{\theta}_{jc} = (n_{jc} + \alpha) / (n_c + \alpha|V|)$ using Laplace smoothing.

nodes.label: multivariate normal distribution
nodes.definition: The $d$-dimensional Gaussian: $N(\boldsymbol{\mu}, \boldsymbol{\Sigma})$ with PDF $f(\mathbf{x}) = \frac{1}{(2\pi)^{d/2}|\boldsymbol{\Sigma}|^{1/2}} \exp(-\frac{1}{2}(\mathbf{x}-\boldsymbol{\mu})^\top \boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1}(\mathbf{x}-\boldsymbol{\mu}))$. Fully specified by mean $\boldsymbol{\mu}$ and covariance $\boldsymbol{\Sigma}$.

nodes.label: multivariate time series
nodes.definition: A multivariate time series is a sequence of vector-valued random variables $(X_t)_{t \in T}$, typically with $X_t \in \mathbb{R}^d$, observed over ordered times. It models multiple interdependent temporal signals jointly rather than one scalar series at a time.

nodes.label: muon
nodes.definition: An optimizer that applies Newton's method in the spectral domain of weight matrices: for each weight matrix, compute the SVD of the gradient (or use a running estimate), and update using the matrix sign function of the gradient (setting all singular values to 1 while preserving singular vectors), providing a scale-free update direction.

nodes.label: mutual information
nodes.definition: A measure of the statistical dependence between two random variables: $I(X; Y) = D_{\text{KL}}(P_{XY} \| P_X P_Y) = H(X) - H(X \mid Y) = H(Y) - H(Y \mid X)$. $I = 0$ iff independent. Used in: InfoNCE, CPC, DIAYN, feature selection.

nodes.label: muzero
nodes.definition: A model-based RL system that learns a dynamics model, reward model, and value/policy predictions entirely in latent space (without modeling observations), using MCTS to plan with the learned model: the representation function encodes observations, the dynamics function predicts latent transitions, and the prediction function outputs policy and value.

nodes.label: n-hits
nodes.definition: Neural Hierarchical Interpolation for Time Series (N-HiTS) extends N-BEATS by adding multi-rate input sampling (downsampling the lookback window at different rates per stack) and hierarchical interpolation (predicting at a lower temporal resolution and upsampling to the forecast horizon), enabling efficient long-horizon forecasting.

nodes.label: nadaraya-watson estimator
nodes.definition: A nonparametric kernel regression estimator that estimates the conditional expectation $\hat{m}(x) = \frac{\sum_i K_h(x - x_i) y_i}{\sum_i K_h(x - x_i)}$, computing a locally weighted average of the response values with weights given by a kernel function $K_h$ centered at the query point.

nodes.label: naive bayes classifier
nodes.definition: A probabilistic classifier based on Bayes' theorem with the assumption of conditional independence between features given the class: $P(y \mid \mathbf{x}) \propto P(y) \prod_j P(x_j \mid y)$. Despite the naive assumption, performs well in practice, especially for text classification.

nodes.label: named entity recognition
nodes.definition: An NLP task identifying and classifying named entities (person, organization, location, date, etc.) in text. Methods: CRF, BiLSTM-CRF, BERT fine-tuning. Sequence labeling with BIO/BIOES tagging scheme.

nodes.label: natural language processing
nodes.definition: The field of AI/ML dealing with understanding and generating human language. Tasks: classification, NER, QA, translation, summarization, generation. Methods: statistical → neural → Transformer → LLMs.

nodes.label: nearest centroid
nodes.definition: A simple classification method that assigns each new point to the class whose centroid (mean of training points) is nearest: $\hat{y} = \arg\min_c \|\mathbf{x} - \boldsymbol{\mu}_c\|$, equivalent to a linear classifier when using Euclidean distance.

nodes.label: nearest neighbor search
nodes.definition: Finding the closest point(s) to a query from a database: $\text{NN}(\mathbf{q}) = \arg\min_{\mathbf{x} \in D} d(\mathbf{q}, \mathbf{x})$. Exact: KD-tree, ball tree. Approximate: LSH, HNSW, FAISS. $O(n)$ exact, sublinear approximate.

nodes.label: negative binomial regression
nodes.definition: A generalized linear model for overdispersed count data where the response follows a negative binomial distribution with $\log E[Y \mid \mathbf{x}] = \mathbf{x}^\top \boldsymbol{\beta}$ and an additional dispersion parameter $\alpha$ such that $\operatorname{Var}(Y) = \mu + \alpha \mu^2$.

nodes.label: nequip
nodes.definition: Neural Equivariant Interatomic Potentials: a GNN for molecular simulations that uses E(3)-equivariant convolutions with learnable spherical tensor features, maintaining equivariance under rotations, reflections, and translations, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy for molecular dynamics force fields with data efficiency orders of magnitude better than invariant models.

nodes.label: neural collaborative filtering
nodes.definition: A framework that replaces the inner product in matrix factorization with a neural network: $\hat{y}_{ui} = f(\mathbf{p}_u, \mathbf{q}_i; \boldsymbol{\Theta})$ where $f$ is an MLP operating on concatenated user and item embeddings, learning nonlinear user-item interactions.

nodes.label: neural decision forest
nodes.definition: An ensemble of soft (differentiable) decision trees where each tree's internal nodes learn routing functions and each tree's leaf nodes store learned class distributions, all trained jointly end-to-end as a neural network layer, often placed on top of a CNN feature extractor for image classification.

nodes.label: neural network
nodes.definition: A neural network is a parameterized function built as a composition of linear or affine transformations with nonlinear activations. It is a flexible function approximator trained from data by gradient-based optimization.

nodes.label: neural statistician
nodes.definition: A meta-learning model that learns to compute summary statistics of datasets by encoding each dataset as a fixed-dimensional embedding using a permutation-invariant set encoder, trained in a VAE framework to generate datasets from the statistics, enabling few-shot generalization.

nodes.label: neural thompson sampling
nodes.definition: A contextual bandit algorithm that uses a neural network for reward prediction and performs Thompson sampling by maintaining a posterior approximation over the network's last-layer weights (or using the neural tangent kernel approximation), sampling reward functions from this posterior to balance exploration and exploitation.

nodes.label: neural turing machine
nodes.definition: A differentiable computing architecture that couples a neural network controller with an external memory matrix $\mathbf{M} \in \mathbb{R}^{N \times W}$, using content-based and location-based addressing mechanisms to read from and write to memory via soft attention weights, enabling the network to learn algorithmic procedures.

nodes.label: neuralucb
nodes.definition: A contextual bandit algorithm that uses a neural network to estimate reward functions and constructs UCB-style confidence bounds using the neural tangent kernel (NTK) theory: $\text{UCB}_t(a) = f_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t, a) + \alpha \sqrt{\mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x}_t, a)^\top \mathbf{Z}_t^{-1} \mathbf{g}(\mathbf{x}_t, a)}$, where $\mathbf{g}$ is the gradient of the network output.

nodes.label: neuroevolution
nodes.definition: The application of evolutionary algorithms to optimize neural network architectures, weights, or learning rules, including evolving network topologies (NEAT: NeuroEvolution of Augmenting Topologies), weights (evolution strategies), or both, as an alternative to gradient-based training.

nodes.label: newton method
nodes.definition: A second-order optimization method that iterates $\mathbf{x}_{t+1} = \mathbf{x}_t - \mathbf{H}^{-1} \nabla f(\mathbf{x}_t)$, using the Hessian to find the step that minimizes the quadratic approximation. Converges quadratically near the optimum but requires $O(n^3)$ for Hessian inversion.

nodes.label: neyman orthogonality
nodes.definition: A property of the moment condition used in DML: the influence of first-stage nuisance estimation error on the causal parameter estimate is zero to first order, ensuring $\sqrt{n}$-consistency even when nuisance functions converge slowly.

nodes.label: ngboost
nodes.definition: Natural Gradient Boosting: a probabilistic gradient boosting algorithm that predicts full probability distributions (not just point predictions) by fitting the parameters of a parametric distribution (e.g., Normal, LogNormal) using natural gradient descent within the boosting framework, enabling calibrated uncertainty estimates.

nodes.label: no-u-turn sampler
nodes.definition: An adaptive extension of Hamiltonian Monte Carlo that automatically determines the trajectory length $L$ by building a binary tree of leapfrog steps in both forward and backward directions, stopping when the trajectory would "turn back" (the U-turn criterion: $(\boldsymbol{\theta}^+ - \boldsymbol{\theta}^-) \cdot \mathbf{p}^- < 0$ or $(\boldsymbol{\theta}^+ - \boldsymbol{\theta}^-) \cdot \mathbf{p}^+ < 0$), eliminati…

nodes.label: node labeling
nodes.definition: Assigning structural labels to nodes in a graph for GNN processing. In SEAL: Double-Radius Node Labeling (DRNL) labels each node based on its distances to the target link's endpoints, encoding structural context.

nodes.label: node2vec
nodes.definition: A graph embedding method that extends DeepWalk with biased random walks controlled by parameters $p$ (return parameter: likelihood of revisiting the previous node) and $q$ (in-out parameter: bias toward BFS-like vs. DFS-like exploration), enabling the embeddings to capture both local (community) and global (structural role) graph properties.

nodes.label: noise-contrastive estimation
nodes.definition: A method for estimating parameters of unnormalized probabilistic models by training a binary classifier to distinguish between data samples and samples from a known noise distribution $p_n$, with the log-partition function $\log Z$ treated as a learnable parameter, yielding $\hat{\theta} = \arg\max_\theta \sum_i [\log h(\mathbf{x}_i; \theta) + k \cdot \log(1-h(\mathbf{y}_i; \theta))]$ where $h$ is the logistic functi…

nodes.label: noisy network
nodes.definition: A neural network where weights include learnable noise: $\mathbf{w} = \boldsymbol{\mu} + \boldsymbol{\sigma} \odot \boldsymbol{\epsilon}$ (factored Gaussian noise). Replaces $\epsilon$-greedy exploration in Rainbow DQN. The network learns when to explore.

nodes.label: non-maximum suppression
nodes.definition: Non-maximum suppression is a post-processing algorithm that removes redundant overlapping detections by keeping high-scoring candidates and suppressing nearby lower-scoring ones according to an overlap threshold, usually based on intersection over union.

nodes.label: normal distribution
nodes.definition: The normal distribution is the one-dimensional Gaussian distribution with density $f(x)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi\sigma^2}}\exp\!\bigl(-\frac{(x-\mu)^2}{2\sigma^2}\bigr)$ for mean $\mu$ and variance $\sigma^2>0$. It is the canonical bell-shaped distribution in classical statistics.

nodes.label: normalizing flow
nodes.definition: A generative model that transforms a simple base distribution $\mathbf{z} \sim p_0(\mathbf{z})$ (e.g., standard Gaussian) into a complex target distribution via a composition of invertible, differentiable mappings $\mathbf{x} = f_K \circ \cdots \circ f_1(\mathbf{z})$, with the density computed using the change of variables formula: $p(\mathbf{x}) = p_0(\mathbf{z}) \prod_{k=1}^{K} |\det J_{f_k}^{-1}|$.

nodes.label: nystrom method
nodes.definition: A method for approximating a large kernel matrix $\mathbf{K} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times n}$ using a subset of $m$ landmark points: $\tilde{\mathbf{K}} = \mathbf{K}_{nm}\mathbf{K}_{mm}^{-1}\mathbf{K}_{mn}$, reducing eigendecomposition from $O(n^3)$ to $O(nm^2)$. Used in Nystromformer for attention approximation.

nodes.label: nyströmformer
nodes.definition: An efficient Transformer that approximates the softmax attention matrix using the Nyström method: selecting $m$ landmark tokens, computing $\tilde{\mathbf{F}} = \operatorname{softmax}(\mathbf{Q} \tilde{\mathbf{K}}^\top) (\operatorname{softmax}(\tilde{\mathbf{Q}} \tilde{\mathbf{K}}^\top))^{\dagger} \operatorname{softmax}(\tilde{\mathbf{Q}} \mathbf{K}^\top)$ as a low-rank approximation, reducing complexity to $O(n m)$.

nodes.label: object detection
nodes.definition: Object detection is the task of locating and classifying object instances in an image or video, typically by predicting bounding boxes and class labels. It combines recognition with geometric localization.

nodes.label: offline reinforcement learning
nodes.definition: A paradigm where the agent learns entirely from a fixed dataset without further environment interaction, addressing distributional shift between the learned and data collection policies.

nodes.label: online bagging
nodes.definition: An online version of the bagging ensemble method where, instead of drawing bootstrap samples, each incoming training example is processed with a Poisson(1)-distributed weight for each base learner: for each base model $h_m$, draw $k \sim \operatorname{Poisson}(1)$ and update $h_m$ with the example $k$ times.

nodes.label: online boosting
nodes.definition: An online adaptation of the AdaBoost algorithm where each incoming example is processed sequentially through all base learners, with each learner receiving a weight proportional to the errors of preceding learners, and base learner weights are updated based on their cumulative weighted error rates.

nodes.label: optical character recognition
nodes.definition: Recognizing text in images: detecting and reading printed or handwritten text. Modern: end-to-end deep learning (CRNN + CTC, TrOCR). Scene text: irregular text in natural images. Document: structured layout (tables, forms).

nodes.label: optics
nodes.definition: Ordering Points To Identify the Clustering Structure: a density-based algorithm that produces a reachability plot (ordered list of reachability distances) from which clusters at any density level can be extracted, generalizing DBSCAN to handle varying-density clusters by creating an augmented ordering of the dataset.

nodes.label: ordinary least squares
nodes.definition: The fundamental linear regression method that estimates coefficients $\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}} = (\mathbf{X}^\top \mathbf{X})^{-1} \mathbf{X}^\top \mathbf{y}$ by minimizing the sum of squared residuals $\sum_{i=1}^{n} (y_i - \mathbf{x}_i^\top \boldsymbol{\beta})^2$, equivalent to the maximum likelihood estimator under Gaussian errors.

nodes.label: orthogonal matrix
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: A square matrix $\mathbf{Q}$ satisfying $\mathbf{Q}^\top \mathbf{Q} = \mathbf{Q}\mathbf{Q}^\top = \mathbf{I}$ (equivalently: columns are orthonormal). Preserves lengths and angles. $\det(\mathbf{Q}) = \pm 1$. $\det = +1$: rotation. $\det = -1$: rotation + reflection.

nodes.label: outer product
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: The tensor product of two vectors producing a matrix: $\mathbf{u} \otimes \mathbf{v} = \mathbf{u}\mathbf{v}^\top$ where $(\mathbf{u}\mathbf{v}^\top)_{ij} = u_i v_j$. Rank-1 matrix. Used in: PNN (product-based interaction), attention (QK^T), SGD weight update ($\Delta W = \eta \mathbf{g} \mathbf{a}^\top$).

nodes.label: pairwise ranking
nodes.definition: Learning to rank by comparing pairs: given $(a, b)$ with $a \succ b$, learn $s(a) > s(b)$. Losses: BPR ($\log \sigma(s_a - s_b)$), RankNet ($\text{CE}(\sigma(s_a - s_b), 1)$). More natural for implicit feedback than pointwise methods.

nodes.label: parallel trends
nodes.definition: Parallel trends is the identifying assumption in difference-in-differences that, absent treatment, treated and control groups would have had the same average outcome trend over time. It justifies attributing post-treatment trend differences to the treatment rather than to preexisting drift.

nodes.label: parti
nodes.definition: Pathways Autoregressive Text-to-Image: a text-to-image model that uses an encoder-decoder Transformer to autoregressively generate image tokens from a VQ-GAN codebook, conditioned on text tokens from a SentencePiece tokenizer, treating image generation as a sequence-to-sequence problem and scaling to 20B parameters.

nodes.label: patch embedding
nodes.definition: In Vision Transformers: splitting an image into non-overlapping patches ($P \times P$, typically $16 \times 16$) and linearly projecting each patch to a $d$-dimensional token embedding: $\mathbf{z}_i = \mathbf{W} \text{flatten}(\text{patch}_i) + \mathbf{e}_{\text{pos},i}$.

nodes.label: patching
nodes.definition: In PatchTST: dividing a time series lookback window into non-overlapping segments (patches) of length $P$ and treating each as a token for Transformer processing. Reduces the number of tokens by factor $P$ and captures local temporal patterns.

nodes.label: patchtst
nodes.definition: A Transformer for time series forecasting that divides the lookback window into patches (subsequences), treats each patch as a token, and applies a standard Transformer encoder to the patch tokens independently per channel (channel independence), enabling efficient long-range temporal modeling.

nodes.label: perceptual loss
nodes.definition: A loss function that measures the difference between images in a learned feature space (typically VGG features) rather than pixel space: $\mathcal{L}_{\text{perc}} = \sum_l \|\phi_l(\mathbf{x}) - \phi_l(\hat{\mathbf{x}})\|^2$ where $\phi_l$ are intermediate CNN feature maps, producing results that are perceptually more similar to human judgment.

nodes.label: phi
nodes.definition: A family of small language models (1.3B-14B parameters) from Microsoft that achieve quality comparable to much larger models through high-quality training data: using curated textbook-quality synthetic data and filtered web data, demonstrating that data quality can compensate for model size.

nodes.label: phydnet
nodes.definition: A physics-informed video prediction network that disentangles physical dynamics from residual information: a PhyCell branch models known physical laws via partial differential equations (PDE constraints) while a ConvLSTM branch captures complementary visual details not explained by the physics, combining both for prediction.

nodes.label: point transformer
nodes.definition: A Transformer-based architecture for 3D point cloud processing that applies self-attention to local point neighborhoods with vector attention: $\mathbf{y}_i = \sum_{j \in \mathcal{N}(i)} \rho(\gamma(\phi(\mathbf{x}_i) - \psi(\mathbf{x}_j) + \delta)) \odot (\alpha(\mathbf{x}_j) + \delta)$, where $\delta$ is a positional encoding and $\rho$ is softmax normalization.

nodes.label: poisson distribution
nodes.definition: The Poisson distribution is a discrete distribution on $\mathbb{N}$ with mass function $P(X=k)=e^{-\lambda}\lambda^k/k!$ for rate $\lambda>0$. It models counts of events occurring independently over a fixed interval at constant average rate.

nodes.label: policy smoothing
nodes.definition: In TD3: adding noise to the target policy's actions for regularization: $a' = \mu_{\theta'}(s') + \text{clip}(\epsilon, -c, c)$ where $\epsilon \sim N(0, \sigma^2)$. Prevents the critic from exploiting sharp peaks in the Q-function.

nodes.label: poly-encoder
nodes.definition: A Transformer-based architecture for retrieval that uses $m$ learnable global attention codes to extract $m$ context vectors from the candidate encoding, then attends over these $m$ codes using the label encoding, providing a richer interaction than bi-encoders (dot product) while being more efficient than cross-encoders (full cross-attention).

nodes.label: polyak averaging
nodes.definition: A technique that maintains an exponential (or uniform) moving average of the model parameters during training: $\bar{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_t = \alpha \bar{\boldsymbol{\theta}}_{t-1} + (1-\alpha) \boldsymbol{\theta}_t$, using the averaged parameters for evaluation, which typically achieves better generalization than the last iterate due to averaging out noise.

nodes.label: polynomial
nodes.definition: An expression of the form $p(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{n} a_k x^k = a_0 + a_1 x + \cdots + a_n x^n$, where $a_k$ are coefficients and $n$ is the degree. Polynomials form a vector space and are the simplest class of smooth functions.

nodes.label: power series
nodes.definition: An infinite series of the form $\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} a_n (x-c)^n$, representing a function as a polynomial with infinitely many terms. Taylor series: $f(x) = \sum \frac{f^{(n)}(c)}{n!}(x-c)^n$. Converges within its radius of convergence $R$.

nodes.label: ppo
nodes.definition: Proximal Policy Optimization: a policy gradient method that approximates TRPO's trust region constraint with a simpler clipped surrogate objective: $\mathcal{L}^{\text{CLIP}} = E[\min(r_t(\theta) \hat{A}_t, \text{clip}(r_t(\theta), 1-\epsilon, 1+\epsilon) \hat{A}_t)]$ where $r_t = \pi_\theta(a_t|s_t)/\pi_{\theta_{\text{old}}}(a_t|s_t)$, preventing excessively large policy updates.

nodes.label: precision matrix
nodes.definition: The inverse of the covariance matrix: $\boldsymbol{\Theta} = \boldsymbol{\Sigma}^{-1}$. Zeros in $\boldsymbol{\Theta}$ encode conditional independencies: $\Theta_{ij} = 0 \iff X_i \perp X_j \mid \mathbf{X}_{-(i,j)}$. Estimated by the Graphical Lasso.

nodes.label: preference learning
nodes.definition: Learning from pairwise human preferences ($y_w \succ y_l$) rather than absolute scores, training a reward model or directly optimizing the policy to match human preferences. Bradley-Terry model: $P(y_w \succ y_l) = \sigma(r(y_w) - r(y_l))$.

nodes.label: prefix language model
nodes.definition: A language modeling objective that combines a bidirectional prefix (where tokens can attend to all other prefix tokens) with a causal continuation (where subsequent tokens attend only to the prefix and preceding continuation tokens), used in models like UniLM and PrefixLM for unified understanding and generation.

nodes.label: prefix tree
nodes.definition: A tree data structure (trie) where nodes represent characters and paths represent strings. Efficient for: prefix matching, autocomplete, string lookup. In BPE: merge pairs represented in a vocabulary trie.

nodes.label: prefix tuning
nodes.definition: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that prepends trainable continuous vectors (prefix tokens) to the keys and values of each Transformer attention layer: the prefix $P_\theta \in \mathbb{R}^{|P| \times d}$ is optimized while all other parameters remain frozen, effectively steering the model's behavior through attention conditioning.

nodes.label: principal component analysis
nodes.definition: Principal component analysis finds orthogonal directions of maximal variance in data and projects observations onto those directions for dimensionality reduction. For centered data, the principal directions are the eigenvectors of the covariance matrix or, equivalently, the right singular vectors of the data matrix.

nodes.label: prioritized experience replay
nodes.definition: An experience replay variant that samples transitions with probability proportional to their TD error: $P(i) \propto |\delta_i|^\alpha$ (or rank-based: $P(i) \propto 1/\text{rank}(i)^\alpha$), focusing learning on surprising or informative transitions, with importance sampling weights to correct the bias.

nodes.label: probabilistic forecasting
nodes.definition: Forecasting that produces a probability distribution (or quantiles/prediction intervals) over future values, rather than a single point prediction. DeepAR: parametric distribution (Gaussian, NB). Conformal: non-parametric intervals. NGBoost: distributional boosting.

nodes.label: probabilistic latent semantic analysis
nodes.definition: A generative model for co-occurrence data where each word in a document is generated by first selecting a latent topic $z$ with document-specific probability $P(z \mid d)$ and then selecting the word with topic-specific probability $P(w \mid z)$, yielding $P(w \mid d) = \sum_{z=1}^{K} P(w \mid z) P(z \mid d)$.

nodes.label: probabilistic pca
nodes.definition: A latent variable model that formulates PCA probabilistically as $\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{W}\mathbf{z} + \boldsymbol{\mu} + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}$, where $\mathbf{z} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I}_q)$ and $\boldsymbol{\epsilon} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \sigma^2 \mathbf{I}_d)$, with the maximum likelihood solution for $\mathbf{W}$ recovering the principal component subspace as $\sigma^2 \to 0$.

nodes.label: product-limit estimator
nodes.definition: Synonym for Kaplan-Meier estimator: $\hat{S}(t) = \prod_{t_i \leq t} (1 - d_i/n_i)$. The product of conditional survival probabilities across observed event times.

nodes.label: proximal operator
nodes.definition: The proximal operator of a function $g$ with step size $\lambda$ maps a point $\mathbf{x}$ to the minimizer of $g$ plus a quadratic penalty: $\text{prox}_{\lambda g}(\mathbf{x}) = \arg\min_\mathbf{u} \left(g(\mathbf{u}) + \frac{1}{2\lambda}\|\mathbf{u} - \mathbf{x}\|^2\right)$, generalizing projection onto convex sets and enabling optimization of non-smooth functions.

nodes.label: pruning
nodes.definition: In decision trees: removing branches that do not improve generalization, reducing overfitting. Pre-pruning: stop growing early (min samples, max depth). Post-pruning: grow full tree, then remove branches (cost-complexity pruning, reduced error pruning).

nodes.label: qr-dqn
nodes.definition: Quantile Regression DQN: a distributional RL algorithm that represents the return distribution using $N$ quantile values $\theta_i(s,a)$ at fixed quantile fractions $\tau_i = (2i-1)/(2N)$ for $i = 1, \ldots, N$, trained by minimizing the quantile regression (Huber) loss between predicted and target quantile values.

nodes.label: quadratic programming
nodes.definition: An optimization problem with a quadratic objective and linear constraints: $\min \frac{1}{2} \mathbf{x}^\top \mathbf{Q} \mathbf{x} + \mathbf{c}^\top \mathbf{x}$ subject to $\mathbf{A}\mathbf{x} \leq \mathbf{b}$, $\mathbf{A}_{eq}\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}_{eq}$. Convex if $\mathbf{Q} \succeq 0$ (positive semidefinite).

nodes.label: quate
nodes.definition: A knowledge graph embedding model that represents entities and relations as quaternions (hypercomplex numbers $q = a + bi + cj + dk$) and models relation as rotation in quaternion space: $\mathbf{t} = \mathbf{r} \otimes \mathbf{h} \otimes \bar{\mathbf{r}}$ (Hamilton product), capturing richer rotational patterns than RotatE's complex rotations.

nodes.label: radam
nodes.definition: Rectified Adam: an Adam variant that automatically controls the variance of the adaptive learning rate during the early stages of training by computing the variance of the second-moment estimator and only applying the adaptive learning rate when its variance is sufficiently low, using SGD with momentum in the initial warmup phase.

nodes.label: random subspace method
nodes.definition: The random subspace method is an ensemble strategy that trains each base learner on a randomly selected subset of input features rather than on all features. It promotes diversity among learners and is especially useful in high-dimensional settings.

nodes.label: rational quadratic spline
nodes.definition: In Neural Spline Flows: a monotone piecewise rational function defined by knot positions, values, and derivatives, used as the coupling layer transformation. More expressive than affine coupling while remaining analytically invertible.

nodes.label: realnvp
nodes.definition: Real-valued Non-Volume Preserving: a normalizing flow that uses affine coupling layers where the input is split into two halves $(\mathbf{x}_1, \mathbf{x}_2)$, one is passed through unchanged while the other is affinely transformed conditioned on the first: $\mathbf{y}_1 = \mathbf{x}_1$, $\mathbf{y}_2 = \mathbf{x}_2 \odot \exp(s(\mathbf{x}_1)) + t(\mathbf{x}_1)$, yielding a triangular Jacobian with tractable determin…

nodes.label: recurrent state-space model
nodes.definition: A latent dynamics model combining deterministic recurrence (GRU) with stochastic state: $h_t = f(h_{t-1}, z_{t-1}, a_{t-1})$ (deterministic), $z_t \sim p(z_t|h_t)$ (prior) or $z_t \sim q(z_t|h_t, x_t)$ (posterior). Used in PlaNet, Dreamer.

nodes.label: recursive partitioning
nodes.definition: The process of building a decision tree by recursively splitting the data at each node: choose the best feature and threshold, create two child nodes, and repeat on each child until a stopping criterion is met.

nodes.label: reduced rank regression
nodes.definition: A multivariate regression method that constrains the coefficient matrix $\mathbf{B}$ in $\mathbf{Y} = \mathbf{X}\mathbf{B} + \mathbf{E}$ to have rank $r < \min(p, q)$: $\mathbf{B} = \mathbf{C}\mathbf{D}^\top$ where $\mathbf{C} \in \mathbb{R}^{p \times r}$, $\mathbf{D} \in \mathbb{R}^{q \times r}$, capturing the most important linear combinations of predictors and responses.

nodes.label: reformer
nodes.definition: An efficient Transformer variant that replaces standard $O(n^2)$ dot-product attention with locality-sensitive hashing (LSH) attention that is $O(n \log n)$, and uses reversible residual layers to reduce memory from $O(nL)$ to $O(n)$ by recomputing activations during backpropagation.

nodes.label: regret
nodes.definition: In online learning/bandits, the difference between the cumulative reward of the best fixed strategy and the learner's cumulative reward: $R_T = \max_a \sum_{t=1}^{T} r_t(a) - \sum_{t=1}^{T} r_t(a_t)$. Sublinear regret ($R_T / T \to 0$) means the learner is asymptotically optimal.

nodes.label: regret minimization
