nodes.definition: The goal of achieving low cumulative regret $R_T = \sum_t (\max_a r_t(a) - r_t(a_t))$: the difference between the best fixed strategy and the learner's performance. Sublinear $R_T$ → asymptotically optimal. CFR minimizes regret per information set.

nodes.label: relation network
nodes.definition: A few-shot learning model that replaces fixed distance metrics with a learned relation module: for each query-support pair, concatenate their embeddings and pass through a neural network that outputs a relation score $r(\mathbf{x}_q, \mathbf{x}_s) = g_\phi(\text{concat}(f_\theta(\mathbf{x}_q), f_\theta(\mathbf{x}_s)))$, enabling the model to learn task-specific similarity.

nodes.label: relational graph convolutional network
nodes.definition: An extension of graph convolutional networks to multi-relational (heterogeneous) graphs where edges have types, using relation-specific weight matrices: $\mathbf{h}_i^{(l+1)} = \sigma\left(\sum_{r \in \mathcal{R}} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{N}_r(i)} \frac{1}{c_{i,r}} \mathbf{W}_r^{(l)} \mathbf{h}_j^{(l)} + \mathbf{W}_0^{(l)} \mathbf{h}_i^{(l)}\right)$.

nodes.label: relevance vector machine
nodes.definition: A Bayesian sparse kernel method that places independent Gaussian priors $w_i \sim N(0, \alpha_i^{-1})$ on the weights of a kernel model $y = \sum_i w_i K(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{x}_i) + \epsilon$, then uses type-II maximum likelihood (evidence maximization) to estimate the hyperparameters $\{\alpha_i\}$, driving most $\alpha_i \to \infty$ and pruning the corresponding basis functions to yield a sparse model.

nodes.label: reparameterization trick
nodes.definition: A technique for backpropagating through stochastic nodes by expressing a random sample as a deterministic function of parameters and noise: $\mathbf{z} = \boldsymbol{\mu} + \boldsymbol{\sigma} \odot \boldsymbol{\epsilon}$ where $\boldsymbol{\epsilon} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I})$, making the sampling process differentiable.

nodes.label: representation learning
nodes.definition: Already defined.

nodes.label: residual
nodes.definition: The difference between observed and predicted values: $e_i = y_i - \hat{y}_i$. In regression: used for model diagnostics (normality, heteroscedasticity, autocorrelation). In gradient boosting: pseudo-residuals $r_i = -\partial L / \partial \hat{y}_i$.

nodes.label: resnext
nodes.definition: An extension of ResNet that replaces the residual block with a split-transform-merge strategy: the input is split into $C$ parallel pathways (cardinality), each applying a small convolution, then outputs are summed — equivalent to grouped convolution, providing a new dimension (cardinality) to scale besides depth and width.

nodes.label: restricted boltzmann machine
nodes.definition: A Boltzmann machine with a bipartite structure: connections only between visible units $\mathbf{v}$ and hidden units $\mathbf{h}$ (no intra-layer connections), enabling efficient block Gibbs sampling since $P(\mathbf{h} \mid \mathbf{v})$ and $P(\mathbf{v} \mid \mathbf{h})$ factorize: $P(h_j = 1 \mid \mathbf{v}) = \sigma(\sum_i w_{ij} v_i + c_j)$.

nodes.label: retinanet
nodes.definition: A single-stage object detector that uses a Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) backbone and introduces focal loss $\text{FL}(p_t) = -\alpha_t (1-p_t)^\gamma \log(p_t)$ to address the extreme foreground-background class imbalance that causes single-stage detectors to underperform two-stage ones.

nodes.label: retro
nodes.definition: Retrieval-Enhanced Transformer: a language model that retrieves nearest-neighbor passages from a large external database during both training and inference, integrating retrieved text via chunked cross-attention layers inserted every few Transformer blocks, enabling a 25x smaller model to match the performance of larger models.

nodes.label: reward modeling
nodes.definition: Reward modeling is the process of learning a scalar-valued model of human or task preference, often from pairwise comparisons or demonstrations, so that the learned reward can guide optimization or reinforcement learning. It is a core ingredient of preference-based alignment methods such as RLHF.

nodes.label: reward prediction
nodes.definition: In world models predicting reward from latent state. Part of RSSM in Dreamer and PlaNet.

nodes.label: ripper
nodes.definition: Repeated Incremental Pruning to Produce Error Reduction: a rule learning algorithm that learns an ordered set of if-then rules by growing rules greedily (adding conditions to maximize information gain), then pruning and optimizing each rule, with a separate-and-conquer strategy.

nodes.label: rlhf
nodes.definition: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback: a framework for aligning LLMs with human preferences by: (1) collecting human comparisons of model outputs, (2) training a reward model on the comparison data, and (3) fine-tuning the LLM using PPO to maximize the reward while staying close to the original model via a KL penalty.

nodes.label: robotic control
nodes.definition: Using ML/RL to control robots: joint torques, end-effector positions, grasping actions. Methods: RL (SAC, PPO for continuous control), imitation learning (BC, DAgger), RT-2 (VLM for robot actions). Challenges: sim-to-real transfer, safety.

nodes.label: robust statistics
nodes.definition: Statistical methods resistant to outliers and model misspecification. Huber loss, Theil-Sen, RANSAC, Median Absolute Deviation, MCD (Minimum Covariance Determinant). Breakdown point: fraction of outliers the method can handle.

nodes.label: rotate
nodes.definition: A knowledge graph embedding model that represents relations as rotations in complex space: $\mathbf{t} = \mathbf{h} \circ \mathbf{r}$ where $\mathbf{h}, \mathbf{t} \in \mathbb{C}^d$, $\mathbf{r} \in \mathbb{C}^d$ with $|r_i| = 1$ (unit-modulus), and $\circ$ is the element-wise (Hadamard) product, enabling modeling of symmetry, antisymmetry, inversion, and composition relation patterns.

nodes.label: rotation
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: A rigid transformation that preserves distances and orientations, represented by an orthogonal matrix $\mathbf{R}$ with $\det(\mathbf{R}) = 1$ (proper rotation, $SO(n)$). In 2D: $\mathbf{R}(\theta) = \begin{pmatrix} \cos\theta & -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta & \cos\theta \end{pmatrix}$. In RoPE: positional encoding via rotation.

nodes.label: rprop
nodes.definition: Resilient Propagation: a gradient descent variant that uses only the sign of the gradient (not its magnitude) and adapts step sizes individually per parameter based on sign consistency: if the gradient sign is the same as the previous step, increase the step size; if it flips, decrease it.

nodes.label: rt-2
nodes.definition: Robotic Transformer 2: a vision-language-action model that fine-tunes a large VLM (PaLI-X or PaLM-E) on robotic trajectory data, outputting robotic actions as text tokens in the VLM's vocabulary, enabling the robot to leverage the VLM's world knowledge for novel object manipulation and semantic reasoning.

nodes.label: safety constraint
nodes.definition: In SafeOpt: a constraint that must be satisfied at every evaluation: $g(\mathbf{x}) \geq h$ (the system must remain safe). The safe set grows as the GP confidence bounds narrow, enabling cautious exploration.

nodes.label: sandwich estimator
nodes.definition: A robust variance estimator $\hat{\text{Var}}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\beta}}) = \mathbf{B}^{-1} \mathbf{M} \mathbf{B}^{-1}$ (sandwich: $B^{-1}$ is the bread, $M$ is the meat) that is consistent even when the assumed model is misspecified. Used in GEE for valid standard errors under working correlation misspecification.

nodes.label: se(3)-transformer
nodes.definition: A Transformer architecture that is equivariant under the SE(3) group (3D rotations and translations), using SE(3)-equivariant attention where queries, keys, and values are type-$l$ spherical tensor features and the attention mechanism preserves the transformation properties, enabling principled processing of 3D point clouds and molecular structures.

nodes.label: second-order gradient
nodes.definition:
The gradient of the gradient: $
abla^2 f$ (Hessian) or $
abla_	heta (
abla_	heta L)$. Required for: Newton's method, MAML (gradient through gradient), K-FAC. First-order approximation (FOMAML, Reptile) avoids computing it.

nodes.label: self-organizing map
nodes.definition: An unsupervised neural network that maps high-dimensional data onto a low-dimensional grid (typically 2D) while preserving topological relationships, using competitive learning where the best-matching unit (BMU) and its grid neighbors are updated toward the input: $\mathbf{w}_j \leftarrow \mathbf{w}_j + \alpha h(j, j^*)(\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{w}_j)$.

nodes.label: self-representation
nodes.definition: In subspace clustering each data point is a linear combination of others: X = XC with diag(C) = 0.

nodes.label: semantic segmentation
nodes.definition: Semantic segmentation is the dense prediction task of assigning a semantic class label to every pixel or image location. It produces a category map rather than a single image-level label or a sparse set of detections.

nodes.label: seq2seq
nodes.definition: A sequence-to-sequence model maps an input sequence to an output sequence, possibly of different length. It is a general framework for tasks such as translation, summarization, transcription, and structured generation.

nodes.label: sequential monte carlo
nodes.definition: A family of particle-based algorithms that approximate a sequence of target distributions $\{\pi_t\}_{t=0}^{T}$ by maintaining a weighted particle population, applying importance sampling and resampling at each step, generalizing particle filtering beyond state space models to static Bayesian inference, rare event simulation, and optimization.

nodes.label: session-based recommender
nodes.definition: A recommendation system that generates recommendations based only on the sequence of interactions within an anonymous session (without long-term user profiles), using RNNs, attention, or graph neural networks to model the temporal sequence of clicks/views within the current session.

nodes.label: set intersection
nodes.definition: Already defined as 'intersection'.

nodes.label: set transformer
nodes.definition: A Transformer architecture for set-structured data that uses Induced Set Attention Blocks (ISAB) with $m$ learnable inducing points to reduce the $O(n^2)$ attention complexity to $O(nm)$, and a Pooling by Multihead Attention (PMA) block for permutation-invariant set-level output.

nodes.label: sgc
nodes.definition: Simple Graph Convolution: a simplified GCN that removes nonlinear activations between layers, collapsing the entire network to a single linear transformation: $\hat{\mathbf{Y}} = \text{softmax}(\hat{\mathbf{S}}^K \mathbf{X} \mathbf{W})$ where $\hat{\mathbf{S}} = \hat{\mathbf{D}}^{-1/2} \hat{\mathbf{A}} \hat{\mathbf{D}}^{-1/2}$, achieving comparable performance with much faster training.

nodes.label: shortest path algorithm
nodes.definition: An algorithm for finding the path with minimum total weight between vertices in a graph. Dijkstra: $O((V+E) \log V)$ for non-negative weights. Bellman-Ford: $O(VE)$ for general. Floyd-Warshall: $O(V^3)$ all-pairs. Used in Isomap for geodesic distances.

nodes.label: singular value decomposition
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: The singular value decomposition factors a matrix as $A=U\Sigma V^	op$, where $U$ and $V$ are orthogonal matrices and $\Sigma$ is diagonal with nonnegative singular values. It is the canonical orthogonal decomposition of a rectangular matrix.

nodes.label: sinkhorn algorithm
nodes.definition: An iterative algorithm for solving the entropy-regularized optimal transport problem: alternating row and column normalization of the kernel matrix $\mathbf{K}_{ij} = \exp(-\mathbf{C}_{ij}/\epsilon)$ to produce a doubly stochastic transport plan. Used in SuperGlue for differentiable matching.

nodes.label: slice sampling
nodes.definition: An MCMC algorithm that samples from a distribution by defining a slice $S = \{x : u < f(x)\}$ (where $u$ is uniformly sampled below the current density) and uniformly sampling from $S$. No tuning of proposal distribution needed. Used in NUTS for selecting from the trajectory.

nodes.label: slot attention
nodes.definition: An attention-based module that decomposes a scene into a fixed number of object-centric representations (slots) by iteratively applying attention between slots (queries) and the input features (keys/values), with competition between slots via softmax normalization over the slot dimension.

nodes.label: softmax function
nodes.definition: The softmax function maps a vector $z \in \mathbb{R}^K$ to the probability simplex by $\mathrm{softmax}(z)_i = e^{z_i}/\sum_{j=1}^K e^{z_j}$. It converts arbitrary logits into normalized nonnegative class probabilities.

nodes.label: span corruption
nodes.definition: T5's pre-training objective: randomly select and mask contiguous spans of tokens, replacing each span with a single sentinel token. The model predicts the original span content. More efficient than per-token masking (BERT) because fewer tokens need prediction.

nodes.label: sparse approximation
nodes.definition: The problem of approximating a signal $\mathbf{y}$ as a sparse linear combination of dictionary atoms: $\mathbf{y} \approx \mathbf{D}\mathbf{x}$ with $\|\mathbf{x}\|_0 \leq K$ (at most $K$ non-zero coefficients). Solved by: OMP, basis pursuit ($L_1$), iterative thresholding.

nodes.label: sparse gaussian process
nodes.definition: A sparse Gaussian process is an approximation to Gaussian process inference that uses a reduced set of inducing variables or other structure to avoid the full cubic cost of exact GP methods. It aims to preserve the uncertainty-aware benefits of GPs at larger scale.

nodes.label: sparse gradient
nodes.definition: A sparse gradient is a gradient vector in which only a small fraction of coordinates are nonzero or significantly nonzero. Such gradients arise when the objective depends on only a few parameters per example or when the model or regularizer induces coordinate sparsity.

nodes.label: sparse representation
nodes.definition: Representing data as a sparse linear combination of dictionary elements: $\mathbf{x} \approx \mathbf{D}\boldsymbol{\alpha}$ with $\|\boldsymbol{\alpha}\|_0 \ll n$. Sparse coding learns both the dictionary and sparse codes. Related to compressed sensing.

nodes.label: spatial transformer
nodes.definition: A differentiable module that applies a learned spatial transformation (affine, thin-plate spline) to feature maps: (1) localization network predicts transformation parameters, (2) grid generator creates a sampling grid, (3) bilinear sampler produces the transformed output. Used in PointNet for input alignment.

nodes.label: spherical harmonics
nodes.definition: Orthonormal basis functions $Y_l^m(\theta, \phi)$ on the sphere $S^2$, indexed by degree $l \geq 0$ and order $|m| \leq l$. Used to represent: view-dependent color in 3D Gaussian Splatting, angular functions in equivariant GNNs (NequIP), and directional signals.

nodes.label: spline
nodes.definition: A piecewise polynomial function defined on intervals between knots, with specified continuity at the knots. Cubic spline: degree 3, $C^2$ continuity. B-splines: local basis functions. Used in: spline regression, GAM, KAN, Neural Spline Flows.

nodes.label: squeezenet
nodes.definition: A compact CNN architecture that achieves AlexNet-level accuracy with 50x fewer parameters by using Fire modules consisting of a squeeze layer (1x1 convolutions reducing channels) followed by an expand layer (mix of 1x1 and 3x3 convolutions expanding channels).

nodes.label: ssd
nodes.definition: Single Shot MultiBox Detector: a single-stage object detection architecture that uses multi-scale feature maps from different layers of a CNN backbone, predicting bounding box offsets and class scores from default (anchor) boxes at multiple scales and aspect ratios, enabling efficient detection of objects at various sizes.

nodes.label: stable diffusion
nodes.definition: An open-source text-to-image latent diffusion model that uses a frozen CLIP text encoder for text conditioning, a U-Net denoiser operating in the latent space of a VQ-GAN autoencoder, and classifier-free guidance for high-quality conditional generation, enabling widespread adoption of diffusion-based image generation.

nodes.label: state space model
nodes.definition: A probabilistic model for time series that represents the system as latent state dynamics $\mathbf{x}_t = \mathbf{F}\mathbf{x}_{t-1} + \mathbf{w}_t$ (state equation) and observations $\mathbf{y}_t = \mathbf{H}\mathbf{x}_t + \mathbf{v}_t$ (observation equation), where $\mathbf{w}_t$ and $\mathbf{v}_t$ are noise processes.

nodes.label: stepwise selection
nodes.definition: Iteratively adding or removing features based on statistical criteria. Forward: add best. Backward: remove worst. Bidirectional: both. Criticized for multiple testing. Modern alternatives: Lasso, elastic net.

nodes.label: stochastic gradient descent
nodes.definition: Stochastic gradient descent updates parameters using a noisy but cheap estimate of the full gradient, typically $\theta_{t+1}=\theta_t-\eta_t g_t$ with $\mathbb{E}[g_t \mid \theta_t]=\nabla f(\theta_t)$. It is the basic scalable optimizer for large datasets and streaming problems.

nodes.label: stochastic matrix
nodes.definition: A square matrix $\mathbf{P}$ with non-negative entries where each row (row-stochastic) or column (column-stochastic) sums to 1: $\sum_j P_{ij} = 1$. Represents the transition probabilities of a discrete Markov chain.

nodes.label: structural topic model
nodes.definition: An extension of topic models (LDA) that incorporates document-level metadata (covariates) into both the topic prevalence ($\boldsymbol{\theta}_d$ depends on document covariates via logistic-normal prior) and topic content ($\boldsymbol{\phi}_k$ can vary by covariates), enabling researchers to study how topics relate to document characteristics.

nodes.label: subset
nodes.definition: A set $A$ is a subset of $B$ ($A \subseteq B$) if every element of $A$ is also an element of $B$: $\forall x: x \in A \Rightarrow x \in B$. Proper subset: $A \subset B$ means $A \subseteq B$ and $A \neq B$.

nodes.label: sum of squared errors
nodes.definition: The sum of squared residuals: $\text{SSE} = \sum_i (y_i - \hat{y}_i)^2 = \|\mathbf{y} - \hat{\mathbf{y}}\|^2$. OLS minimizes SSE. In k-means: minimize total within-cluster SSE. In bisecting k-means: split cluster with highest SSE.

nodes.label: support vector regression
nodes.definition: An extension of SVM to regression that fits a function within an $\epsilon$-insensitive tube around the data: $\min \frac{1}{2}\|\mathbf{w}\|^2 + C \sum_i (\xi_i + \xi_i^*)$ s.t. $|y_i - \mathbf{w}^\top \mathbf{x}_i - b| \leq \epsilon + \xi_i + \xi_i^*$, penalizing only predictions more than $\epsilon$ away from the target.

nodes.label: survival analysis
nodes.definition: Statistical methods for analyzing time-to-event data (survival times), handling censored observations (incomplete event times). Key methods: Kaplan-Meier (nonparametric), Cox PH (semiparametric), parametric models (Weibull, log-normal).

nodes.label: svd++
nodes.definition: An extension of matrix factorization that incorporates implicit feedback: $\hat{r}_{ui} = \mu + b_u + b_i + \mathbf{q}_i^\top (\mathbf{p}_u + |N(u)|^{-1/2} \sum_{j \in N(u)} \mathbf{y}_j)$ where $N(u)$ is the set of items user $u$ has interacted with and $\mathbf{y}_j$ are implicit factor vectors, enriching the user representation beyond explicit ratings.

nodes.label: switch transformer
nodes.definition: A Transformer architecture that replaces dense feed-forward layers with sparse Mixture-of-Experts layers where a learned router selects exactly one expert per token: $\text{Router}(\mathbf{x}) = \arg\max_i (\mathbf{W}_r \mathbf{x})_i$, achieving up to 7x faster pre-training than T5 with the same compute budget by scaling to thousands of experts.

nodes.label: synthetic control method
nodes.definition: A causal inference method for evaluating the effect of an intervention on a single treated unit by constructing a synthetic counterfactual from a weighted combination of donor (untreated) units: $\hat{Y}_{1t}^{N} = \sum_{j=2}^{J+1} w_j Y_{jt}$ where weights $\mathbf{w}$ are chosen to match pre-intervention outcomes of the treated unit, and the treatment effect is the gap between the treated unit and its synthetic con…

nodes.label: tabular data
nodes.definition: Data organized in rows (samples) and columns (features): $\mathbf{X} \in \mathbb{R}^{n \times p}$. Features may be numerical or categorical. Best methods: gradient boosting (XGBoost, LightGBM), BART, TabPFN. Deep learning alternatives: TabNet, FT-Transformer, NODE.

nodes.label: target network
nodes.definition: In DQN: a copy of the Q-network $\theta^-$ updated periodically (hard: copy every $C$ steps) or continuously (soft: $\theta^- \leftarrow \tau\theta + (1-\tau)\theta^-$) to provide stable target values, preventing the moving-target problem in temporal difference learning.

nodes.label: taylor expansion
nodes.definition: Approximating a function $f(x)$ near a point $a$ by a polynomial: $f(x) \approx \sum_{n=0}^{N} \frac{f^{(n)}(a)}{n!}(x-a)^n$. First-order: gradient. Second-order: includes Hessian. Used in: XGBoost (second-order Taylor of the loss), trust region methods.

nodes.label: td(lambda)
nodes.definition: A temporal difference learning method that uses eligibility traces to interpolate between TD(0) (bootstrapping from one step) and Monte Carlo (using full episode returns): $V(s) \leftarrow V(s) + \alpha \delta_t e_t(s)$ where the eligibility trace $e_t(s) = \gamma \lambda e_{t-1}(s) + \mathbf{1}[s_t = s]$ decays past states' credit by $\gamma\lambda$ per step.

nodes.label: td3
nodes.definition: Twin Delayed Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient: improves DDPG with three key tricks: (1) twin critics (take the minimum of two Q-networks to reduce overestimation), (2) delayed policy updates (update actor less frequently than critic), and (3) target policy smoothing (add noise to target actions for regularization).

nodes.label: temporal encoding
nodes.definition: Encoding temporal information (timestamps, time of day, day of week) for time series and temporal models. Methods: sinusoidal (Transformer), learned embeddings, datetime features (hour, day, month), time2vec.

nodes.label: test-time training
nodes.definition: A method that adapts a pre-trained model to each test sample by performing a few gradient steps at test time on a self-supervised auxiliary task (e.g., rotation prediction, masked autoencoding) computed on the test input itself, then using the adapted model for prediction, improving robustness to distribution shift.

nodes.label: text classification
nodes.definition: The task of assigning a category label to a text document. Methods: Naive Bayes, SVM on TF-IDF, CNN, LSTM, BERT fine-tuning. Tasks: sentiment analysis, spam detection, topic classification.

nodes.label: text conditioning
nodes.definition: Conditioning generation on text input. Methods: cross-attention (Stable Diffusion: image attends to text), classifier-free guidance, text projection (DALL-E 2), concatenation.

nodes.label: text-to-speech
nodes.definition: Converting text to spoken audio. Pipeline: text analysis → acoustic model → vocoder. Modern: VITS (end-to-end), VALL-E (codec language model), Bark, neural vocoders (HiFi-GAN, WaveRNN).

nodes.label: tf-idf
nodes.definition: Term Frequency-Inverse Document Frequency: a text feature weighting scheme that computes the importance of a word in a document relative to a corpus: $\text{TF-IDF}(t, d) = \text{TF}(t, d) \cdot \text{IDF}(t) = f_{t,d} \cdot \log\frac{N}{\text{df}_t}$, where $f_{t,d}$ is the term frequency and $\text{df}_t$ is the number of documents containing term $t$.

nodes.label: time series forecasting
nodes.definition: Predicting future values of a time series. Already defined as 'forecasting'. Methods: ARIMA, ETS, Prophet, N-BEATS, DeepAR, TFT, PatchTST, iTransformer, DLinear, TimesNet.

nodes.label: timesformer
nodes.definition: A video Transformer that applies separate temporal and spatial self-attention (divided space-time attention): each layer first applies self-attention across frames at each spatial position, then across spatial positions within each frame, decomposing the $O((T \times H \times W)^2)$ full attention into $O(T^2 + (HW)^2)$.

nodes.label: tokenization
nodes.definition: The process of splitting text into tokens (subwords, words, or characters) that serve as the input units for language models. Methods: BPE, SentencePiece, WordPiece, Unigram.

nodes.label: transformer-xl
nodes.definition: An extension of the Transformer that introduces segment-level recurrence by caching and attending to hidden states from previous segments, along with relative positional encodings, enabling modeling of long-range dependencies beyond the fixed context window.

nodes.label: tree search
nodes.definition: Tree search is the systematic exploration of a tree-structured state space in order to find a node, path, or optimal solution satisfying a specified criterion. Each node represents a partial solution or state, and edges represent admissible expansions.

nodes.label: tree-structured parzen estimator
nodes.definition: A sequential model-based optimization algorithm that models the densities $\ell(\mathbf{x}) = p(\mathbf{x} \mid y < y^*)$ and $g(\mathbf{x}) = p(\mathbf{x} \mid y \geq y^*)$ of configurations below and above a quantile threshold $y^*$ using kernel density estimators (tree-structured Parzen windows), then maximizes the ratio $\ell(\mathbf{x})/g(\mathbf{x})$ to select the next evaluation point.

nodes.label: tri-training
nodes.definition: A semi-supervised ensemble method that trains three classifiers on bootstrap samples of the labeled data, then iteratively labels unlabeled instances where two classifiers agree (majority vote) and adds them to the training set of the third classifier, cycling through all three classifiers as the learner.

nodes.label: triplet network
nodes.definition: A metric learning architecture that processes three inputs — an anchor, a positive (same class), and a negative (different class) — through a shared network, trained with triplet loss $\mathcal{L} = \max(0, d(a, p) - d(a, n) + \alpha)$ to make the anchor closer to the positive than to the negative by at least a margin $\alpha$.

nodes.label: trust region
nodes.definition: A region around the current parameters where the local approximation (e.g., quadratic model) is trusted: $\|\Delta\boldsymbol{\theta}\| \leq \delta$. TRPO: trust region for policy updates constrained by KL divergence. Trust region methods: solve constrained subproblem within the region.

nodes.label: tweedie regression
nodes.definition: A generalized linear model using the Tweedie distribution family, which includes Gaussian ($p=0$), Poisson ($p=1$), Gamma ($p=2$), and compound Poisson-Gamma ($1 < p < 2$) as special cases, with variance function $\text{Var}(Y) = \phi \mu^p$, particularly useful for insurance and rainfall data with exact zeros and continuous positive values.

nodes.label: uncertainty quantification
nodes.definition: Methods for estimating and communicating the uncertainty in model predictions. Bayesian: posterior predictive variance. Frequentist: confidence/prediction intervals. Deep learning: MC dropout, deep ensembles, conformal prediction.

nodes.label: unsupervised learning
nodes.definition: A learning paradigm where the model discovers structure in data without labeled examples: find patterns, clusters, density, or representations from the data distribution $P(\mathbf{x})$ alone.

nodes.label: user behavior modeling
nodes.definition: Modeling user behavior patterns for recommendation: click sequences (DIN), interest evolution (DIEN), multi-interest (MIND), session patterns (GRU4Rec). Captures: temporal dynamics, diverse interests, context dependence.

nodes.label: var
nodes.definition: Vector Autoregression: a multivariate time series model where each variable is a linear function of its own past values and the past values of all other variables: $\mathbf{X}_t = \mathbf{c} + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \mathbf{A}_i \mathbf{X}_{t-i} + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}_t$, denoted VAR($p$).

nodes.label: variance
nodes.definition: The variance of a random variable $X$ is $\mathrm{Var}(X)=\mathbb{E}[(X-\mathbb{E}X)^2]$. It measures the expected squared deviation from the mean and is the standard second-order measure of dispersion.

nodes.label: variational autoencoder recommender
nodes.definition: A collaborative filtering model based on the variational autoencoder that encodes user interaction vectors into a latent space via an inference network $q_\phi(\mathbf{z} \mid \mathbf{x}_u)$, then decodes to reconstruct user preferences, regularized by a KL divergence term, with multinomial likelihood for implicit feedback data.

nodes.label: vdn
nodes.definition: Value Decomposition Networks: factorizes the joint action-value function as a sum of individual agent utilities for decentralized multi-agent RL.

nodes.label: vector quantization
nodes.definition: The process of mapping continuous vectors to a finite set of codebook vectors (prototypes): $q(\mathbf{x}) = \arg\min_{\mathbf{e}_k \in \mathcal{C}} \|\mathbf{x} - \mathbf{e}_k\|$, minimizing distortion. Used in VQ-VAE, neural audio codecs, and data compression.

nodes.label: vector-quantized vae
nodes.definition: A VAE variant that uses a discrete latent space by quantizing the encoder output to the nearest vector in a learned codebook: $\mathbf{z}_q = \arg\min_{\mathbf{e}_k \in \mathcal{C}} \|\mathbf{z}_e - \mathbf{e}_k\|$, with the straight-through estimator to pass gradients through the non-differentiable quantization, producing discrete latent representations.

nodes.label: vicreg
nodes.definition: Variance-Invariance-Covariance Regularization: a self-supervised method with three loss terms: (1) invariance (MSE between embeddings of augmented views), (2) variance (hinge loss to keep embedding standard deviation above a threshold), and (3) covariance (minimize off-diagonal covariance to decorrelate embedding dimensions).

nodes.label: video prediction
nodes.definition: Predicting future video frames. ConvLSTM PredRNN PhyDNet.

nodes.label: video understanding
nodes.definition: Extracting information from video: action recognition, temporal localization, video captioning, video QA. Methods: 3D CNN (C3D, I3D), two-stream (RGB + flow), Video Transformers (TimeSformer, Video Swin), video LLMs.

nodes.label: vigilance parameter
nodes.definition: ART threshold rho controlling category granularity. High rho: many categories. Low: few.

nodes.label: vision-language model
nodes.definition: A model processing both images and text: CLIP (contrastive alignment), BLIP-2 (Q-Former bridge), LLaVA (project visual features to LLM), Flamingo (cross-attention), GPT-4V, Gemini (native multimodal). Enables: VQA, captioning, grounding.

nodes.label: volume rendering
nodes.definition: Rendering a 3D volume by accumulating color and opacity along rays: $C(\mathbf{r}) = \int_{t_n}^{t_f} T(t) \sigma(\mathbf{r}(t)) \mathbf{c}(\mathbf{r}(t), \mathbf{d}) dt$ where $T(t) = \exp(-\int_{t_n}^t \sigma(\mathbf{r}(s))ds)$. Foundation for NeRF.

nodes.label: voting
nodes.definition: Combining predictions by counting votes. Majority voting: most common prediction wins. Weighted voting: weight by classifier quality. Soft voting: average probabilities.

nodes.label: voxelnet
nodes.definition: A 3D object detection network for LiDAR point clouds that partitions the 3D space into voxels, encodes each voxel's points using a PointNet-like module (Voxel Feature Encoding), then applies 3D sparse convolutions followed by a region proposal network to predict 3D bounding boxes.

nodes.label: wake-sleep
nodes.definition: A training algorithm for generative models with latent variables that alternates between a wake phase (updating generative weights $\theta$ to maximize $E_{q_\phi(\mathbf{z} \mid \mathbf{x})}[\log p_\theta(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{z})]$ using recognition-network samples) and a sleep phase (updating recognition weights $\phi$ to minimize $E_{p_\theta(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{z})}[-\log q_\phi(\mathbf{z} \mid \mathbf{x})]$ using…

nodes.label: weibull distribution
nodes.definition: A continuous distribution $f(t; k, \lambda) = \frac{k}{\lambda}(t/\lambda)^{k-1}\exp(-(t/\lambda)^k)$ for $t \geq 0$, used in survival analysis. $k = 1$: exponential. $k > 1$: increasing hazard. $k < 1$: decreasing hazard. The only distribution that is both an AFT and a proportional hazards model.

nodes.label: weight decay
nodes.definition: A regularization technique that shrinks weights toward zero by adding a penalty $\frac{\lambda}{2}\|\mathbf{w}\|^2$ to the loss, equivalent to $L_2$ regularization for SGD but different for Adam (AdamW implements true weight decay: $\mathbf{w} \leftarrow (1-\eta\lambda)\mathbf{w} - \eta\mathbf{g}$).

nodes.label: weight pruning
nodes.definition: Removing weights (setting to zero) from a neural network to reduce model size and computation. Unstructured: individual weights. Structured: entire filters/channels. Magnitude pruning: remove smallest weights. Lottery Ticket: prune + rewind to init.

nodes.label: weight standardization
nodes.definition: Normalizing the weights of convolutional layers to have zero mean and unit variance per output channel: $\hat{W}_{ij} = (W_{ij} - \bar{W}_j)/\sigma_j$. Used in NFNet (with Scaled Weight Standardization) to enable training without batch normalization.

nodes.label: weighted average
nodes.definition: A generalization of the arithmetic mean where each value is multiplied by a weight: $\bar{x}_w = \frac{\sum_i w_i x_i}{\sum_i w_i}$ with $w_i \geq 0$. Equal weights recovers the standard mean. Foundation for attention mechanisms, EMA, and kernel methods.

nodes.label: whisper
nodes.definition: A large-scale speech recognition model trained on 680,000 hours of weakly supervised audio-text data from the internet, using an encoder-decoder Transformer that takes log-mel spectrogram input and outputs text tokens, capable of multilingual speech recognition, translation, and language identification in a single model.

nodes.label: word2vec
nodes.definition: A family of neural embedding methods that learn dense vector representations of words from their co-occurrence contexts, using either Skip-gram (predict context words from target) or CBOW (predict target from context), trained efficiently with negative sampling: $\mathcal{L} = \log \sigma(\mathbf{w}_c^\top \mathbf{w}_t) + \sum_{k=1}^K E[\log \sigma(-\mathbf{w}_{n_k}^\top \mathbf{w}_t)]$.

nodes.label: world model
nodes.definition: A learned neural network model of the environment's dynamics that predicts future states, rewards, and/or observations given the current state and action, used in model-based reinforcement learning to simulate ("imagine") trajectories for planning or policy training without real-environment interaction.

nodes.label: x-means
nodes.definition: An extension of $k$-means that automatically determines the number of clusters by starting with $k=1$ and iteratively attempting to split each cluster using 2-means, accepting the split if it improves the BIC (Bayesian Information Criterion) under a Gaussian model assumption.

nodes.label: xlstm
nodes.definition: Extended Long Short-Term Memory: a modernized LSTM architecture with exponential gating ($\mathbf{f}_t = \exp(\mathbf{w}_f^\top \mathbf{x}_t)$), matrix memory (sLSTM uses scalar memory, mLSTM uses matrix memory $\mathbf{C}_t \in \mathbb{R}^{d \times d}$ with covariance update), and residual blocks, designed to compete with Transformers at scale.

nodes.label: yogi
nodes.definition: An adaptive gradient method that modifies Adam's second-moment update to use an additive control: $v_t = v_{t-1} + (1-\beta_2) \operatorname{sign}(g_t^2 - v_{t-1}) \odot g_t^2$ instead of the exponential moving average, preventing the effective learning rate from increasing (which can cause divergence in Adam), providing convergence guarantees for non-convex optimization.

nodes.label: yolo
nodes.definition: You Only Look Once: a single-stage object detection framework that divides the image into an $S \times S$ grid, predicts $B$ bounding boxes with confidence scores and $C$ class probabilities per cell in a single forward pass, treating detection as a regression problem rather than a classification pipeline.

nodes.label: zero-inflated poisson regression
nodes.definition: A regression model for count data with excess zeros that combines a point mass at zero with a Poisson distribution: with probability $\pi_i$, the count is exactly zero, and with probability $1-\pi_i$, it follows Poisson($\mu_i$), where both $\pi_i$ and $\mu_i$ are modeled as functions of covariates via logistic and log link functions.

nodes.label: zero-shot learning
nodes.definition: Zero-shot learning is the ability to perform prediction for classes, tasks, or outputs not seen during task-specific training by using side information, semantic descriptions, or broad pretraining. It relies on transfer through representation rather than direct labeled examples of the target classes.

nodes.label: zfnet
nodes.definition: An improved version of AlexNet that won ImageNet 2013, using deconvolution-based visualization to understand and optimize CNN features, resulting in smaller first-layer filters (7x7 instead of 11x11) and smaller stride (2 instead of 4) for better feature capture.

nodes.label: aalen additive model
nodes.definition: A nonparametric survival model that specifies the hazard as a linear function of covariates with time-varying coefficients: $h(t \mid \mathbf{x}) = \beta_0(t) + \sum_j \beta_j(t) x_j$, where the $\beta_j(t)$ are unspecified functions of time estimated nonparametrically.

nodes.label: actor-critic
nodes.definition: A policy gradient architecture with two components: an actor $\pi_\theta(a \mid s)$ that selects actions and a critic $V_\phi(s)$ (or $Q_\phi(s,a)$) that estimates the value function used as a baseline, updating the actor with $\nabla_\theta \log \pi_\theta(a_t \mid s_t) \cdot \hat{A}_t$ where $\hat{A}_t = r_t + \gamma V(s_{t+1}) - V(s_t)$ is the advantage.

nodes.label: adjoint method
nodes.category: Calculus of variations and optimal control
nodes.definition: A technique for efficiently computing gradients of a scalar objective with respect to parameters of a dynamical system (ODE/PDE) by solving an adjoint (backward-in-time) equation $\frac{d\mathbf{a}}{dt} = -\mathbf{a}^\top \frac{\partial f}{\partial \mathbf{x}}$ that propagates sensitivity information backward, avoiding storage of intermediate states.

nodes.label: affinity propagation
nodes.definition: A clustering algorithm that simultaneously considers all data points as potential exemplars (cluster centers) by exchanging messages (responsibilities and availabilities) between pairs of data points until convergence, automatically determining the number of clusters based on a preference parameter.

nodes.label: aft survival model
nodes.definition: The accelerated failure time (AFT) model specifies that the logarithm of survival time is a linear function of covariates: $\log T = \mathbf{x}^\top \boldsymbol{\beta} + \sigma \epsilon$, where $\epsilon$ follows a specified distribution (e.g., standard normal, logistic, or extreme value), directly modeling the effect of covariates on the time scale.

nodes.label: alternating least squares
nodes.definition: An optimization algorithm for matrix factorization that alternates between fixing one factor matrix and solving for the other via least squares: fix $\mathbf{V}$ and solve for $\mathbf{U}$ (each row is a least squares problem), then fix $\mathbf{U}$ and solve for $\mathbf{V}$, iterating until convergence.

nodes.label: annealed importance sampling
nodes.definition: A method for estimating the ratio of normalizing constants $Z_T/Z_0$ between two distributions by constructing a sequence of intermediate distributions $\pi_t \propto \pi_0^{1-\beta_t} \pi_T^{\beta_t}$ (with $\beta_0=0, \beta_T=1$) and importance-sampling through them using MCMC transitions, yielding an unbiased estimator of the normalizing constant ratio.

nodes.label: anogan
nodes.definition: Anomaly detection with Generative Adversarial Networks: a method that trains a GAN on normal data, then detects anomalies by mapping test images to the GAN's latent space (via gradient descent on $\mathbf{z}$) and computing an anomaly score based on the reconstruction error and discriminator score.

nodes.label: approximate bayesian computation
nodes.definition: A likelihood-free inference method for models with intractable likelihoods that works by: (1) sampling parameters from the prior $\theta \sim \pi(\theta)$, (2) simulating data $\mathbf{x}^* \sim p(\mathbf{x} \mid \theta)$, and (3) accepting $\theta$ if $d(S(\mathbf{x}^*), S(\mathbf{x}_{\text{obs}})) < \epsilon$, where $S$ are summary statistics and $\epsilon$ is a tolerance, producing approximate posterior samples.

nodes.label: apriori
nodes.definition: A frequent itemset mining algorithm that uses the anti-monotone property of support (if an itemset is infrequent, all its supersets are infrequent) to prune the search space, iteratively generating candidate itemsets of size $k+1$ from frequent itemsets of size $k$ and scanning the database to count their support.

nodes.label: art
nodes.definition: Adaptive Resonance Theory (ART) is a family of unsupervised neural network models that solve the stability-plasticity dilemma by using a vigilance parameter $\rho$ to gate resonance: an input is assigned to an existing category if the match function $\frac{\|\mathbf{I} \wedge \mathbf{w}_j\|}{\|\mathbf{I}\|} \geq \rho$ (for ART1 with binary inputs), otherwise a new category is created.

nodes.label: attention mechanism
nodes.definition: An attention mechanism computes a weighted combination of candidate values, where the weights depend on the compatibility between a query and a set of keys or contexts. It is a differentiable mechanism for selective information retrieval.

nodes.label: audioldm
nodes.definition: A text-to-audio generation model that applies latent diffusion to audio: a VAE encodes mel spectrograms into a latent space where a U-Net diffusion model operates, conditioned on CLAP (Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining) text embeddings, generating diverse audio from text descriptions.

nodes.label: autorec
nodes.definition: An autoencoder-based collaborative filtering model that takes a partially observed user (or item) rating vector as input, encodes it through a hidden layer, and reconstructs the full rating vector, with the reconstructed values serving as predicted ratings for unobserved items.

nodes.label: backpropagation
nodes.definition: Backpropagation is the reverse-mode automatic differentiation algorithm used to compute gradients of a scalar loss with respect to parameters in a computational graph. In neural networks it propagates error signals backward through layers using the chain rule.

nodes.label: bagging
nodes.definition: Bootstrap Aggregating: an ensemble method that trains $M$ base models on $M$ bootstrap samples (random samples with replacement) of the training data, then aggregates predictions by majority vote (classification) or averaging (regression), reducing variance without increasing bias.

nodes.label: banditron
nodes.definition: An online multiclass classification algorithm for the bandit setting where the learner only observes whether its prediction was correct (binary feedback), not the true label, extending the Perceptron by performing updates based on an exploration-exploitation trade-off with probability $\gamma$ of random exploration.

nodes.label: bayesian linear regression
nodes.definition: A probabilistic approach to linear regression that places a prior distribution on the weights $p(\boldsymbol{\beta})$ (typically Gaussian) and computes the posterior $p(\boldsymbol{\beta} \mid \mathbf{X}, \mathbf{y}) \propto p(\mathbf{y} \mid \mathbf{X}, \boldsymbol{\beta}) p(\boldsymbol{\beta})$, which is also Gaussian under conjugate priors, providing full uncertainty quantification over predictions.

nodes.label: bayesian optimization
nodes.definition: A sequential strategy for global optimization of expensive black-box functions that maintains a surrogate model (typically a Gaussian process) of the objective and uses an acquisition function (e.g., expected improvement $\text{EI}(\mathbf{x}) = E[\max(f(\mathbf{x}) - f^+, 0)]$) to select the next evaluation point, balancing exploration and exploitation.

nodes.label: bayesian personalized ranking
nodes.definition: An optimization framework for implicit feedback recommendation that maximizes the posterior probability of a pairwise item ordering, training a model to score observed (positive) items higher than unobserved (negative) items using the BPR-OPT criterion: $\sum_{(u,i,j)} \log \sigma(\hat{x}_{ui} - \hat{x}_{uj}) - \lambda \|\Theta\|^2$.

nodes.label: beit
nodes.definition: Bidirectional Encoder representation from Image Transformers: a self-supervised pre-training method for Vision Transformers that masks random image patches and predicts discrete visual tokens (from a pre-trained VQ-VAE codebook) at the masked positions, analogous to BERT's masked language modeling.

nodes.label: bigbird
nodes.definition: A sparse attention Transformer that combines three attention patterns — random attention (each token attends to $r$ random tokens), sliding window attention ($w$ local neighbors), and global attention ($g$ designated tokens attend to all) — to achieve $O(n)$ complexity while provably maintaining the universal approximation and Turing completeness of full attention.

nodes.label: bisenet
nodes.definition: Bilateral Segmentation Network: a real-time semantic segmentation architecture with two paths — a Spatial Path (preserving spatial details at high resolution via few downsampling steps) and a Context Path (capturing semantics via a deep backbone with global average pooling) — merged via a Feature Fusion Module.

nodes.label: boltzmann machine
nodes.definition: A stochastic recurrent neural network with symmetric connections where units have binary states $s_i \in \{0, 1\}$ sampled from the Boltzmann distribution $P(\mathbf{s}) = \frac{1}{Z} \exp(-E(\mathbf{s}))$ with energy $E(\mathbf{s}) = -\sum_{i<j} w_{ij} s_i s_j - \sum_i \theta_i s_i$, trained by matching data statistics via Gibbs sampling.

nodes.label: byol
nodes.definition: Bootstrap Your Own Latent: a self-supervised learning method that learns without negative pairs by using two networks — an online network (encoder + projector + predictor) and a target network (EMA of online, without predictor) — trained to predict the target's representation from a different augmented view of the same image.

nodes.label: c51
nodes.definition: A distributional reinforcement learning algorithm that represents the return distribution as a categorical distribution over $N = 51$ fixed, equally-spaced atoms $\{z_1, \ldots, z_N\}$ in $[V_{\min}, V_{\max}]$, learning the probability $p_i(s,a) = P(Z(s,a) = z_i)$ for each atom via a projected distributional Bellman update and cross-entropy loss.

nodes.label: cart
nodes.definition: Classification and Regression Trees: a decision tree algorithm that recursively partitions the feature space using binary splits chosen to minimize impurity (Gini impurity or entropy for classification, MSE for regression), with pruning via cost-complexity: $R_\alpha(T) = R(T) + \alpha |T|$.

nodes.label: causal language model
nodes.definition: A language modeling objective where the model predicts the next token given all preceding tokens: $P(x_t \mid x_1, \ldots, x_{t-1})$, enforced by a causal (left-to-right) attention mask that prevents each position from attending to future positions, enabling autoregressive text generation.

nodes.label: cdae
nodes.definition: Collaborative Denoising Autoencoder: an autoencoder-based CF model that adds corruption noise to user interaction vectors (randomly setting some observed interactions to zero) and trains to reconstruct the uncorrupted vector, with a user-specific node added to the hidden layer to personalize the reconstruction.

nodes.label: chaid
nodes.definition: Chi-squared Automatic Interaction Detector: a decision tree algorithm that uses chi-squared tests of independence to determine the best split at each node, merging non-significantly different categories before splitting, producing multi-way splits that directly correspond to statistically distinct groups.

nodes.label: chameleon
nodes.definition: A hierarchical agglomerative graph-based clustering algorithm that first partitions a $k$-nearest-neighbor graph into small sub-clusters using a graph partitioning algorithm, then iteratively merges sub-cluster pairs that maximize both relative interconnectivity (RI) and relative closeness (RC).

nodes.label: change of variables formula
nodes.definition: A formula for computing the density of a transformed random variable: if $\mathbf{y} = f(\mathbf{x})$ with $f$ invertible, then $p_Y(\mathbf{y}) = p_X(f^{-1}(\mathbf{y})) |\det J_{f^{-1}}(\mathbf{y})|$. Foundation for normalizing flows.

nodes.label: classifier-free guidance
nodes.definition: A technique for improving conditional generation quality in diffusion models that trains a single model with both conditional and unconditional objectives (randomly dropping the condition during training), then at inference, extrapolates between conditional and unconditional predictions: $\tilde{\epsilon} = \epsilon_{\text{uncond}} + s(\epsilon_{\text{cond}} - \epsilon_{\text{uncond}})$ with guidance scale $s > 1$.

nodes.label: clip
nodes.definition: Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training: a model that learns aligned image and text representations by training an image encoder and text encoder to maximize the cosine similarity of matching (image, text) pairs while minimizing it for non-matching pairs, using a symmetric cross-entropy (InfoNCE) loss over a batch of pairs.

nodes.label: coatnet
nodes.definition: A hybrid architecture that systematically combines depthwise separable convolutions (for local features) and self-attention (for global features) in a vertical layout: early stages use convolutions (better for local patterns) and later stages use attention (better for global patterns), with relative attention for translation equivariance.

nodes.label: compound scaling
nodes.definition: EfficientNet's method of jointly scaling network depth, width, and resolution using a compound coefficient $\phi$: $d = \alpha^\phi$, $w = \beta^\phi$, $r = \gamma^\phi$ with $\alpha \cdot \beta^2 \cdot \gamma^2 \approx 2$.

nodes.label: conditional gan
nodes.definition: A GAN variant where both the generator and discriminator are conditioned on additional information $\mathbf{y}$ (class label, text, image): $G(\mathbf{z}, \mathbf{y})$ generates data conditioned on $\mathbf{y}$, and $D(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y})$ evaluates whether $\mathbf{x}$ is a real sample of class $\mathbf{y}$.

nodes.label: conditional random field
nodes.definition: A conditional random field is an undirected probabilistic model for structured prediction that defines a conditional distribution $p(y \mid x)$ over output structures given an input. It is especially common in sequence labeling and segmentation tasks.

nodes.label: connectionist temporal classification
nodes.definition: A loss function and decoding method for sequence labeling that allows training without explicit alignment between input and output sequences, by summing the probabilities of all valid alignments (including blank tokens): $P(\mathbf{l} \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sum_{\boldsymbol{\pi} \in \mathcal{B}^{-1}(\mathbf{l})} \prod_t P(\pi_t \mid \mathbf{x})$, computed efficiently via dynamic programming.

nodes.label: consistency model
nodes.definition: A generative model that learns to directly map any point on the probability flow ODE trajectory to its origin (the clean data), enabling one-step or few-step generation without iterative denoising, trained either by distilling a pre-trained diffusion model or by a standalone consistency training objective.

nodes.label: constitutional ai
nodes.definition: An alignment approach where the AI critiques and revises its own outputs based on a set of principles (constitution), using a self-play process: (1) generate potentially harmful response, (2) critique it using a principle, (3) revise, then train on the revisions (RLAIF: RL from AI feedback instead of human feedback).

nodes.label: contrastive learning
nodes.definition: A self-supervised learning paradigm that learns representations by contrasting positive pairs (similar/augmented views of the same data) against negative pairs (different data points): maximize agreement between positives and disagreement between negatives, often using the InfoNCE loss.

nodes.label: convnext
nodes.definition: A pure CNN architecture that modernizes ResNet with design choices borrowed from Transformers (larger kernel sizes 7x7, GELU activation, fewer normalization layers using LayerNorm, inverted bottleneck blocks), demonstrating that CNNs can match Vision Transformer performance when properly modernized.

nodes.label: convolutional neural network
nodes.definition: A convolutional neural network is a neural architecture built from convolutional filters, local receptive fields, and often pooling or downsampling. It is especially effective for data with spatial or grid structure such as images, audio spectrograms, and video.

nodes.label: coordinate descent
nodes.definition: An optimization algorithm that minimizes $f(\mathbf{x})$ by iteratively optimizing over one coordinate (or block of coordinates) at a time while holding all others fixed: $x_j^{(t+1)} = \arg\min_{x_j} f(x_1^{(t+1)}, \ldots, x_{j-1}^{(t+1)}, x_j, x_{j+1}^{(t)}, \ldots)$, converging for separable or smooth convex objectives.

nodes.label: cornernet
nodes.definition: An anchor-free object detection model that detects objects as pairs of keypoints (top-left and bottom-right corners) using two heatmaps, with corner pooling (max along horizontal/vertical boundaries) for better corner localization and associative embeddings to group matching corners into bounding boxes.

nodes.label: correlation clustering
nodes.definition: A graph clustering problem where edges are labeled positive (similar) or negative (dissimilar), and the goal is to partition vertices to minimize the number of disagreements (positive edges between clusters + negative edges within clusters), solvable via SDP relaxation or combinatorial algorithms.

nodes.label: counterfactual regret minimization
nodes.definition: An iterative algorithm for approximating Nash equilibria in extensive-form games that decomposes overall regret into per-information-set counterfactual regrets, applies regret matching at each information set to update the local strategy, and averages strategies over iterations to converge to a Nash equilibrium.

nodes.label: cpc
nodes.definition: Contrastive Predictive Coding: a self-supervised representation learning method that learns to predict future latent representations $\mathbf{z}_{t+k}$ from past context $\mathbf{c}_t$ using a contrastive (InfoNCE) loss: $\mathcal{L} = -E[\log \frac{\exp(\mathbf{z}_{t+k}^\top \mathbf{W}_k \mathbf{c}_t)}{\sum_j \exp(\mathbf{z}_j^\top \mathbf{W}_k \mathbf{c}_t)}]$, maximizing mutual information between past and future.

nodes.label: cure
nodes.definition: Clustering Using REpresentatives (CURE) is a hierarchical agglomerative clustering algorithm that represents each cluster by a fixed number of well-scattered representative points (rather than a single centroid), shrunk toward the cluster centroid by a fraction $\alpha$, and merges the pair of clusters whose closest representative points are nearest.

nodes.label: dagmm
nodes.definition: Deep Autoencoding Gaussian Mixture Model: an anomaly detection method that combines a deep autoencoder (for dimensionality reduction and reconstruction error features) with a Gaussian mixture model (for density estimation in the reduced space), jointly training both components end-to-end.

nodes.label: dbscan
nodes.definition: Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise: a density-based clustering algorithm that identifies clusters as connected regions of high density (at least $\text{minPts}$ points within radius $\epsilon$), classifying points as core (dense), border (near core), or noise (neither), finding arbitrarily shaped clusters without specifying the number of clusters.

nodes.label: ddpg
nodes.definition:
Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient: an off-policy actor-critic algorithm for continuous action spaces that uses a deterministic policy $\mu_	heta(s)$, experience replay, target networks for both actor and critic, and updates the actor by the deterministic policy gradient $
abla_	heta J = E[
abla_a Q(s, a)|_{a=\mu_	heta(s)} 
abla_	heta \mu_	heta(s)]$.

nodes.label: ddpm
nodes.definition: Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Model: a generative model that defines a forward process adding Gaussian noise over $T$ steps ($q(\mathbf{x}_t \mid \mathbf{x}_{t-1}) = N(\sqrt{1-\beta_t}\mathbf{x}_{t-1}, \beta_t \mathbf{I})$) and learns a reverse denoising process ($p_\theta(\mathbf{x}_{t-1} \mid \mathbf{x}_t) = N(\boldsymbol{\mu}_\theta(\mathbf{x}_t, t), \sigma_t^2 \mathbf{I})$) to generate data by iteratively den…

nodes.label: deep equilibrium model
nodes.definition: A deep learning architecture that defines the output as the fixed point of a single repeated layer $\mathbf{z}^* = f_\theta(\mathbf{z}^*, \mathbf{x})$, computed by root-finding algorithms rather than stacking explicit layers, with gradients computed via implicit differentiation without storing intermediate activations.

nodes.label: deeplab
nodes.definition: A family of semantic segmentation models that use atrous (dilated) convolutions to enlarge the receptive field without reducing resolution, Atrous Spatial Pyramid Pooling (ASPP, parallel atrous convolutions at multiple rates), and a CRF post-processing step (DeepLab v1/v2) or encoder-decoder structure (v3+).

nodes.label: densenet
nodes.definition: A CNN architecture where each layer receives feature maps from all preceding layers (via concatenation) and passes its feature maps to all subsequent layers: $\mathbf{x}_l = H_l([\mathbf{x}_0, \mathbf{x}_1, \ldots, \mathbf{x}_{l-1}])$, encouraging feature reuse and requiring fewer parameters per layer.

nodes.label: detr
nodes.definition: DEtection TRansformer: an end-to-end object detection model that uses a Transformer encoder-decoder with a set of learned object queries, predicting a fixed-size set of detections in parallel via bipartite matching loss, eliminating the need for anchor boxes, NMS, and other hand-designed components.

nodes.label: diffdock
nodes.definition: A diffusion-based molecular docking method that models the ligand pose (translation, rotation, and torsion angles) as a diffusion process over the product space SE(3) x torsion angles, learning to reverse the diffusion to generate binding poses, replacing traditional docking search with learned generative sampling.

nodes.label: difference-in-differences
nodes.definition: A causal inference method that estimates treatment effects by comparing the change in outcomes over time between a treated group and a control group: $\hat{\tau}_{\text{DiD}} = (\bar{Y}_{\text{treat, post}} - \bar{Y}_{\text{treat, pre}}) - (\bar{Y}_{\text{ctrl, post}} - \bar{Y}_{\text{ctrl, pre}})$, assuming parallel trends (both groups would have had the same outcome trends absent treatment).

nodes.label: differentially private sgd
nodes.definition: A training algorithm that provides formal privacy guarantees by clipping per-example gradients to a maximum norm $C$ and adding calibrated Gaussian noise: $\tilde{\mathbf{g}}_t = \frac{1}{B}(\sum_i \text{clip}(\mathbf{g}_i, C) + N(0, \sigma^2 C^2 \mathbf{I}))$, ensuring that the model's output is $(\epsilon, \delta)$-differentially private with respect to any individual training example.

nodes.label: diffpool
nodes.definition: A differentiable graph pooling method that learns a soft assignment matrix $\mathbf{S}^{(l)} \in \mathbb{R}^{n_l \times n_{l+1}}$ mapping $n_l$ nodes to $n_{l+1}$ cluster nodes at each layer, enabling hierarchical graph coarsening: $\mathbf{X}^{(l+1)} = \mathbf{S}^{(l)\top} \mathbf{Z}^{(l)}$ and $\mathbf{A}^{(l+1)} = \mathbf{S}^{(l)\top} \mathbf{A}^{(l)} \mathbf{S}^{(l)}$.

nodes.label: diffusion maps
nodes.definition: A nonlinear dimensionality reduction method that embeds data using the eigenvectors of a normalized random walk transition matrix on a similarity graph: the diffusion distance between points captures multi-scale geometric structure, and the embedding $\mathbf{y}_i = [\lambda_1^t \psi_1(\mathbf{x}_i), \ldots, \lambda_k^t \psi_k(\mathbf{x}_i)]$ preserves diffusion distances at time scale $t$.

nodes.label: dimenet
nodes.definition: Directional Message Passing Neural Network: a 3D molecular GNN that incorporates both interatomic distances and bond angles into message passing via spherical Bessel functions and spherical harmonics, enabling the network to capture directional information beyond pairwise distances for more accurate molecular property prediction.

nodes.label: dino
nodes.definition: A self-supervised learning method for Vision Transformers using self-distillation: a student network learns to match the output of a teacher network (exponential moving average of student weights) across different augmented views of the same image, using a cross-entropy loss on the [CLS] token representations.

nodes.label: dot product
nodes.category: Linear and multilinear algebra; matrix theory
nodes.definition: The inner product of two vectors: $\mathbf{a} \cdot \mathbf{b} = \sum_{i=1}^n a_i b_i = \|\mathbf{a}\| \|\mathbf{b}\| \cos\theta$, measuring the similarity (alignment) between vectors. Foundation for projections, cosine similarity, and attention mechanisms.

nodes.label: double machine learning
nodes.definition: A framework for estimating causal parameters in the presence of high-dimensional confounders that uses cross-fitting: first estimate nuisance functions (propensity score and outcome model) with any ML method on one fold, then estimate the causal parameter on the other fold using the Neyman-orthogonal moment condition, providing $\sqrt{n}$-consistent and asymptotically normal estimates.

nodes.label: dp-means
nodes.definition: A k-means variant inspired by Dirichlet process mixture models that automatically creates new clusters when a point is farther than a threshold $\lambda$ from all existing centroids: if $\min_k \|\mathbf{x}_i - \boldsymbol{\mu}_k\| > \lambda$, create a new cluster centered at $\mathbf{x}_i$, otherwise assign to the nearest centroid.

nodes.label: dreamer
nodes.definition: A model-based RL agent that learns a world model in a compact latent space (using a Recurrent State-Space Model with discrete and continuous components), imagines trajectories by rolling out the world model, and optimizes the policy on imagined trajectories using actor-critic learning, achieving strong performance without real-environment interaction during policy optimization.

nodes.label: dssm
nodes.definition: Deep Structured Semantic Model: a dual-encoder architecture that separately encodes queries and documents into a shared low-dimensional semantic space using deep neural networks, computing relevance as the cosine similarity between the query and document embeddings, enabling efficient retrieval via approximate nearest neighbor search.

nodes.label: ease
nodes.definition: Embarrassingly Shallow Autoencoders for Sparse Data: a linear autoencoder for collaborative filtering that learns an item-item weight matrix $\mathbf{B}$ by solving $\min_\mathbf{B} \|\mathbf{X} - \mathbf{X}\mathbf{B}\|_F^2 + \lambda \|\mathbf{B}\|_F^2$ with the constraint $\text{diag}(\mathbf{B}) = 0$, yielding a closed-form solution $\hat{\mathbf{B}} = \mathbf{I} - \hat{\mathbf{P}} \cdot \text{diagMat}(1./\text{dia…

nodes.label: echo state network
nodes.definition: A recurrent neural network where the recurrent weights (reservoir) are randomly initialized and fixed, and only the output weights are trained: $\mathbf{h}_t = f(\mathbf{W}_{\text{in}} \mathbf{x}_t + \mathbf{W}_{\text{res}} \mathbf{h}_{t-1})$, $\hat{\mathbf{y}}_t = \mathbf{W}_{\text{out}} \mathbf{h}_t$, where $\mathbf{W}_{\text{out}}$ is trained via linear regression, providing fast training of RNNs.

nodes.label: eclat
nodes.definition: Equivalence CLAss Transformation: a frequent itemset mining algorithm that uses a vertical database format (each item mapped to its set of transaction IDs/tidset), finding frequent itemsets by intersecting tidsets: $\text{tidset}(X \cup Y) = \text{tidset}(X) \cap \text{tidset}(Y)$, with support computed as the intersection size.

nodes.label: efficientnet
nodes.definition: A family of CNN models discovered by neural architecture search that uses a compound scaling method to uniformly scale network depth ($d$), width ($w$), and resolution ($r$) using a compound coefficient $\phi$: $d = \alpha^\phi$, $w = \beta^\phi$, $r = \gamma^\phi$ subject to $\alpha \cdot \beta^2 \cdot \gamma^2 \approx 2$.

nodes.label: elliptic envelope
nodes.definition: An anomaly detection method that fits a robust covariance (Minimum Covariance Determinant) to the data assuming a Gaussian distribution, then classifies points as outliers based on their Mahalanobis distance from the estimated center exceeding a threshold.

nodes.label: elmo
nodes.definition: Embeddings from Language Models: a contextualized word embedding method that produces context-dependent representations by concatenating the outputs of forward and backward language model LSTMs at each layer, combining them as a task-specific weighted sum: $\mathbf{ELMo}_k = \gamma \sum_l s_l \mathbf{h}_{k,l}$ where $s_l$ are softmax-normalized layer weights.

nodes.label: equivariant gnn
nodes.definition: A graph neural network that preserves geometric symmetries: if the input is transformed by a group element $g$ (rotation, translation, reflection), the output transforms predictably according to the same group action, ensuring that the network's predictions respect the physical symmetries of the problem (e.g., E(3) equivariance for 3D molecular systems).

nodes.label: es-rnn
nodes.definition: A hybrid model combining per-series exponential smoothing (Holt-Winters) for level and seasonality with a shared recurrent neural network (LSTM/dilated LSTM) that models the residual nonlinear dynamics across all series, winning the M4 forecasting competition.

nodes.label: estimation of distribution algorithm
nodes.definition: A class of evolutionary algorithms that replace traditional crossover and mutation operators with probabilistic model building and sampling: at each generation, a probability distribution (e.g., Gaussian, Bayesian network) is fitted to the selected (elite) individuals, and new candidates are sampled from this distribution.

nodes.label: exp3
nodes.definition: Exponential-weight algorithm for Exploration and Exploitation: an adversarial multi-armed bandit algorithm that maintains weights $w_{t,a}$ for each action, selects actions with probability $p_{t,a} = (1-\gamma) \frac{w_{t,a}}{\sum_b w_{t,b}} + \frac{\gamma}{K}$, and updates weights using importance-weighted rewards: $w_{t+1,a} = w_{t,a} \exp(\frac{\gamma \hat{r}_{t,a}}{K})$ where $\hat{r}_{t,a} = r_t \mathbf{1}[a_t=…

nodes.label: expectation-maximization
nodes.definition: Expectation-maximization is an iterative algorithm for maximum-likelihood or MAP estimation in latent-variable models. It alternates an E-step computing expectations under the current posterior over latent variables and an M-step maximizing the expected complete-data objective.

nodes.label: factor analysis
nodes.definition: A latent variable model that assumes observed variables are linear combinations of a smaller number of latent factors plus noise: $\mathbf{x} = \boldsymbol{\Lambda} \mathbf{f} + \boldsymbol{\mu} + \boldsymbol{\epsilon}$, where $\mathbf{f} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I})$ and $\boldsymbol{\epsilon} \sim N(\mathbf{0}, \boldsymbol{\Psi})$ with diagonal $\boldsymbol{\Psi}$ (factor-specific noise variances).

nodes.label: factorization machine
nodes.definition: A general predictor that models all pairwise feature interactions via factored parameters: $\hat{y}(\mathbf{x}) = w_0 + \sum_i w_i x_i + \sum_{i<j} \langle \mathbf{v}_i, \mathbf{v}_j \rangle x_i x_j$, where each feature $i$ has a latent vector $\mathbf{v}_i \in \mathbb{R}^k$, enabling efficient $O(nk)$ computation and handling of sparse high-dimensional data.

nodes.label: faster r-cnn
nodes.definition: A two-stage object detection framework consisting of a Region Proposal Network (RPN) that shares convolutional features with a Fast R-CNN detection network, where the RPN generates object proposals by sliding anchor boxes over the feature map and predicting objectness scores, and the second stage classifies and refines the proposed regions.

nodes.label: fcos
nodes.definition: Fully Convolutional One-Stage Object Detection: an anchor-free detector that predicts, for each spatial location on multi-scale feature maps, the distances $(l, t, r, b)$ to the four sides of the bounding box and a centerness score, directly regressing boxes without predefined anchors.

nodes.label: feature pyramid network
nodes.definition: A multi-scale feature extractor that builds top-down pathway with lateral connections from a bottom-up CNN backbone. Already defined.

nodes.label: federated averaging
nodes.definition: The standard algorithm for federated learning where each client trains a local model on its private data for several SGD steps, then sends the model update (or updated weights) to a central server, which averages the updates across all participating clients: $\mathbf{w}_{t+1} = \sum_{k=1}^{K} \frac{n_k}{n} \mathbf{w}_{t+1}^k$, repeating for multiple communication rounds.

nodes.label: fisher information matrix
nodes.definition:
The expected outer product of the score function: $\mathbf{F}( oldsymbol{	heta}) = E\left[
abla_	heta \log p(\mathbf{x};  oldsymbol{	heta}) 
abla_	heta \log p(\mathbf{x};  oldsymbol{	heta})^	opight] = -E\left[
abla_	heta^2 \log p(\mathbf{x};  oldsymbol{	heta})ight]$. Measures information about $ oldsymbol{	heta}$ contained in the data.

nodes.label: fp-growth
nodes.definition: Frequent Pattern Growth: a frequent itemset mining algorithm that compresses the database into a compact FP-tree (prefix tree with support counts), then mines frequent patterns by recursively constructing conditional FP-trees (projected databases) for each item, without candidate generation.

nodes.label: fully convolutional network
nodes.definition: A CNN for dense prediction (semantic segmentation) that replaces fully connected layers with convolutional layers to produce output of the same spatial dimensions as the input, using upsampling (transposed convolutions) and skip connections from earlier layers for fine-grained predictions.

nodes.label: g-means
nodes.definition: A k-means variant that automatically determines $k$ by testing whether each cluster's data follows a Gaussian distribution (Anderson-Darling test): if not, the cluster is split using 2-means along its principal component, continuing until all clusters pass the Gaussianity test.

nodes.label: gail
nodes.definition: Generative Adversarial Imitation Learning: matches the agent's state-action distribution to the expert's using a discriminator, bypassing explicit reward learning.

nodes.label: gan
nodes.definition: Generative Adversarial Network: a generative model consisting of a generator $G$ that maps random noise $\mathbf{z} \sim p_z$ to synthetic data, and a discriminator $D$ that distinguishes real from generated data, trained via the minimax game $\min_G \max_D E[\log D(\mathbf{x})] + E[\log(1-D(G(\mathbf{z})))]$.

nodes.label: garch
nodes.definition: Generalized Autoregressive Conditional Heteroskedasticity: a time series model for the variance (volatility) of returns where the conditional variance is a function of past squared returns and past variances: $\sigma_t^2 = \alpha_0 + \sum_{i=1}^{p} \alpha_i r_{t-i}^2 + \sum_{j=1}^{q} \beta_j \sigma_{t-j}^2$, capturing volatility clustering in financial data.

nodes.label: gaussian mixture model
nodes.definition: A Gaussian mixture model is a finite mixture density of the form $p(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K \pi_k \, \mathcal{N}(x \mid \mu_k,\Sigma_k)$ with mixing weights $\pi_k \ge 0$ summing to one. It models data as arising from one of several latent Gaussian components.

nodes.label: gaussian process classification
nodes.definition: A Bayesian nonparametric classifier that places a GP prior on a latent function $f \sim \mathcal{GP}(0, k)$, then passes it through a sigmoid (or probit) link to obtain class probabilities $P(y=1 \mid \mathbf{x}) = \sigma(f(\mathbf{x}))$, with the posterior $p(f \mid \mathbf{X}, \mathbf{y})$ being non-Gaussian and requiring approximate inference (Laplace approximation or EP).

nodes.label: gaussian process regression
nodes.definition: A nonparametric Bayesian regression method that places a Gaussian process prior $f \sim \mathcal{GP}(m(\mathbf{x}), k(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{x}'))$ over functions, yielding a posterior predictive distribution $f^* \mid \mathbf{X}, \mathbf{y}, \mathbf{x}^*$ that is Gaussian with mean $\mathbf{k}_*^\top (\mathbf{K} + \sigma^2 \mathbf{I})^{-1} \mathbf{y}$ and variance $k_{**} - \mathbf{k}_*^\top (\mathbf{K} + \sigma^2 \mat…

nodes.label: gemini
nodes.definition: A family of natively multimodal large language models from Google that process interleaved sequences of text, images, audio, and video through a single decoder-only Transformer, trained on multimodal data from the outset (rather than connecting separate vision and language models).

nodes.label: generalized additive model
nodes.definition: A flexible regression model of the form $g(E[Y \mid \mathbf{x}]) = \beta_0 + \sum_{j=1}^{p} f_j(x_j)$, where $g$ is a link function and $f_j$ are smooth nonparametric functions estimated from the data (typically via penalized regression splines), generalizing GLMs by allowing nonlinear covariate effects.

nodes.label: generalized linear model
nodes.definition: A generalized linear model is a regression model in which the response distribution belongs to an exponential family and a link function $g$ satisfies $g(\mathbb{E}[Y \mid X])=X^\top\beta$. It generalizes ordinary linear regression to non-Gaussian outcomes such as counts and binary labels.

nodes.label: generative adversarial network
nodes.definition: A generative adversarial network is a generative model trained through a game between a generator that produces synthetic samples and a discriminator that tries to distinguish real from generated samples. The classical objective is $\min_G \max_D \mathbb{E}[\log D(x)] + \mathbb{E}[\log(1-D(G(z)))]$.

nodes.label: gin
nodes.definition: Graph Isomorphism Network: a GNN that is provably as powerful as the Weisfeiler-Lehman (WL) graph isomorphism test in distinguishing graph structures, using the update $\mathbf{h}_v^{(l)} = \text{MLP}^{(l)}((1+\epsilon^{(l)}) \mathbf{h}_v^{(l-1)} + \sum_{u \in \mathcal{N}(v)} \mathbf{h}_u^{(l-1)})$ with injective aggregation.

nodes.label: glove
nodes.definition: Global Vectors for word representation: a word embedding method that learns vectors by factoring the log-co-occurrence count matrix, minimizing $\sum_{i,j} f(X_{ij})(\mathbf{w}_i^\top \tilde{\mathbf{w}}_j + b_i + \tilde{b}_j - \log X_{ij})^2$ where $X_{ij}$ is the co-occurrence count and $f$ is a weighting function that caps frequent pairs.

nodes.label: googlenet
nodes.definition: A deep CNN that introduced the Inception module (parallel application of 1x1, 3x3, and 5x5 convolutions plus max-pooling, concatenated along the channel dimension) with 1x1 convolution bottlenecks for dimensionality reduction, achieving 22 layers with only 6.8M parameters.

nodes.label: gradient descent
nodes.definition: Gradient descent is the iterative optimization method $x_{t+1}=x_t-\eta_t \nabla f(x_t)$ for minimizing a differentiable objective $f$. It moves opposite the gradient, the direction of steepest local increase, and is the canonical first-order optimization algorithm.

nodes.label: graph convolutional network
nodes.definition: A neural network for graph-structured data that learns node representations by aggregating features from each node's neighbors via a spectral convolution approximation: $\mathbf{H}^{(l+1)} = \sigma(\hat{\mathbf{D}}^{-1/2} \hat{\mathbf{A}} \hat{\mathbf{D}}^{-1/2} \mathbf{H}^{(l)} \mathbf{W}^{(l)})$, where $\hat{\mathbf{A}} = \mathbf{A} + \mathbf{I}$ adds self-loops.

nodes.label: graph diffusion network
nodes.definition: A graph neural network that incorporates graph diffusion (e.g., personalized PageRank or heat kernel diffusion) as the propagation mechanism instead of standard message passing, computing node representations by diffusing features through a generalized diffusion matrix $\mathbf{S} = \sum_{k=0}^{\infty} \theta_k \mathbf{T}^k$ where $\mathbf{T}$ is the transition matrix.

nodes.label: graphsage
nodes.definition: A scalable inductive GNN that learns node embeddings by sampling a fixed number of neighbors per node at each layer and aggregating their features using a learned aggregator (mean, LSTM, or max-pooling): $\mathbf{h}_v^{(l)} = \sigma(\mathbf{W}^{(l)} \cdot \text{CONCAT}(\mathbf{h}_v^{(l-1)}, \text{AGG}(\{\mathbf{h}_u^{(l-1)} : u \in \mathcal{N}_S(v)\})))$.

nodes.label: graphsaint
nodes.definition: Graph SAmpling based INductive learning: a scalable GCN training method that constructs mini-batches by sampling subgraphs (via node, edge, or random walk sampling) from the full graph, with normalization coefficients that correct for sampling bias, enabling unbiased gradient estimates.

nodes.label: grounding dino
nodes.definition: An open-set object detection model that combines the DINO detector with grounded pre-training, accepting text prompts to detect arbitrary objects by fusing language and vision features through cross-modality attention, enabling detection of objects described by any text phrase without predefined categories.

nodes.label: gshard
nodes.definition: A framework for scaling Transformer models to 600B+ parameters using sparsely-gated Mixture-of-Experts layers with top-2 expert routing per token, distributed across thousands of TPU devices with automatic sharding and expert/data parallelism.

nodes.label: hamiltonian monte carlo
nodes.definition: An MCMC algorithm that introduces auxiliary momentum variables $\mathbf{p}$ and simulates Hamiltonian dynamics $H(\boldsymbol{\theta}, \mathbf{p}) = -\log \pi(\boldsymbol{\theta}) + \frac{1}{2}\mathbf{p}^\top \mathbf{M}^{-1} \mathbf{p}$ using the leapfrog integrator, proposing distant states in parameter space while maintaining high acceptance rates, dramatically reducing random walk behavior.

nodes.label: hamiltonian neural network
